text:
To be an American is a privilege, whether you were born here or not.
My family came from Ireland and Scotland in the early 1800s. Immigrants. 
My great-great-grandfather served in the Army. My great-grandfather served in the Army. Both of my grandfathers served in the Air Force. My father served in the Air Force. I served in the Navy. 
Does that make me more American than someone who just arrived to enjoy the privileges and freedoms this country offers? Yes and no.
If you come here legally, go through the long process of citizenship, learn the language, assimilate into American culture, and become a productive member of society....then yes. 
Your children will grow up among kids who share the same values as long-generational American families and the legacy begins.
If you come here intending to replace our social norms with yours, skip the legal process, refuse the language, and remain a burden on the society that took you in.... then..... NO.
America is a melting pot. Those flavors produced something the world has wanted for 250 years. Keep throwing new spices into a stew that has been simmering that long and you don’t improve it.
You ruin it!
Americans are a breed of their own. That identity takes time to bake into a person’s consciousness. People with familial history here, neighbors, friends, and a willingness to serve and die for this country are different. 
That's not hatred. 
It's inheritance.
If you are new to America, it's on you to appreciate the gift: the people, this imperfect but unmatched Constitutional Republic, and 250 years of hard-won liberty. 
We should all thank God for the privilege of being called an American.

text:
A Fresno State assistant coach once drove to Palo Alto High School to scout a player.

It was not Davante Adams.

Tonight, at 33, Adams caught 8 passes for 195 yards and two touchdowns on Monday Night Football. His 119th career touchdown catch moved him to seventh in NFL history.

Here is how he almost got missed.

Adams grew up in East Palo Alto. Basketball was his sport. He played varsity guard at Palo Alto High and did not get serious about football until he was an upperclassman.

His grades were a problem too.

"He had bad grades. He hadn't applied himself his first two years," said Keith Williams, then the receivers coach at Fresno State.

Williams had come to Palo Alto to see someone else. Head coach Earl Hansen pulled him aside.

"The kid you're coming to see is good, but we have another kid, Davante Adams, he's a late bloomer in football experience, but he's a heck of an athlete."

As a senior, Adams played receiver and cornerback and helped Palo Alto go undefeated and win a state title.

He still only got two offers. San Diego State and Fresno State.

He picked Fresno State and sat out his first year to get eligible in the classroom.

Williams saw something the transcripts did not.

"He was able to realize, 'This dude is actually legit smart, he's just not applying himself in the classroom,'" Adams said later.

In 2013, catching passes from Derek Carr, Adams led the entire country in catches, yards and touchdowns. 131 catches. 1,719 yards. 24 touchdowns.

The Packers took him 53rd overall.

Six Pro Bowls. Three All-Pro teams. He has led the NFL in touchdown catches three times, the most recent one just last season with the Rams.

Tonight, he caught a 31 yarder in the first quarter and an 11 yarder in the third. He finished 11 yards shy of the best receiving game of his career.

That is 119 touchdown catches for his career.

Only Jerry Rice, Randy Moss, Terrell Owens, Cris Carter, Marvin Harrison and Larry Fitzgerald have more. Fitzgerald is two away.

Rams 28, Giants 6.

Not bad for the other kid.

text:
A close-up photograph of the Moon in a gibbous phase reveals its stunning details against a dark night sky. The Moon, Earth's only natural satellite, offers a captivating view that entices both amateur and experienced astronomers alike. Tonight, a rare Blue Moon is set to rise, offering a spectacular celestial event that will attract many stargazers. As it reaches peak visibility, the atmosphere will be charged with excitement and curiosity about this unusual lunar occurrence.

Sky and Telescope highlights the significance of the waning gibbous moon on November 6, providing context for those keen on observing these phenomena. The gibbous phase occurs when more than half of the visible side of the Moon is illuminated by sunlight. This particular illumination allows enthusiasts to appreciate the intricate surface features of our lunar companion. In close-up views, one can easily distinguish the bright highland areas and darker flat regions known as maria. These maria are ancient volcanic plains formed by past eruptions, giving the Moon its unique landscape.

Each detail adds to the allure of the Moon. In this close-up shot, the contrast between the illuminated regions and the darker areas emphasizes the rugged terrain of the lunar surface. The gibbous phase provides an ideal opportunity for observing these features, as the shadows cast by sunlight reveal the relief and depth of the craters and mountains. Whether viewed through a telescope or simply with the naked eye, the sight of the Moon in this phase is undeniably striking.

An incredible shot of the Corn Moon rising over Arkansas exemplifies the beauty and variety of lunar phases. Each lunar event, including the rise of the Corn Moon, generates a sense of wonder as its light shines down on the landscape below. For many, these moments create a connection to the cosmos and a sense of peace in watching the celestial body cycle through its phases. The interplay of light and shadow on its surface during a gibbous phase showcases not just the Moon itself but also the intricate dance of the Earth, Moon, and Sun.

Such photographs capture the imagination and remind us of the grandeur of our universe, as we seek to understand our place within it. These lunar observations open the door for discussions about astronomy, photography, and the beauty found in nature, ensuring that the legacy of exploring the night sky continues to inspire generations.

Old Flame (Gambler's Folly Book 4) by Mellie Miller is a heartfelt second-chance paranormal shifter romance that blends emotional healing, mature love, and the magic of fate. Billionaire and bear shifter Kort Behrens has been lucky in business but unlucky in love—after two failed marriages and a string of gold diggers, he’s given up hope of finding a real connection. Elizabeth Murphy, a widow for four years, has rebuilt her life through her Reiki practice and the quiet companionship of her cat, Puzzle, still carrying the quiet ache of a long marriage that never fully satisfied her deeper desires. When these old college friends (who never dated) unexpectedly reunite on the way to the enchanted world of Gambler’s Folly, sparks fly and a full-blown romance blooms. Will they seize this second chance at a happily-ever-after, or will doubts and fears snatch it away? On Gambler’s Folly, every love story is a gamble—and Fate always deals the final hand. A slow-burn friends-to-lovers tale full of heart, sensuality, and the series’ signature fantasy charm.

Buy links
Amazon (Kindle ebook): https://t.co/vaKDyp19Rj

- Also available on Kindle Unlimited and through other major retailers (including Smashwords and Barnes & Noble).

About the author
Mellie Miller first fell in love with writing in a high school creative writing class. Married to her one and only, Steve, they began their journey through life in 1976 and, after two children and many moves, she finally has the time to devote to this love. She mainly writes fantasy romance, often with a paranormal twist, though she also has a short book sharing her struggle with breast cancer. Mellie feels her background in music, martial arts (2nd-degree black belt), and Reiki gives her a broad palette to draw on for her character development. Many of her stories incorporate one or more of these talents. As a lover of fantasy, Mellie hopes the worlds and stories she creates will give others a bit of escape from the hectic world around us and offer hope for a happy outcome. She and her husband live in rural Georgia and share their lives with cats, dogs, and a flock of chickens. She also writes under the pen name Sultonna Nadine.

text:
For foreign universities, I can see where good counselling can add value, particularly in helping a student understand the range of options beyond simply chasing rankings.

For example, in the US, an undergraduate student could choose among large public universities such as UC Berkeley, large private universities such as Stanford, and small liberal arts colleges such as Pomona. They offer very different academic environments, student communities, campus experiences and approaches to undergraduate education.

For an international student, the cost of attendance can also be broadly comparable across these categories, so the question is not simply “which university is ranked higher?” but “which environment is the right fit for this student?”

That said, I would be cautious about paying a consultancy primarily for admissions strategy. For a 10th grader, I think the more valuable role is helping the student discover their interests, pursue extracurricular activities, understand the landscape and make informed choices.

text:
Meta's Muse AI agent app ranks as the leading free app on the US iOS chart, surpassing ChatGPT on Friday. Sensor Tower reports over 2.5 million downloads since its September 8 launch. This includes approximately 1.5 million on iOS and 1.1 million on Android.

In its initial 13 days, Muse recorded over 2.5 million downloads. Claude saw 400,000 downloads and Grok 200,000 in the same post-launch window. ChatGPT logged 3.1 million downloads during that period.

Powered by Meta's Muse Spark AI models, the app signals CEO Mark Zuckerberg's strategic focus on the AI agent market for broader consumer adoption. Bernstein analyst Stacy Rasgon notes this shift toward mainstream use. News of the app's performance contributed to Meta stock increasing over 11% on Monday, with Wells Fargo raising its price target to $796.

Muse offers free access and monthly subscriptions priced at $20 or $100.

Amazon has blocked Muse from accessing its shopping site, citing privacy and security risks. Amazon stated Muse bypassed personalization features, captured customer credentials, and scraped account data without prior notice. In contrast, Shopify CEO Tobias Lütke announced a partnership with Muse to enable agentic checkout in online stores.

Broader concerns regarding AI safety and cybersecurity risks persist within the tech industry.

text:
Should a small company be a CAT or a DOG?

An insight from evolutionary biology, a confession, and a ProConCloud analysis.

A house cat and a lion share one blueprint. 
A pug and a greyhound do not.

Why?

Biologist Dr Anjali Goswami traced it to one early mutation. 

Cats lost their grinding molars. From then on they could only eat meat. 

That locked them into one niche: the perfect hunter. Dominant, and the slowest to change shape. 
Dogs kept their molars. A golden retriever can still eat a carrot.

The SPECIALIST wins the niche. 

The GENERALIST keeps its options.

But her most important finding is about SPEED. Across 200 million years, what decided a species' fate was not how much the climate changed, but how FAST.

Under rapid change, specialists slow down. Flexible, social groups speed up.

Today the climate is changing 10 times faster than any event on record.

Sound familiar?

Companies do not fail because they cannot adapt.

They fail because they adapt slower than the market changes. And with AI, we've never seen markets change as fast.

Now my confession. Goldratt Research Labs is a dog 📷

We have worked across publishing, mining, aerospace, high tech, metal production, automotive, healthcare, pharma, government and more.

That variety is where our innovations come from. It is also hard to scale and be profitable.

Every project is new. Nothing compounds.

Specialists grow faster because they repeat.

So should we become a cat?

Episode 26 of my Deep Dive podcast works through our ProConCloud analysis.

In short:

1. ONE PROBLEM: 
Generalization causes spreading of attention.

2. ONE CONFLICT:  
To scale, we must SPECIALIZE. And say NO to every other opportunity. 
Pros: repeatable offer, compounding referrals, higher margins. 
Cons: the cat's trap. If our one industry shifts, we become a "dead clade walking". Alive, but our ecosystem is gone.

To keep innovating, we must GENERALIZE. And keep saying YES. 
Pros: variety, cross-industry insight, resilience if one market shifts. 
Cons: slow growth, custom work every time, low profitability.

Dr. Eli Goldratt taught us that every conflict survives on a hidden assumption. Ours: a specialist must specialize by INDUSTRY.

3. ONE INNOVATION: What if we specialize by PROBLEM instead?

Not "we serve book publishers" but "we eliminate shortages and surpluses".

For publishers, retailers, manufacturers, hospitals ...
Same method. Same Digital Twin.
The problem is the specialty.
The industry is the variable.
ONE problem across 10 industries is more focused than 10 problems in one industry.
A cat that kept its molars.
Is your business a CAT (one niche, fast growth) or a DOG (broad, resilient, slow)?
Comment CAT or DOG. And tell us which ONE problem you could be the best in the world at solving.
Comment PLAYBOOK for the full ProConCloud analysis.

Looking forward to your questions and comments.

text:
Trump called AI concerns “a HOAX.”

He said opponents of data centers “want to end up being backwards and poor.”
No, Mr. President, Americans want Congress and you to do your job protecting humanity, protecting our utility bills, and protecting us from out-of-control, corrupt greed.

A principal role for government is to protect the American people. Safety must always be our first mandate. It is also the government’s job to protect the American people from unmitigated greed. The billionaires that you are listening to now would prefer the government stay on the sidelines. But the U.S. government knows how to regulate corporate greed and how to address new technologies that could destroy our world.

The robber barons of the Gilded Age amassed enormous fortunes while working families struggled. Soon thereafter, unchecked Wall Street speculation and a devastating stock market crash helped plunge America into the Great Depression.

President Franklin D. Roosevelt and Democrats responded with landmark reforms to rein in Wall Street, protect working families, and prevent another financial catastrophe. They established the Securities and Exchange Commission to police the stock market, created Social Security to provide economic security for Americans, and enacted the first federal minimum wage to protect workers from exploitation.

When we invented and exploded the atomic bomb in New Mexico in 1944, the scientist who oversaw it, J. Robert Oppenheimer, said, “now I am become Death, the destroyer of worlds.” He realized that this new technology could mean the end of humankind. After Hiroshima and Nagasaki, the United States, Congress, and our top scientists worked to limit the spread of nuclear weapons, even while many of the scientific inventions coming out of that discovery made their way into our business community and way of life.

What we do now will matter. We cannot just let AI and data centers regulate themselves or depend on their goodwill to lower utility costs and limit the most destructive possibilities inherent in this rapidly evolving technology. We must let local communities have a say in what is built in their neighborhoods so they can protect their water, environment, and cost burdens. 

But Congress must act. There must be a strong, enforceable national regulatory framework. We must have civil and criminal liability. We must protect the local and national financial interests of working families.

It is not a hoax, Mr. President. And we have a job to do.

text:
How Some Companies Thrived After the 1929 Crash

The crash and the Depression that followed wiped out thousands of firms. They also minted some of the most durable companies of the twentieth century.

Here is how that happened.

When the floor disappeared

On Black Thursday, October 24, 1929, crowds packed Wall Street as the ticker fell behind the selling. By Tuesday the 29th the Dow had suffered its worst single-day percentage drop of the era. Over the next three years industrial production collapsed, a quarter of the workforce lost jobs, and roughly half of all U.S. banks failed. Auto sales fell about 75 percent. Entire industries that had looked invincible in 1928 simply vanished.

That is the familiar photograph. The less familiar one is this: a handful of companies used the same years to take market share, invent new categories, and lock in brands that still sit on shelves today.

They did not “thrive” because they were lucky. They thrived because they did the opposite of what panic demanded.

They advertised when everyone else went quiet

The cereal aisle is the cleanest case study.

In the late 1920s Kellogg and Post split the packaged-cereal market. When demand cracked, Post did the obvious thing: it cut advertising. Kellogg doubled the budget, poured money into radio, and pushed a new product called Rice Krispies. “Snap! Crackle! Pop!” arrived in the early 1930s. By 1933, with the economy still in free fall, Kellogg’s profits were up nearly 30 percent and the company had become the category leader—a position it never really lost.

W.K. Kellogg also shortened the factory day. In December 1930 the Battle Creek plant switched from three eight-hour shifts to four six-hour shifts. The company hired more people, raised hourly pay, and found that output per machine actually rose. The six-hour day was treated as both a civic act and an operating experiment. It worked on both counts.

Procter & Gamble ran a parallel play. Soap still sold—people still washed—but grocery orders shrank and warehouses filled. Instead of shrinking the ad budget, P&G invented a new medium. In 1933 it launched Oxydol’s Own Ma Perkins, a daily radio serial aimed at housewives. The form was so effective that by the late 1930s the company was producing more than twenty such programs. The phrase “soap opera” is not a metaphor. It is a business model. P&G owned the stories that sold the soap.

The lesson was not “spend more.” It was: when rivals go silent, the remaining voice owns the customer’s attention at a discount.

They sold what people still had to buy—and made it cheaper

Sears stopped chasing fashion and doubled down on socks, underwear, and other staples at lower prices. By the end of the decade it had roughly doubled its store count.

General Motors did something similar with cars. New-vehicle sales cratered. GM mothballed plants, cut mid-range and luxury output, slashed prices to clear inventory, unified sales teams, and poured capacity into Chevrolet. It also offered its own financing when banks would not. GM made a profit in every year of the Depression and picked up about 15 extra points of market share. Chrysler gained even more, in part by driving Plymouth line speeds far above Ford and GM. Ford, slower to change mix and pricing, lost ground it never fully recovered.

There was also the so-called lipstick effect. Cosmetics and a few other small luxuries held up better than expected. A cheap tube of color was one of the last affordable ways to feel human. Companies that understood “affordable dignity” did better than companies that waited for the old luxury customer to return.

They treated the crash as a clearance sale on talent, assets, and attention

text:
In round seven, on September 22, 1927, former titlist Jack Dempsey pummels Heavyweight Champion Gene Tunney to the canvas.

Less than a half hour earlier Referee Dave Barry, at center ring, had instructed both fighters:

"In the event of a knockdown, the man scoring the knockdown must go to the farthest nuetral corner."

"Is that clear Jack" asked Barry. Dempsey nodded his head.

"Is that clear champ?" he asked Tunney, who also nodded in the affirmative.

"Now, in the event of a knockdown, I will not begin counting unless the boy scoring it goes to the farthest corner. I will not begin the count until he does." added Barry yet again.

"Is that clear Jack?" he asked.

"Yes." Dempsey replied.

"Is that clear champ?" he again asked Tunney who nodded affirmatively once more.

Tunney had begun to fight more aggressively, as he again dominated Dempsey in the first five rounds, much to his corner's chagrin and a frustrated jimmy Bronson warned him after the 5th "Don't take chances Gene. You're winning by a mile. Don't slug with him."

In the 7th, the fight would change in dramatic fashion as Gene Tunney found himself on the canvas for the first, and only, time in his storied career.

Dempsey, who used to stand over opponents after knockdowns and rush right back at them after they got up, looked down on Tunney.

Referee Dave Barry, trying to enforce the new rule where the knockdown count will not begin until the standing boxer is in a neutral corner, will order Dempsey into a neutral corner to no avail; Dempsey just stood there, observing his opponent.

This short delay gave Tunney five extra precious seconds to recuperate and regain his senses.

By the time Dempsey finally walked to a neutral corner, Tunney had been down for approximately five seconds.

Again, Ref Barry could not start to count on Tunney until Dempsey reached the neutral corner, but he was still able to count to nine before Tunney got up.

Many believed (and still do) that if Dempsey had responded to the referee's orders in time, he would have likely regained the World Heavyweight Championship with a seventh round knockout of Tunney. The validity of that argument has been debated even to this day.

In the fight film, a clock was later superimposed that recorded Tunney's time on the floor for a total of fourteen seconds, from the moment he fell until he got up.

Paul Beeler, the official time keeper, later said that he was at 13 when Tunney got up.

Tunney will not only get up but he will, to his credit, dominate the rest of the bout andl win a 10-round unanimous decision at Soldier Field in Chicago.

The 7th was the only round of the fight that Dempsey had won.

Because of this delay, it became known as "The Long Count Fight."

In the era when "The fix is in" had serious legitimacy many suspected either way that some shenanigans could've been afoot. It's hard to believe, however, that either Dempsey or Tunney would have taken part in any such affair.

Gangster Al Capone had told newspaper reporters prior to the bout that he had bet heavily on Dempsey.

Capone made his bet after hearing that Davy Miller was going to referee the fight and that Miller's brother had also wagered heavily on Dempsey. Thinking there might be a connection, Capone bet on Dempsey, too.

Shortly before the fight, Illinois boxing officials, believing Miller might be in league with Capone, replaced him with Dave Barry.

Rumors also flew that racketeer Arnold Rothstein and former World Featherweight Champion Abe Attell, two of the men behind the infamous World Series "Fix" of 1919, had allegedly offered Gene Tunney $1 million to throw the fight.

In early February of 1928, Tex Rickard announced that Dempsey was retiring.

In April, Dempsey said a muscle injury to his left eye influenced his decision to retire and insisted that he would not make a comeback, not even for $50 million dollars.

"Money is no object to me now. I've got plenty," Dempsey said. He also said that his health was good. "I can still walk around and tell the time of day."

text:
Trump says the U.S. is working on a “massive” deal to buy cheaper potash from Belarus.

But the real question isn’t the price at the mine. It’s the delivered price to the U.S. farmer.

Belarus is landlocked. With its traditional export route through Lithuania largely closed, potash generally needs to move:

🇧🇾 Belarus mine
→ rail through Belarus/Russia
→ Russian port
→ Atlantic vessel
→ U.S. port
→ unloading/storage
→ rail/barge into the Midwest
Compare that with Canadian potash:
🇨🇦 Saskatchewan mine
→ unit train
→ U.S. Midwest
That means Belarus potentially has to overcome additional rail, port handling, ocean freight, transloading, storage and U.S. inland transportation costs before reaching the same customer.
And there’s another issue: Lukashenko says much of Belarus’s production is already contracted, potentially limiting how much incremental volume can actually be supplied.
Belarus may be able to offer a lower headline potash price.
But mine-gate price ≠ farm-gate price.

For Canadian potash producers, the number that matters isn’t what Belarus sells it for.

It’s what it costs to land it in Iowa.

Surrendering to your Higher Self #ascension #5d #angel 

Awakening is the gradual embracing and embodiment of more of our divine consciousness - more of our higher self.  

For me, this began in earnest about a year after I started to awaken.  Until then, I was still feeling very much like the woman I had incarnated as in this lifetime. I was changing, of course, becoming more spiritual, learning how to heal, but I was still very much a work in progress within the 3d framework.  

Surrendering to my higher self took courage. I was asked to begin the process by galactic support around me. I didn't fully understand how it would work, and for some reason I felt reluctant to ask for guidance beyond the instructions I had received...  Breathe…  Lol... What did that even mean? At that time I was still learning...  

Ascension seemed like a goalpost way in the distance. So I approached this whole embracing my higher self with some trepidation and a great deal of faith that this was something I needed to do for the highest good of all. Actually, I was told that by the Arcturian Council of Light.  

I know… that sounds overly dramatic. It wasn't drama. But it was a profound shift in my reality.  I could feel my higher self approaching through my crown chakra… gently, little by little. As she arrived I felt a little light headed, euphoric even… and then it would settle and I would come back down to earth. Then it would happen again.  

When I say my higher self I need to offer an understanding of the structure, not a very good word to describe the beauty of fluid living light, but hopefully it helps. My higher self, my divine consciousness, is a rainbow of light frequency that radiates across the architecture of the 5th through to the 12th dimension. The 12th dimension is where the essence of who I am originates from. Where I was born as a Soul.  

I am an Arcturian Angel. My higher self is the mother of Arcturians.  Descending into this earthly experience from that height was a significant journey of descension. But we came because light was needed here. We came to help illuminate the way. We came her for love...  

And so, when I began consciously breathing my higher self into my temple, it was initially the 5th-dimensional aspect of my divine consciousness that I was embodying.  My field is vibrating at the 5th dimension right now, quite a few of us already are. You will know you are embodying this frequency because you will have fully aligned with love and compassion. Not much will faze you. You are not a picture of perfection, it just means you have made a conscious choice to release all ties to, and rise above, the 3rd and 4th dimensions. 

It doesn’t mean the world that surrounds you has changed and that you are now surrounded by waterfalls, crystal cities and butterflies. It just means YOU are the vibration of the 5th dimension. You are emitting this frequency into the collective. You are making a difference. Your frequency is reaching others who have yet to awaken and reminding them, it is time...  

When enough of us have begun to vibrate in this higher frequency the balance will tip over, and then we absolutely will be able to see the profound changes around the earth that Gaia has already prepared for us.    

But I did find the process needed courage, because I wasn’t sure what would happen to me, the human, when my galactic angelic higher-self arrived into the temple. I couldn’t really remember details about who I was, even though I had some understanding. It was all happening so fast and there didn’t seem to be any kind of guarantee or safety net that made the unfolding of the process easier.  

As I felt my galactic and angelic higher self aligning more closely, some very human questions began running through my mind.  What happens to human me when she arrives?  Do I have to leave?  Will I die?  Will we somehow share this body?  And perhaps the most vulnerable question of all...  Am I being replaced because human me isn't adequate enough to become what the collective needs me to be?  

For several days, I carried those questions while meditating and consciously breathing into the connection with my higher self.  And then, almost without ceremony... it was done.  I hadn't disappeared.  I hadn't died.  I hadn't been replaced.  I was still me. But there was more of me here.  

Over the following weeks and months, I began noticing changes. I was more patient. More compassionate. More loving. More peaceful.  About six months later, the strangest realisation came to me. My old self felt almost like a past life. I remember her completely. I still carry everything she experienced. I still look like her. But I am no longer the woman I once knew myself to be. I have grown beyond her. Or perhaps more accurately... I am becoming more of who I have always been.  

And yet my human life continues.  I am still a mother. My children still need me. There are meals and conversations and all the ordinary realities of family life. But internally, my life has changed profoundly.  My days still revolve around my children, of course, but my connection with the Divine and galactic family, sharing light with Gaia and the crystalline lattice surrounding this Earth, creating, healing, releasing and continuing to embody more of my higher self has become my true purpose.  

I am also healing and strengthening the bond of my Divine Union with my eternal flame – which has been an extraordinary part of this journey, but one that deserves its own expression.  

I am blessed to have a close bond with Gaia and her divine flame Thoth, and their guidance and love, along with that of my galactic and angelic family has been an intricate part of my awakening.  

If you have just awakened, I want you to know this galactic support surrounds you too. This part is such a beautiful unfolding of the awakening process. Embrace it!  

There is nothing to fear in surrendering to your higher self.  You don't have to let go of who you are, or reject your humanity.  You don't disappear.  The life you have lived becomes part of the wisdom you carry forward. Just like the many past lives we have lived do too.  You just allow more of your divine consciousness to inhabit the life you are already living.  Little by little. Breath by breath. Layer by layer.  You become so much more of who you truly are ❤️.

text:
The Day of Atonement was never a festival of man’s resolve. It was the day God appointed a substitute, a high priest, and blood. “For the life of the flesh is in the blood: and I have given it to you upon the altar to make an atonement for your souls: for it is the blood that maketh an atonement for the soul” (Lev. 17:11). The high priest entered once a year, not without blood, which he offered for himself and for the errors of the people (Lev. 16; Heb. 9:7). That day pointed forward to the one Sacrifice that actually takes away sin. When the veil of the temple was rent from the top to the bottom (Matt. 27:51), the type was finished. “By one offering he hath perfected for ever them that are sanctified” (Heb. 10:14).

What remains in the synagogues is a day without the priest and without the blood. Men afflict their souls, recite their prayers, give their alms, and ask that their names be sealed for another year. That is not the atonement of Scripture. It is man attempting to cover himself. “Without shedding of blood is no remission” (Heb. 9:22). It is humanism wearing a sacred calendar.

A supposed Christian magistrate who takes that language on his lips and offers it as a blessing is not being gracious. He is treating an empty form as if it were still the ordinance of God. He is saying, in effect, that there is a way of life apart from the Cross. There is not. “Neither is there salvation in any other: for there is none other name under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved” (Acts 4:12). The Book of Life is not sealed by ten days of effort. It is “the Lamb’s book of life” (Rev. 21:27; 13:8). The names written there were written because Another stood in their place. “He was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities… and the Lord hath laid on him the iniquity of us all” (Isa. 53:5–6).

The Israel of God is not a bloodline that rejected the Messiah. “And as many as walk according to this rule, peace be on them, and mercy, and upon the Israel of God” (Gal. 6:16). It is the people bought by His blood and gathered into His church. To wish a man “sealed” on any other terms is to leave him in his sin and to deny the only Atonement God has provided. “I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me” (John 14:6). Speak Christ, or be silent. The law and the prophets are fulfilled in Him, not in a greeting that has no priest and no sacrifice.

Matthew 5:17 is exactly why I said what I said.

Jesus did not say, “I came to keep ancient Israel permanently under the Mosaic civil code.” He said:

“Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil.” — Matthew 5:17

The Greek word translated “fulfil” is πληρόω — plēroō: to fulfill, accomplish, bring to completion, or bring something to its intended fullness.

And this is not “following Paul instead of Jesus.”

Jesus Himself established the New Covenant:

“This cup is the new covenant in My blood, which is shed for you.” — Luke 22:20

Jesus Himself taught that the Law and the Prophets pointed toward fulfillment:

“For all the prophets and the law prophesied until John.” — Matthew 11:13

And in the very Sermon on the Mount you are quoting, Jesus repeatedly says:

“You have heard that it was said … But I say unto you …”

He was not destroying God’s revelation. He was revealing its fullness and authority in Himself.

Christians therefore do not execute adulterers, offer animal sacrifices, observe Israel’s temple regulations, enforce ancient Israel’s dietary laws, or administer every judicial penalty contained in the Torah. That does not mean we have “destroyed the Law.” It means the Mosaic covenant must be understood in light of its fulfillment in Christ and the New Covenant He Himself inaugurated.

So quoting Matthew 5:17 does not establish that an ancient Israelite civil provision should be imposed upon a Christian woman—or any woman—nearly 2,000 years after Christ.

And most importantly, Matthew 5:17 certainly does not establish that a raped woman should be compelled or pressured to marry the man who violated her.

That conclusion does not follow from Jesus’ words.

Nor am I “following Paul rather than Jesus.” I am taking Jesus at His own words when He said His blood established the NEW COVENANT.

Jesus fulfilled the Law.

He did not hand violent men a permanent biblical entitlement to the women they violated.

If “I did not come to abolish but to fulfill” means every Mosaic civil law remains directly enforceable, then you have to explain why Christians are not enforcing the entire Mosaic legal system. You cannot selectively resurrect one ancient civil provision concerning women while ignoring the covenantal structure in which that provision existed.

Keep the distinction very clear: 

“fulfilled” does not mean “God’s moral standards disappeared.” 

Murder, adultery, deceit, violence, injustice, and treachery certainly do not suddenly become acceptable under grace. The question is whether Christians remain under the Mosaic covenant as Israel’s national legal covenant. 

Jesus’ own declaration of a New Covenant is directly relevant to that question.

text:
Happy Birthday Paul Muni 

From a modern point of view, Muni occasionally has a whiff of what goes between two slices of bread, but in the 1930s, the star of “Scarface” was one of the biggest names in Hollywood, showing flashes of real brilliance which earned him the privilege of choosing his own parts. Muni was born Frederich Meier Weisenfreund in 1895 in Austria-Hungary. When he was seven, he emigrated with his family to Chicago and was nicknamed “Moony". He started his acting career in the Yiddish theatre. Film historian Robert Osborne writes that his makeup skills were so consummate that for most of his roles, "he transformed himself so completely, he was dubbed 'the new Lon Chaney.'" In 1929, Muni was signed by Fox and his name was anglicised to Paul Muni (derived from his nickname). He received an Oscar nomination for his first film, “The Valiant” (1929) and achieved stardom in provocative pre-Code films such as “I Am a Fugitive from a Chain Gang” and the iconic gangster film “Scarface.” (both 1932). Warner Bros signed him to a long-term contract, publicising him as "the screen's greatest actor." “Scarface” , the film for which Muni is best remembered, was written by Ben Hecht and directed by Howard Hawks, and is worth at least one viewing. Raw, violent yet oddly touching, critic Richard Corliss commented in 1974 that while it was a conventional gangster movie, it also "managed to congratulate journalism for its importance, and to chastise it for its chicanery, by underlining the newspapers' complicity in promoting the underworld image." In 1935, Muni persuaded Warner Bros. to produce “The Story of Louis Pasteur”, the first of the actor’s biographical roles, for which he won an Oscar. Muni played several historical figures, including Zola in “The Life of Emile Zola” (1937), which won Best Picture and was seen as an attack on the repression of Nazi Germany. He also played the lead role in “Juarez” (1939), opposite Bette Davis, and portrayed a Chinese peasant in “The Good Earth.” The makeup was grotesque, and the part should have gone to an Asian, but, hey, in Old Hollywood that was an impossibility. To his credit, when Irving Thalberg offered him the role, Muni said, "I'm about as Chinese as Herbert Hoover." Dissatisfied with films, he chose not to renew his contract. Muni returned to the screen occasionally in later years, playing Frédéric Chopin's teacher in the unintentionally hilarious “A Song to Remember” (1945). In 1946, he gave a winning performance in a comic role in “Angel on My Shoulder”. Muni’s final part was as a doctor in “The Last Angry Man” (1959). After that, he retired from acting due to his failing eyesight and other health problems. Muni was noted for his intense preparation for his roles. Before playing Pasteur, the actor said he “read every book on him” and found an old woman who had met him, and who remembered his mannerisms. The New York Times commented, “to Paul Muni, acting was not just a career, but an obsession", and Arthur Miller believed that Muni "was pursued by a fear of failure." Extremely eccentric, he objected to anyone wearing red in his presence, and often played the violin between takes. Although Muni was considered one of the greats, and was hero-worshiped by Marlon Brando, some film critics, such as David Thomson and Andrew Sarris, accuse him of overacting. Thomson describes Muni as "a crucial negative illustration in any argument as to what constitutes screen acting."  William Dieterle, who directed him in his three biopics, also called Muni “a slight ham at times.” Having seen four of his films, I have to admit that some of his performances haven’t travelled well. Muni died of a heart disorder in Montecito, California in 1967 at the age of 71.

A coalition of Christian lawmakers, faith leaders and civic organizations urged President Donald Trump to establish a legal immigration and humanitarian pathway for Jewish Canadians who fear persecution resulting from rising antisemitism in Canada.

In a letter sent to Trump, the National Association of Christian Lawmakers and its partners asked the 8 Department of Homeland Security to develop “lawful, secure, and appropriately expedited pathways” for eligible Jewish Canadian nationals and their immediate family members.

The letter pointed to what the signatories described as a growing climate of harassment, intimidation, vandalism, threats and violence targeting Jewish communities in Canada since the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas attack on Israel.

“These numbers represent more than statistics,” the letter read.

 “They represent families who increasingly question whether they can safely send their children to Jewish schools, worship openly, display their faith publicly, or continue building their lives in communities where they no longer feel secure.”

The group said any immigration program should have remain subject to existing law and national-security screening, including identity, criminal-history, medical and admissibility checks.
The letter also cited growing interest among Jewish Canadians in relocating to the United States.

Advocates working with affected families reportedly said more than 2,000 Jewish Canadians had expressed interest in moving because of concerns about their safety, the letter said.

The authors pointed specifically to Oklahoma, writing that Jewish and Christian leaders in Tulsa had offered to help receive Jewish Canadian families. Oklahoma Gov.

 Kevin Stitt had also communicated his willingness to welcome Jewish families seeking safety and opportunity, according to the letter.

The coalition argued that potential immigrants should not be viewed solely as refugees, but as prospective members of American communities.

“They bring talent, faith, family values, entrepreneurship, and a sincere desire to contribute to the Nation that offers them safety and religious liberty,” the letter said.
The signatories applauded Trump for his stated efforts to combat antisemitism and defend religious liberty while urging him to take decisive action on this particular issue.

MONDAY NIGHT DISPATCH UPDATE | SEPTEMBER 21

A busy Monday evening across the metro included assaults on transit, multiple crashes, medical calls at Red Rocks, a stolen vehicle arrest, an alleged attempt to run over Red Rocks staff, and several unusual animal calls. Dispatch traffic is preliminary unless otherwise noted.

LAKEWOOD / JEFFERSON COUNTY

• 8:32 PM — C-470 & Kipling: Dispatch reported a property-damage-only crash involving a BMW and a construction vehicle in the eastbound center lane. Tow trucks were discussed for both vehicles.

• 8:28 PM — I-70 near Wadsworth: A caller reported a black sedan speeding in what dispatch described as a road-rage complaint. Two occupants were reportedly inside. The caller later lost sight of the vehicle but was willing to sign a complaint.

• 8:03 PM — Kipling / Lakewood: Dispatch traffic described a crash near the 247 area in which two drivers were transported by separate ambulance companies. A Tesla reportedly stopped to help. Dispatch also referenced one driver as a protected party and said it was unclear whether another occupant had been involved.

• 7:39 PM — Highway 58 near McIntyre: Emergency crews responded to a two-vehicle collision with moderate damage. One person was evaluated for arm pain and described over the radio as a green patient. A non-emergency medic was requested, and one patient reportedly did not want hospital transport.

• 7:35 PM — Highway 8 westbound: Engines 60 and 101 were dispatched to a reported vehicle collision.

• 7:07 PM — I-470: A disabled white pickup was reported on the eastbound shoulder near the 7 exit. The vehicle was not drivable, but no immediate hazard was reported and a private tow was reportedly on the way.

• 6:43 PM — I-70 near Genesee Park: A motorist or pedestrian assistance call was created after someone apparently needed directions. The incident was subsequently cleared.

• 6:10 PM — Westbound Sixth Avenue near Wadsworth: Dispatch reported an abandoned vehicle affecting a lane. Lakewood was arranging for its removal. Another vehicle was reported on the right shoulder with a missing tire.

• 6:03 PM — Eastbound C-470 near Kipling: Officers conducted a traffic stop involving a silver Honda Pilot with Colorado plates.

• 6:00 PM — Ralston Road & Sheridan Boulevard: Officers discussed a minor crash. A report was taken and no injuries were reported.

• 5:58 PM — C-470 near Ken Caryl: An officer conducted a traffic stop involving a black Nissan Pathfinder and checked registration and expiration information.

• 5:53 PM — Eastbound I-70 east of Sheridan: A disabled vehicle was reported in what radio traffic described as a difficult location while a tire was being changed. Additional assistance was requested because there was reportedly no safe place to move the vehicle.

• 5:50 PM — West Mississippi Avenue & South Union Boulevard: Dispatch reported a motor vehicle collision at the Lakewood intersection.

• 5:39 PM — Jefferson County Government Center / Golden Station: Officers were dispatched for a report of a woman stumbling, screaming on the platform and walking in the bus loop.

• 5:33 PM — West 44th Avenue, Wheat Ridge: Emergency crews were dispatched to a reported possible overdose or poisoning at an apartment.

• 5:25 PM — Red Rocks: Rangers were asked to check on a deer reportedly in distress near the Rock Room on the back south side of the park. The deer was reported to have labored breathing.

• 5:10 PM — Eastbound I-70, Wheat Ridge: Crews were directed to a reported trailer fire in lane three.

• 5:07 PM — Evergreen Walmart / Swede Gulch Road: Fire and medical units responded to an unspecified incident and established command at the Walmart before incoming fire units were told to stand down.

• 4:55 PM — Sheridan Boulevard & West 30th Avenue, Wheat Ridge: Officers responded to a report of a tall, thin masked man in a tan or trench-style coat who may have had a firearm. Dispatch traffic indicated what appeared to be a firearm handle had reportedly been seen, but it was unclear whether the object was actually a gun. Officers checked the area.

• 4:28 PM — Wadsworth Boulevard & Coal Mine Avenue: Crews responded to a reported motor vehicle collision involving a person complaining of neck pain.

• 4:20 PM — Westbound US 6 near Kipling: Fire and EMS responded to a two-vehicle crash reported in the number one lane.

RED ROCKS / MORRISON

• 9:22 PM — Eastbound C-470 near Morrison Road: Dispatch received a report of four motorcycles reportedly speeding eastbound.

• 8:17 PM — Red Rocks Jurassic Lot: Dispatch received a report of an erratic driver who allegedly tried to run over staff. Staff reported feeling unsafe. The vehicle was later reported traveling north on Highway 93 before units cleared the area.

• 8:07 PM — Red Rocks Amphitheatre: Medical responders were requested for a patron reportedly experiencing possible altitude sickness and going in and out of consciousness in the seating area.

• 7:54 PM — Red Rocks Amphitheatre: Medics were requested for a patron near the top gate who was reportedly feeling faint.

• 7:54 PM — Red Rocks Amphitheatre: A separate medical response was requested for a patron on the south stairs near row 18 who was reportedly having difficulty climbing the stairs.

• 7:03 PM — Red Rocks Amphitheatre: Stadium medical requested medics for a patron experiencing shortness of breath near the north outer stairs and row 23. The patient was reportedly taken to first aid.

DENVER

• 9:22 PM — Federal Boulevard & Mexico Avenue: Dispatch reported a possible roadway blockage with a northbound Route 31 bus apparently stuck on Mexico Avenue.

• 9:21 PM — Colfax & Broadway: Officers responded to a report that a man assaulted a woman aboard a bus before getting off near 15th and California. Units planned to search the surrounding area. The direction of travel was unknown.

• 9:11 PM — Denver Union Station Bus Concourse: Officers responded to a report of a large group of juveniles causing a disturbance and harassing people. The group reportedly ran toward the CRT area. Units planned to make sure they left the property. Dispatch indicated no charges were filed and no report was made.

• 8:50 PM — Colfax near I-25: Radio traffic described an officer following a stolen vehicle. The driver was detained and taken into custody, and assisting units were advised the situation was under control.

• 8:38 PM — Bryant Street: EMS was dispatched to an apartment for a reported possible overdose with an expedited response requested.

• 8:33 PM — Capitol area / East Colfax: Dispatch traffic discussing surveillance video described an altercation between two men. The video reportedly showed a man in jeans appearing to initiate part of the confrontation before another man struck back, although the initial contact between them was not captured on camera.

• 8:27 PM — West Evans Avenue: Officers reportedly contacted a wanted person at a store. Dispatch traffic indicated the person had a warrant related to dangerous drugs.

• 8:21 PM — Lincoln Street near the Merrick: Officers responded to a reported assault involving two men. One man in a black shirt reportedly punched another, leaving one person on the ground. One person was detained while officers reviewed camera footage to determine who struck first.

• 8:16 PM — Auraria West Station: Radio traffic indicated a transit employee had reportedly been assaulted. Another unit was asked to meet or check on the employee at a nearby station.

• 7:55 PM — 22nd Street / East Center area: Medical responders were sent after a person was reportedly found face down on the ground near bus gate B.

• 7:46 PM — Mississippi Avenue & Quebec Street: A woman at a park reportedly screamed that someone had punched her in the face. Officers and a park ranger were sent to locate her and meet with Denver police.

• 7:40 PM — Park Avenue: Radio traffic described a traffic-control incident in which a worker was reportedly nearly struck multiple times. Cones, pylons and a pilot light were also reported damaged. A response unit was requested.

• 7:40 PM — Eastbound I-70 near C-470 / 44th Avenue: A blue Tesla with its hazard lights on was reported possibly blocking the right lane. Dispatch was unsure whether it was the same vehicle involved in another call, so both incidents remained open.

• 6:43 PM — South Knox Court: Animal control was dispatched for a report of a raccoon apparently having a seizure.

• 6:39 PM — 8th Street: A bus passenger reportedly struck and damaged a bus service door. The driver was instructed to stop for a street supervisor. No medical need was confirmed.

• 6:39 PM — Larimer Street: Dispatch traffic indicated a threats-related complaint remained open for police follow-up after another unit closed its portion of the call.

• 6:28 PM — South Utica Street: Officers located a red Chevrolet pickup that dispatch traffic indicated was confirmed stolen through its VIN.

• 6:27 PM — Eastbound I-76 east of Sheridan: Fender debris was reported blocking the right lane.

• 6:07 PM — South Federal Boulevard: A caller reported a loose dog running across the roadway.

• 6:04 PM — West 104th Avenue: Officers were dispatched for a report of a truck parked in an accessible parking space without a placard.

• 5:42 PM — Commons Park: A park ranger was sent near 16th and Little Raven to contact a person reportedly behaving aggressively near a park bathroom.

• 5:37 PM — Northbound I-25 south of Bellevue: Dispatch discussed a possible hit-and-run crash while agencies checked for related victim or suspect information.

• 5:35 PM — Eastbound I-70 east of Sheridan: A white Chevrolet SUV with a blown tire was reported disabled on the right shoulder.

• 5:10 PM — Northbound I-25 near 23rd Street: A disabled semi was reported mainly on the right shoulder and unable to move.

• 5:05 PM — Northbound I-25 off-ramp near Exit 167: Officers responded to a disabled vehicle on the right shoulder. Assistance was reportedly offered and declined.

• 4:55 PM — Sheridan Boulevard: Officers checked a report of a masked man who may have been carrying a firearm. Dispatch traffic indicated it was unclear whether the object was actually a gun.

• 4:27 PM — Larimer Street: A caller reported being bitten by a dog and alleged that the dog's owner threatened him. The caller requested police and said he would wait in a building lobby.

• 4:16 PM — Perry Street between Louisiana and Arkansas: A caller reported a disabled truck stopped in the roadway.

• 4:11 PM — Decatur-Federal Station: Radio traffic indicated possible vandalism to a bus. The back door and front window were reportedly broken before a relief driver took over, and a supervisor was expected to meet the driver to document the damage.

• 4:07 PM — Train inbound to Union Station: Security and other units responded after a person was reportedly charging at security aboard a train. Dispatch traffic indicated units checked for weapons and broadcast suspect descriptions.

ARVADA

• 9:07 PM — West 58th Avenue: Engine 21 remained on or responding to a reported motor vehicle crash while another unit was cleared.

• 8:50 PM — Wadsworth Bypass near West 62nd Avenue: Medical crews were dispatched for a reported sick person at a church.

• 8:50 PM — Park Terrace Apartments / West 53rd Avenue: Engine 51 was dispatched to a reported medical emergency.

• 7:45 PM — Highway 58 westbound near 44th Avenue: Medic 21 was dispatched to a reported motor vehicle collision.

• 4:55 PM — Kipling near 52nd: Fire crews investigated smoke reported inside a four-story apartment building. The resident later reported everything was okay and that the smoke may have come from burnt beans.

THORNTON / NORTHGLENN

• 7:27 PM — Thornton, east of York Street: Emergency crews responded to a reported death. Dispatch traffic indicated police located the person westbound about one mile east of York and that a field pronouncement of death was made. Command was later terminated.

• 6:48 PM — West 114th Way, Northglenn: Emergency crews were dispatched after a caller reported finding a man apparently deceased and said CPR was not being performed.

LONGMONT

• 4:37 PM — East 17th Avenue: An officer contacted a person who reportedly claimed that a friend had been “abducted by a bear.” Another unit checked West Magnolia for a white sedan while the first officer remained with the reporting person. Dispatch traffic later described the situation as under control. No independent confirmation of an actual bear abduction was provided.

FORT LUPTON

• 2:25 PM — South McKinley Avenue: Emergency crews responded to a single-vehicle crash where the driver was reported deceased inside a truck. Fire and rescue staged while law enforcement and the coroner were requested.

All information above comes from publicly available dispatch traffic and should be treated as preliminary until confirmed by the responding agency.

text:
Sometime in 2019, I had just completed my ND programme in Mass Communication at Kwara State Polytechnic. At the time, all I had in mind was finding a brand I could work with as a social media manager.

That same year, a photography brand in my hometown came to mind. I wanted to reach out to the owner and offer to manage their social media, but I was honestly too shy to make the move.

Then, in 2020, I did my freedom in fashion designing, and that became a turning point for me.

It suddenly occurred to me that instead of trying to manage someone else’s brand online, I could actually build and manage my own brand strategically.

That year, I opened social media accounts for @dukefashionhq , my own fashion brand, and Ola Chops, my brother’s brand. I started promoting both brands back-to-back.

At the time, my goal was simple: I just wanted to learn social media management and gain experience in that field.

But ever since I launched Duke Fashion, I’ve gained much more than I initially set out to learn.

I’ve gained experience in social media management, business management, leadership, human resource management, partnerships, customer relations, marketing, and so much more.

Looking back now, I realise something:

Sometimes, you think you are dreaming big because you are pursuing a particular goal, not knowing that the goal itself might be limiting you.

You may be chasing one opportunity when you are actually capable of creating your own.

You may be trying to work for a brand when you have the capacity to build one.

Sometimes, the bigger picture is beyond what you can currently see.

So, dream. But don’t be afraid to dream beyond the goal you have already set for yourself.
