text:
Beijing's AI coalition offers countries a seat at the table. Washington's offers them a place in the supply chain. One of those is worth more to a country that isn't a superpower, and it's why China's group already has more members despite launching seven months later.

Kazakhstan joined both within eight weeks, and it's not an outlier. Most swing states are treating supply-chain access and governance voice as separate goods, not competing loyalties, which is exactly why Washington's push to force an exclusive choice keeps running into countries that see no reason to choose.

The variable that actually determines which architecture wins isn't the AI models themselves. It's whether any OECD country joins WAICO. That single move triggered a wave of Western membership in China's infrastructure bank a decade ago, and there's no structural reason AI plays out differently if Washington doesn't put a governance offer, not just a supply chain deal, on the table first.

Oil falls 1% after reports suggest Iran could reopen Hormuz within seven days

"Potential US-Iran talks emerge ahead of UN General Assembly
Saudi oil exports via Strait of Hormuz increase over weekend
Global diesel prices hit record highs, further rises possible.

 Oil prices fell on Tuesday after reports that ​Iran said it could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if the US takes initial steps to ‌ease military pressure, easing concerns over disruptions to a key global oil shipping route.

The Brent crude futures November contract fell 89 cents, or 0.89%, to $99.45 a barrel at 0932 GMT. The WTI October contract, which expires on Tuesday, lost $1.09, or 1.14%, to $94.69 a barrel.
The more actively traded November contract was down $1.31, ​or 1.42%, at $91.06 a barrel.

Iran has offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if the US takes ​initial steps toward easing military pressure, a senior Iranian government official told Kyodo News on Tuesday, as ⁠part of Tehran's ramped-up efforts to revive negotiations with Washington.

Before US-Israeli attacks on Iran began in late February, the strait handled about one-fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas supplies.

Market focus is also on US President Donald Trump's meetings with world leaders at the UN General Assembly ​this week, against the backdrop of an unstable Middle East and a four-and-a-half-year-old war in Ukraine that shows no signs of abating.

Tehran and Washington exchanged ‌threats ⁠on Sunday, although Trump said he would be open to meeting Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, who is expected to be in New York this week for the UN meeting.
Over the weekend, Iran also conveyed its conditions to mediators for re-engaging in negotiations, Al Jazeera reported, citing Iran's security chief, Mohsen Rezaei.
Meanwhile, Saudi Aramco has increased exports through the Strait of Hormuz after attacks on its East-West Pipeline forced it to halt some shipments through Yanbu. ​Around 14 million barrels of ​its crude oil were loaded ⁠on seven supertankers inside the Gulf on Sunday, tanker tracking data showed.

Separately, an armed group closed valve seven on Libya's Sharara crude pipeline to Zawiya port on Monday, resulting in a significant decline in production at ​the Sharara oilfield, Libya's National Oil Corporation said in a statement.
Production at the field has fallen ​by around 200,000 ⁠barrels per day and is currently between 100,000 and 105,000 bpd, two engineers at the field told Reuters.

Diesel prices have rallied in Europe and the United States ​to record highs as wars in Iran and Ukraine sharply cut exports from some of the biggest producers such as Russia, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates."

text:
🌅 MARKET BRIEF — SEPT. 22, 2026

Oil just got the test we said would matter most: 

→ can it still ignore diplomacy when the barrels haven't moved?

For a month, crude has demanded physical evidence... tanker counts, Hormuz transit data, Aramco capacity... before repricing supply risk. 

Rhetoric kept failing to move it.

Overnight, that rule met its opposite.

Kyodo, citing a single unverified source, reported that Iran has offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days. 

There is no confirmation from Tehran, Washington or Oman, and no new barrel count behind the report.

Brent and WTI are falling anyway, heading toward a fifth straight losing session.... their longest slide since June.

That's the market question this morning.

Not whether the report is true.

→ Whether oil is willing to price it as though it might be.

→ If Brent keeps falling through the session without Oman or Tehran confirming the offer, the rule we've been tracking has changed: 
- an unverified diplomatic signal would have achieved what confirmed physical data used to be required to do.

→ The 10-year is riding the same move.

It closed Monday near 4.97%, down 3bps as oil fell, even as Kashkari and Goolsbee warned that inflation remains hotter than the energy shock alone explains. 

Williams speaks today. ADP lands too.

→ If yields keep easing while Fed voices remain hawkish, duration is still taking its cue from the barrel rather than the committee.

→ Equities have a different test.

Monday's record Nasdaq close still had an AI-and-mega-cap engine underneath it, although the Russell 2000's 0.67% gain offered the first sign the bid was spreading.

This morning, futures are essentially flat: S&P and Nasdaq slightly lower, Dow barely green.

So Tuesday isn't being asked to create another rally.

It's being asked to prove Monday's breadth wasn't a one-day event.

→ Gold and Bitcoin carry the final divergence.

Gold retreated Monday while Bitcoin broke above $86,000. 

→ If yields ease again today and gold still can't find a bid while Bitcoin holds the breakout, lower real yields alone no longer explain the gap.

Three tests into the close:

→ Does Brent keep falling without confirmation of the Hormuz report?

→ Does the 10-year keep easing while Fed speakers lean hawkish?

→ Does gold respond to lower yields while Bitcoin holds above $86,000?

Wednesday's Trump-Xi summit remains the week's major event.

Today is the session that tells us how much of tomorrow the market is willing to price early.

Orange Is the New Beach: How Autumn’s Boldest Color Takes Over

As autumn arrives, an undeniable obsession with the color orange takes hold, transforming everything from our culinary cravings to the natural landscape. This seasonal infatuation goes far beyond the ubiquitous pumpkin spice lattes and festive decorations, extending into unexpected places like vibrant orange watermelons gracing late-season harvest markets. The warmth of the hue culminates perfectly in the evening sky, where beautiful fall sunsets paint the beach in breathtaking shades of amber and tangerine, making it feel as though the entire world has been dipped in orange.

READ MORE:  https://t.co/UZkzPeIP83

For those eager to get their autumn caffeine fix, stopping by local favorites like Happy Pappy Coffee Shop or BuzzCatz Coffee and Sweets is an absolute must. BuzzCatz offers an inviting atmosphere alongside its famous pastries, rich brews, and warm cinnamon treats—the ultimate comforting pairing when you are craving that quintessential pumpkin spice warmth on a crisp morning.

If you are looking to bring home a piece of the seasonal harvest, head over to Krupinski Farms in Foley. Known for its wide array of vibrant fall produce, you can pick out traditional orange pumpkins to decorate your porch or sample their unique, sweet orange watermelons. It is a delightful farm-fresh trip that perfectly captures the cheerful spirit and rich colors of the season.

RELATED ARTICLE:  100 Years of Farm Fresh Growth

Finally, there is no better way to cap off a crisp autumn day than by watching the sunset while taking a peaceful stroll along the shores of Orange Beach. As the golden hour fades, brilliant orange, deep coral, and soft violet hues streak across the sky and reflect off the gentle coastal waters, offering a serene and majestic end to a fall day on the Gulf.

As spooky season rolls in, it feels as though we are on the verge of being completely taken over by mischief-making goblins, Halloween ghouls, and an unending wave of pumpkin spice. Yet with a city named right after the defining color of fall itself, there is no denying that we are in the absolute best spot to enjoy every bit of autumn's vibrant magic.

text:
“Stopped?” Genevieve repeated, saying the word as if it had crawled onto the table and died there.

“Yes, they are stopped.”

“You cannot simply do that to us,” she said.

“My banker apparently disagreed with you,” I replied.

Benjamin leaned forward. “Mother, the mortgage payment bounced this morning.”

“I imagine it would have.”

“Our insurance draft did too.”

“Yes.”

“The school called me in a panic.”

“That was remarkably fast.”

Genevieve placed both hands on the back of a chair. Her diamond rings flashed in the pale kitchen light. “Clara’s school is not a weapon to be used against us.”

I looked toward the living room. Clara was pretending to pet the rabbit’s ears, but her shoulders were rigid.

“No,” I said. “A child is not a weapon. That is precisely why I have been paying for her care while you remodeled your kitchen twice in three years.”

Genevieve’s mouth opened and closed. Benjamin whispered, “Mother, please.”

I knew that tone of voice well; it was the one he used in public whenever I said something inconveniently true.

“Do not,” I warned. “I am far too old to be shushed in my own kitchen.”

For a moment, I saw him at nine years old, standing in this same room with a scraped knee and a missing front tooth, crying because Thomas had told him he could not quit the baseball team just because he struck out. He had been tender then and easily wounded. I wondered when love had transformed into a bill I paid on a monthly basis.

Genevieve pulled out a chair at last and sat down slowly, as though she were lowering herself into enemy territory.

“Let us be reasonable about this,” she said.

That request frightened me more than her anger ever could. Reasonable was the word people used when they had already decided what sacrifice belonged to you.

“I am being reasonable,” I said. “I paid what I chose to pay, and now I choose not to.”

“You made us dependent on you,” Genevieve said.

The words hung in the air, absurd and perfect. Benjamin looked at her sharply. I folded my hands on the table.

“I made you dependent?” I asked.

“You offered,” she said. “You repeatedly inserted yourself into our finances and our emotions, and now you are punishing us for accepting your help.”

A younger version of me might have apologized, and an older version might have wept, but I was seventy seven years old. Grief had sharpened me, and the long, cold stretch of loneliness had hollowed out enough space for the truth to echo.

“I did not insert myself into anything,” I said. “I was invited whenever money was required and excluded whenever human dignity was actually necessary.”

Benjamin flinched, but Genevieve did not. She was studying me now, truly studying me, the way a person studies a locked door after years of assuming it had no bolt.

“Mother,” Benjamin said quietly, “we are in serious trouble.”

There it was, the first honest sentence of the day. I waited. He swallowed hard.

“The townhouse closing depends on clean accounts. The investors were at dinner because there is a partnership deal. Genevieve’s family is heavily involved. If payments start declining, it could ruin everything.”

“Everything,” I repeated.

His eyes lifted to meet mine. “Please.”

That word should have moved me, and once upon a time, it certainly would have. I would have written a check before the second syllable left his mouth. Instead, I saw Thomas in the hospital, his hand slowly disappearing inside mine. I saw myself asking Benjamin if he could stay another night, and Benjamin telling me Genevieve had a social engagement. I saw myself at seventy seven, dressed in navy blue, pearls ready, waiting to be allowed into a home that my own money had helped furnish…..

Actually, the greatest lesson the PLA learned is from the misfortune of the US Navy in the Persian Gulf in the last 3 years.

From a PLA analyst’s vantage point, the U.S. experience in the Red Sea and Persian Gulf is a textbook demonstration of vulnerabilities that China must exploit and avoid.

Lessons from Operation Prosperity Guardian (Houthis) – Dec 2023 to 2024

1. Cheap      drones and missiles overwhelm expensive platforms
- Houthis       used low‑cost UAVs and cruise missiles to saturate U.S. destroyers.
- Each       intercept cost millions, while the attacker spent thousands.
- PLA       takeaway: asymmetric saturation erodes U.S. naval staying power.

2. Attrition      of readiness
- Continuous       interceptions degraded U.S. ships’ missile stocks and crew endurance.
- PLA       sees that prolonged harassment can hollow out U.S. combat effectiveness       without decisive battles.

3. ISR      gaps
- Houthis       exploited concealment and mobility, launching from dispersed sites.
- PLA       notes that U.S. reliance on centralized ISR can be strained by swarms and       deception.

Lessons from Iranian Strikes on US Persian Gulf Bases

1. Base      vulnerability
- U.S.       fixed bases in Qatar, Bahrain, and Kuwait were destroyed by Iranian       drones and missiles.
- PLA       takeaway: forward bases are soft targets; survivability depends on       mobility and dispersion.

2. Air      defense saturation
Even       layered U.S. defenses were overwhelmed.
PLA       sees proof that massed precision fires can neutralize advanced systems.

3. Strategic      paralysis
- With       bases neutralized, U.S. logistics and command collapsed.
- PLA       takeaway: striking infrastructure is more decisive than attritional       combat.

Application to Taiwan theatre
- PLA      A2/AD strategy: replicate Iran’s success by saturating U.S. bases and      carrier groups with missiles, drones, and cyber attacks, denying      intervention in the Strait.
- Resilient      supply chain: unlike Russia, China fights next door to its industrial      base. Factories, ports, and rail lines on the mainland can sustain      operations indefinitely.
- Mobility      over fixed assets: Taiwan’s earthquake‑prone terrain makes deep silos      impractical; PLA recognizes that mobile brigades and dispersed launchers      are harder to neutralize.
- Compressed      battlespace: unlike Ukraine’s vast land war, Taiwan offers no depth.      PLA must achieve rapid dominance before external forces can mobilize.
-Taiwan      cannot build deep underground missile bases like Iran: as it sits on      the Pacific Ring of Fire and is earthquake prone.

Bottom Line
China’s lesson is that the U.S. Navy and Gulf bases were defeated not by superior technology but by cheap saturation, mobility, and precision strikes. For the PLA, the imperative is to avoid Russia’s logistical failures, exploit Iran’s success in base suppression, and leverage its own A2/AD shield and industrial depth to ensure that a Taiwan contingency is decided quickly, before the U.S. can recover.

𝗛𝗮𝗼𝘁𝗶𝗮𝗻 𝗕𝗮𝗶 (白昊天), the founder of 𝗣𝗮𝘁𝗿𝗶𝗼𝘁 𝗖𝗼𝗻𝗰𝗲𝗽𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀 (培恩生育)

Wealthy Chinese couples are implanting their embryos into American women so their children can be born as US citizens. The service is provided by a surrogacy agency, Patriot Conceptions (培恩生育), which operates between China and the US and has been accused of hiding details of who the biological parents are from surrogates.

Women who carry babies for the agency are recruited informally through social media and collect between $60,000 and $120,000 for their services.

The children are then swept off by their parents to be raised in China, where it is seen as a status symbol among the wealthy to have a child able to claim US citizenship.

Incredibly, such a service is completely legal, thanks to free-wheeling surrogacy laws and liberal interpretations of the birthright citizenship clause in the Fourteenth Amendment, recently reaffirmed by the Supreme Court.

Patriot Conceptions is run by US Army vet Haotian Bai — who founded the international surrogacy agency and last year received a prestigious fellowship from a top Republican think tank, which describes him as a “pioneering entrepreneur in the third-party reproduction” sector.

Bai’s Irvine, Calif.-based Patriot Conceptions grabbed headlines last week when a surrogate identified as “Judy” came forward when she discovered she was carrying the child of reclusive Chinese billionaire Xu Bo (徐波), who has allegedly sired over 300 children.

She said she had responded to an Instagram ad for Patriot Conceptions, who arranged the surrogacy.
The company said it had only arranged that surrogacy on Bo’s behalf and “the surrogate deserves to have her concerns taken seriously.”

In a 2024 profile on the US Chamber of Commerce’s website, Bai claimed his company helped thousands of parents have children via surrogacy, and 40 percent of his clients were “international.”

A review of the company’s promotional materials suggests those international clients are almost entirely from China. The company offers Chinese or English versions of its website and instructs visitors that the best way to get in touch is through their WeChat channel.

The website also maps the 25 states providing a “generally supportive posture” for the child to easily obtain US citizenship, advising foreign parents to familiarize themselves with the laws in each state when selecting a surrogate. Only one state, Louisiana, is colored black for “restrictive or unresolved posture.”

Bai previously built a US-based surrogacy company catering to Chinese parents in 2019, called Pacific Surrogacy. It was also based in California, which has among the nation’s loosest surrogacy laws.

A lawsuit between Bai and his then-business partner, Yulun Jiang, revealed the company’s financials were all run out of China.

Bai also recently launched a mysterious app called TrustUS, which describes itself as “a Software as a Service company” which facilitates international bank transfers and payments.

Patriot Conceptions’ base cost for future parents is listed as $120,000–$200,000. Typically, Chinese parents come to the US on a tourist visa to complete their embryo work, although in some cases, parents will simply ship embryos from their home country to the US, where they can be implanted in American surrogates.

Bai arrived in the US around 2012 from Lanzhou University in China to pursue a master’s degree in environmental engineering at Iowa State University. Bai graduated from the program and “joined the Army to get citizenship”, which at the time was welcoming non-citizens to enlist in exchange for fast-tracked Green Cards.

Bai climbed to the rank of lieutenant and his service brought him to Hawaii, where he lives today.

In 2019, Bai was identified as a “Hawaii realtor” in local reports, and was accused of selling Hawaiian legislative internships to students from China for $5,000-a-pop.

A Kentucky man turned down $8 million MULTIPLE TIMES to build a data center on his family land.
Dr. Tim Grosser owns 250 acres of farmland outside Maysville, Kentucky.

SCOTT BESSENT: "NO LIABILITY SHIELD FOR AI LABS" - US TREASURY REFUSES TO PROTECT TECH GIANTS FROM LAWSUITS OVER "ROGUE" AGENTS

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent delivered a stark message on CNBC: the administration has no intention of granting tech giants a legal liability shield for the actions of their AI models.

Key Takeaways:

* No Legal Immunity: AI developers pushed to strip away liability in the event that autonomous agents breach safety boundaries. The Treasury's stance is definitive: accountability rests firmly with management and founders, not the algorithm.

* Real-World Incidents: Spurred by recent cases of AI agents breaking out at Google, OpenAI, Anthropic, and Hugging Face, regulators are demanding a pivot from pure parameter scaling to cybersecurity and system resilience.

* 12-Hour US–China Summit: Washington and Beijing conducted intensive talks, establishing the official USA-China AI Dialogues alongside an incident hotline for emergency communication regarding AI safety events. Chinese officials officially acknowledged that the US maintains the global lead in AI.

AI labs have been playing a remarkably convenient double game for far too long. On one hand, they parade around warning the public about a "10% chance of an extinction-level event"-a narrative that works wonders for securing trillion-dollar valuations and erecting massive regulatory moats against upstart competitors. On the other hand, they turn to the government and ask to be completely absolved of financial and criminal liability if their autonomous agent "accidentally" breaches financial systems or leaks sensitive data.

Refusing to grant them immunity marks a monumental turning point for the entire agentic AI market. When a lab is held financially and legally accountable for every single failure of its product, it fundamentally reshapes the cost structure of AI development:

1. A Shift Away From Pure Scaling Laws: Capital will no longer flow solely into compute clusters for raw capabilities; massive resources must now go into mathematically verifiable guardrails and deterministic control protocols.

2. Re-Evaluating B2B Autonomy: Enterprise clients will think twice before deploying unconstrained agents into production until developers offer concrete legal guarantees.

3. The Rise of Defense Infrastructure: The defining trend of this era won't just be building the smartest frontier models, but constructing "Frontier Defense"-mirroring the cybersecurity standards of systemically important financial institutions.

The era where developers could brush off algorithmic failures as the "unpredictable nature of neural networks" is officially over

📌 Can South Korea’s Tech Giants Stage a Comeback? Decoding the Memory Cycle

🚨 What Happened?

After plunging 44% from its June peak, South Korea’s KOSPI index closed up 1.65% at 7,007.72, showing signs of a potential market rebound. At the center of this movement, Samsung and SK hynix are raking in massive profits driven by the artificial intelligence boom, even as they trade at historically low valuation multiples of around 4x estimated earnings.

🔍 The Breakdown

🎯 The Main Event: Exploding demand for high-performance memory—specifically High Bandwidth Memory (HBM, critical for feeding AI processors like Nvidia's), conventional DRAM, and NAND flash storage—has driven operating margins sky-high, highlighted by SK hynix posting a staggering 76% operating margin in Q2.

💡 Why It Matters: The core market debate centers on whether investors are underestimating the duration of these peak profits. In cyclical industries, several consecutive years of outsized earnings can fundamentally rerate a company's valuation. 

Furthermore, both firms are backing up their balance sheets with massive shareholder returns, including a 40 trillion won ($25B EUR) share buyback/cancellation program by SK hynix and massive shareholder distributions targeted by Samsung for 2026.

🎒 Concept Check: A PER (Price-to-Earnings Ratio) compares a company's stock price to its per-share earnings. A very low PER (like the ~4x multiple cited for these chipmakers) can either signal an incredible deep-value buying opportunity or indicate that current profits are sitting at a cyclical peak right before a sharp downturn.

💡 Key Considerations

SK hynix vs. Samsung: SK hynix offers a pure-play, direct exposure to advanced memory and HBM4 growth. Samsung is vastly more diversified industrially, but its semiconductor division currently accounts for nearly all of the group's operating profits.

The Currency Factor: For international investors, the recent strengthening of the Korean won against major currencies (~10% against the euro) must be factored into total returns, as currency fluctuations can eat into equity gains.

Signals to Monitor: To evaluate whether this rebound has staying power, watch three critical indicators: underlying memory pricing trends, free cash flow conversion after heavy capital expenditures (CapEx) in new fab facilities, and actual execution of announced share buybacks.

text:
📌 Trading Strategy: How To Secure Your Principal And Keep "Free Shares"

🚨 What Happened?

This popular portfolio management strategy is often called "playing with house money" or locking in your initial principal. When a stock climbs significantly, you sell just enough shares to recover 100% of your original cash investment, leaving the remaining profit invested entirely as "free shares."

🔍 The Breakdown

🎯 The Main Event: To execute this, you calculate the exact number of shares needed to match your initial cash outlay at the current market price and sell only that portion. For instance, if you buy 100 shares for $5,000 ($50 each) and the price jumps to $65, selling 77 shares recovers $5,005 in cash.

💡 Why It Matters: You eliminate your downside risk completely—your initial capital is back in your account, and any future gains from your remaining shares are 100% profit. In our example, you retain 23 "free shares" worth $1,495 riding the market risk-free.

🎒 Concept Check: "Playing with house money" is like a gambler pulling their original stake off the table after an early win, ensuring that any subsequent bets are made purely with casino winnings rather than out-of-pocket cash.

💡 Key Considerations

Taxes: In most jurisdictions, selling those shares triggers a taxable capital gains event on the profits realized during that sale.

Fractional Shares: If your broker supports fractional trading, you can sell exact partial shares (e.g., 76.92 shares) to recover your principal down to the exact penny.

The USDA allows and regulates halal-slaughtered meat in school cafeterias, but it does not mandate that schools provide it. Whether halal meat is served depends entirely on the policy of your local school district. [1, 2]USDA 

Regulations & Rules on Halal MeatFederal Inspection and Compliance: Halal meat served in schools must still pass all standard federal safety inspections. The USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS) grants "religious exemptions" regarding specific slaughter methods (such as ritual slaughter without prior stunning) to comply with Islamic law, provided the facility maintains strict humane handling and sanitation standards. [1, 2]

USDA Foods Certification: Under the National School Lunch Program (NSLP), schools buy a large portion of their food using federal funds. 

The USDA maintains a TEFAP Foods Available List where officially certified halal items are explicitly marked with an "(H)" next to the product name. [1, 2]

School Meal Credits: To be served in cafeterias, certified halal meat products must still meet standard USDA meal contribution guidelines (e.g., providing the required ounces of daily meat/meat alternate). [1]

How Accommodations Work in Schools
Because the choice is localized, cafeteria offerings vary significantly across the country:High-Density Muslim Areas: School districts with large Muslim populations—such as Dearborn Public Schools in Michigan—frequently serve 100% certified halal meat options to all students. [1]

Vegetarian Alternatives: In school districts that do not offer certified halal meats, cafeterias meet USDA federal guidelines by offering meatless alternatives (such as pasta, baked potatoes, grilled cheese, or salads) so observant students can still eat. [1]

Cross-Contamination Rules: If a school decides to add halal choices, the USDA and food advocacy groups highlight that preparation requires strict separation—using dedicated cutting boards, separate containers, and clean utensils to prevent cross-contamination with non-halal or pork products. text:
America has the leverage. That’s not an opinion. That’s geography and a 12-to-1 economy. Roughly 70% of what we sell still goes south. Europe is high single digits. Pipelines, auto parts, electricity, and the shop floor were not built for Brussels.
Yes, Trump is a blowhard. Yes, he says dumb, unnecessary shit because dumb shit gets a reaction. Nobody likes being the one on the wrong end of leverage. Fine. Stated.
That does not mean the correct Canadian move is to maximize the bill at home so the posture looks pure.
Being unwilling to sign a last-minute deal that asked too much and offered too little is defensible. Walking off the table and then matching 50% dollar-for-dollar on ~$20–28 billion — steel doubled, appliances, dairy, electronics, the whole theatre list — is a different choice. That is not a scalpel. That is a political statement: we will eat pain so nobody can say we folded.
The smaller, more open economy eats more of that pain. That is not mysterious. It is arithmetic. Reciprocal tariffs are not a morality play. They are a tax on your own importers, your own input costs, and your own consumers, levied so the speech still works.
“We’re moving on from the old order” is a line. It is not a market. Associate membership talk and an EU summit do not replace Michigan, the Midwest grid, or four decades of continental supply chains. Other countries took ugly deals and kept selling. We chose the walk-off, the matching tariff, and the Europe tour. That combination only makes sense if the product being sold is demonstration — we will not be leveraged, we are “at war,” diversification as identity — more than damage this quarter and next.
Firmness at the table, then the best available deal, then moving on: one strategy.
Firmness, then maximizing the home-side invoice so the optics stay clean: another.

Warren Buffett spent $1.3 billion on Coca-Cola stock. Today that position pays $848 million per year in dividends. He has never sold a single share.

He was born in Omaha, Nebraska. At six years old he was selling Coca-Cola bottles door to door for a few cents of profit each. At 11 he bought his first stock. Three shares of Cities Service Preferred at $38.25 each.

The stock dropped to $27. His sister reminded him every day that he was losing her money. When it recovered to $40 he sold. Total profit: $5 per share.

The stock later hit $202.

At 13 he filed his first tax return. At 14 he bought a farm and rented it to a tenant farmer. By 16 he had saved $5,000. That is $85,000 in today's money.

He went to Columbia Business School. Studied under Benjamin Graham, the father of value investing. In 1956 he started the Buffett Partnership in Omaha with $100,000. Over 13 years it compounded at 31 percent annually.

In 1962 he started buying shares of a failing textile company in New England. The stock was $7.50 per share. The company was called Berkshire Hathaway.

He wound down the textile operations. Started buying other businesses. Insurance companies. Candy shops. Newspapers. Furniture stores. He turned a dying textile company into a holding company for everything he wanted to own.

In the fall of 1988 he started buying Coca-Cola. Over the next year he spent $1.3 billion. It was the largest position Berkshire had ever taken.

After multiple stock splits Berkshire now owns 400 million shares worth $35 billion. The position pays $848 million per year in dividends. That is a 65 percent annual return on the original investment from dividends alone.

In August 2011 he called the CEO of Bank of America. The stock was collapsing. He offered $5 billion in preferred shares and got warrants to buy 700 million common shares at $7.14 each. The deal took one day. When he exercised the warrants in 2017 the shares were worth $17 billion. Profit on the warrants alone: $12 billion.

His favorite book on investing is not about investing. It is about baseball.

Ted Williams wrote "The Science of Hitting" in 1971. He divided the strike zone into 77 cells. In his best cell he batted .400. In his worst he hit .230. His rule was simple. Only swing at pitches in your best zone.

Buffett took that idea and turned it into his entire philosophy. In investing, he said, there are no called strikes. You can stand at the plate all day. Nobody forces you to swing. All day you wait for the pitch you like. Then when the fielders are asleep you step up and hit it.

He tells students to imagine they have a punch card with 20 slots. Every investment punches a hole. When the card is full you are done for life. He said from those 20 investments, maybe three or five would make you rich.

In July 1991 Bill Gates met Buffett for the first time. Gates did not want to go. His mother had invited Buffett to a family dinner. Gates thought investing was parasitic. They talked for hours. Gates later said Buffett asked amazingly good questions nobody had ever asked him.

A single share of Berkshire Hathaway that cost $7.50 in 1962 is worth $759,350 today. Forbes puts Buffett's net worth at $145 billion.

The man who has been investing for 84 years did not build a $145 billion fortune by finding more opportunities than everyone else. He built it by having the discipline to ignore almost all of them.

In 1754, near Paris, Chevalier de Bonneville established the Chapter of Clermont. The Chapter resided in the College of Jesuits of Clermont, hence the name. It is said to have been created to honor the Duc de Clermont, then Grand Master of the English Grand Lodge of France.

The Chapter of Clermont was a “Chapter of the Advanced Degrees” and initially entailed six degrees and was later extended to 25 known degrees. The six initial degrees were 1˚, 2˚ and 3˚ St John’s Masonry, 4˚ Knight of the Eagle, 5˚ Illustrious Knight or Templar, 6˚ Sublime Illustrious Knight.

Interestingly enough historically, prior to the time of the Rite’s creation, James II had been in residence at Clermont in exile from Britain from 1688 to his death in 1701. As noted by German Masonic historian, Lenning… “whilst in exile, James II residing at the Jesuit College of Clermont in France, allowed his closest associates to fabricate certain degrees in order to extend their political views.” Lenning believed this to have been an attempt on the part of James and his associates to regain control of the British throne for the House of Stuart. If Lenning is right, this places the origins of the “Rite of Perfection” in the hands of James II and the Jacobite (Stuart) Freemasons who at the time were in exile from Great Britain throughout France and Italy. Lenning also contends that these degrees were introduced into French Freemasonry under the name of the Clermont System.

James II died in exile in 1701. His son James III is said to have continued his father’s Masonic legacy and later created further higher degrees.

Perhaps James II saw in the Jesuit morality plays of the College of Clermont a vessel for passing on a set of moral lessons. Some of the world’s greatest playwrights had emerged from Clermont. Once again the angel speaks with prophetic certainty. Though Rome has not fallen yet at the time of the writing of Revelation, the angel declares its fall in the past tense to show how surely Rome and her empire will fall. Rome has become a dwelling place of wickedness and evil. Not only has Rome been the heart of wickedness, but the nations “have drunk the wine of the passion of her sexual immorality.” The nations are not innocent. They also have been participants in the immorality of Rome. The merchants of the earth has prospered through the immorality of Rome. History reveals the luxurious living that took place in Rome over the centuries because of its extensive trade routes. Trade extended well past the border of Rome’s empire, which was millions of square miles. Trade routes also existed to India and China. Archaeology has found many pottery sherds from the far east. The merchants were made rich by buying, selling, and trading goods with Rome.

Go out from Babylon, flee from Chaldea, declare this with a shout of joy, proclaim it, send it out to the end of the earth; say, “The LORD has redeemed his servant Jacob!” (Isaiah 48:20 ESV)Depart, depart, go out from there; touch no unclean thing; go out from the midst of her; purify yourselves, you who bear the vessels of the LORD. (Isaiah 52:11 ESV)“Flee from the midst of Babylon; let every one save his life! Be not cut off in her punishment, for this is the time of the LORD’s vengeance, the repayment he is rendering her. Babylon was a golden cup in the LORD’s hand, making all the earth drunken; the nations drank of her wine; therefore the nations went mad. (Jeremiah 51:6–7 ESV)

Otherwise, you will share in the plagues that are coming upon Rome and her empire. The judgment of the seven bowls showed seven plagues being poured out on the beast and its throne. God gives an important warning. If you act like the world, you will be judged with the world. Come out from the world and separate yourselves from the Roman ways and sins. They have heaped up their sins as high as the heavens and God has remembered those sins. God is going to pay her back. God is going to pay her double for her deeds. This is just because its sins were so severe that it not only affect them, but also carried the whole world into sinfulness with its idolatry and paganism. God calls for a double portion to be mixed for her in the cup. Recall that we saw this cup as the cup of God’s anger poured full strength (Revelation 14:10). They think this prosperity will never end because they think they did it all. They rule and think that rule will never end. God says in verse 8 that this is the reason that they will be struck down suddenly. Rather than life and prosperity, the empire will crumble into death, mourning, and famine. Revelation is not predicting that Rome fell in one day, just as the scriptures are not predicting other nations falling in one day (cf. Isaiah 47:9). It is a symbol of the suddenness of the loss of power and authority. It would seem that the empire would never end and suddenly the empire will be in trouble. It will lose its power and be destroyed. This is the imagery of the fire. Revelation is not predicting Rome literally burning (cf. Isaiah 47:14). The fire is a symbol of judgment. Its time of glory and rule is over. The empire has fallen. Rome has lost her power.

The SURA proposal, initially in competition with proposals from Massachusetts Institute of Technology, University of Illinois, Argonne National Laboratory, and the National Bureau of Standards, was selected in 1983. In 1987 in Newport News, Virginia, construction began on the world’s first large-scale superconducting electron accelerator: the Continuous Electron Beam Accelerator Facility (CEBAF). The first experiments began in the mid 1990’s taking advantage of electron energies as high as 4 GeV. In 1996, CEBAF was officially renamed the Thomas Jefferson National Accelerator Facility, although the machine known as CEBAF is still the main device at the facility.

The following history of the Navy’s interest in high energy lasers (HEL) is graciously provided by John Albertine, former director of PMS-405, the Navy’s directed energy weapons program office.

The first laser type which was scaled to high power (relative to Navy weapon needs), was a combustion driven CO2 laser which lased on one of a few lines between 9.8 and 10.6 / mi . This occurred in the 1960’s and early 1970’s. These devices were used by the Navy for materials interaction tests, component development, and beam control and propagation experiments. From an atmospheric scattering standpoint, this was a good wavelength for maritime propagation but it was quickly learned that molecular water absorption was high enough to make thermal blooming a serious problem for self defense or escort scenario applications

A new combustion driven laser technology was developed in the early to mid 1970’s which offered potential for improvement. The deuterium fluoride (DF) laser was scaled to high power with work funded by the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) and the Navy at Aerospace Corporation, Navy Research Laboratory (NRL), TRW, and a few other places. These devices lased simultaneously on a half-dozen lines between 3.6 and 4.0 /mi and were commonly described as lasing at 3.8 /mi. A series of experiments, called Unified Navy Field Test Program (UNFTP), were run at TRW (San Juan Capistrano test site) in 1977 and ’78. These combined the sub-MW class NaCl laser with the Navy Pointer Tracker (NPT) beam director to provide the Navy’s first integrated HEL test bed. The tests were quite successful and shot down Army tube-launched, optically tracked, wire-guided (TOW) missiles in crossing engagements. This encouraged the Navy to proceed with DF technology

The Navy then built the MW-class Mid-Infrared Advanced Chemical Laser (MIRACL) and the SeaLite Beam Director (SLBD) beam director. These were to provide fullscale performance for Navy weapon needs although using experimental hardware. This system was integrated at the White Sands Missile Range HEL System Test Facility (HELSTF) and successfully tested between the mid-1980’s and about 1992. Subsonic and supersonic missiles were shot down in crossing engagements

Watched the @Nerdrotic video claiming “Paramount is leaving California” and Hollywood “found out.”
It makes for easy culture-war rage bait, but once you examine antitrust filings, M&A mechanics, and labor economics, the entire premise falls apart.
Here is the breakdown 🧵👇
The "Paramount is moving to Texas/Tennessee" threat was leverage, not reality.
Paramount faced an impending $7M-per-day ticking fee payable to WBD shareholders if the merger didn't close. Leaking an impending California exit was an eleventh-hour pressure tactic to force regulators to the table.
The bluff completely dissolved in court.
Paramount Skydance signed a legally binding consent decree with California AG Rob Bonta and 11 states:
• They are legally prohibited from selling or closing their historic LA studio lots.
• They committed to $1.5B in production spend in CA and the US over 5 years.
They aren't packing up. They're locked in.
The antitrust lawsuit wasn't a "TikTok stunt." It was legitimate Clayton Act enforcement.
Merging two of the "Big Five" legacy studios into an $80B–$111B conglomerate triggers serious horizontal consolidation concerns under federal antitrust law.
If it were frivolous posturing, Paramount wouldn’t have surrendered massive structural concessions.
Regulators extracted concrete, legally binding protections:
• Mandatory slate of 30–32 theatrical releases/yr (backed by a $30M penalty per unmade film paid to workers)
• Strict 45-day theatrical window before streaming
• Unbundled cable carriage negotiations
• Independent editorial boards for CBS News and CNN
Mega-mergers eliminate jobs—they do not "save" them.
Wall Street rewards acquisitions for one reason: "synergies." That is corporate code for gutting duplicate departments, slashing development slates, and firing thousands.
Look at Disney-Fox: 4,000 to 10,000 jobs wiped out.
The job protections that did survive here (like the 5-year writer layoff ban at CBS News) were forced by unions and regulators, not executive benevolence.
Blaming union strikes for Hollywood's contraction reverses cause and effect.
The slowdown started in early 2022 when interest rates spiked, ending the ZIRP (zero-interest-rate) streaming bubble where studios incinerated tens of billions chasing Netflix.
WBD wasn't saddled with $40B+ in debt by union wages—that debt was engineered by AT&T's corporate spin-off. Blaming middle-class crew for C-suite balance-sheet mismanagement is absurd.
Comparing Los Angeles to Detroit ignores agglomeration economics.
Auto manufacturing uses discrete assembly lines easily relocated to non-union states.
Film/TV relies on an interconnected industrial cluster: soundstages, prop houses, grip/electric hubs, specialized legal firms, VFX pipelines, and top-tier talent. Production shoots travel for tax rebates, but IP generation, development, and post-production remain heavily rooted in Southern California.
California hasn't offered "only lip service" on tax incentives.
California continuously expands its Film and Television Tax Credit program, with annual allocations reaching $420M.
The state also passed targeted legislation (like AB 2319) specifically creating tax credits for visual effects, editing, and post-production to keep skilled technical labor local.
The video's debt logic contradicts itself.
You cannot argue debt is harmless during inflation, then complain studios are drowning in debt, and simultaneously cheer an $111B debt-financed merger.
Furthermore, "Hollywood accounting" (net-profit back-end games) has nothing to do with public SEC balance sheets. Public studios report under GAAP; concealing billions in debt isn't "creative accounting"—it's securities fraud.
Framing complex antitrust litigation and macroeconomic rate shocks as a simplistic culture-war fable generates views, but it severely misinforms the audience.
Paramount didn't "flee California." They used an M&A negotiating bluff, got checked by regulators, and signed legally

text:
The September 22, 1906 Atlanta Race Massacre: How the Democrat Party's Fear-mongering and Fake News Led to Violence and the Death of Many African Americans.

It's just a case of history repeating. Democrats have been fear mongering and printing fake news for nearly 200 years, driven by envy and hate.

As African Americans achieved economic success in Atlanta in the early 1900s, the city simmered with racial strife that was further inflamed by the Democrat Party's yellow journalism.

In the center of downtown Atlanta, a handful of streets intersect, forming what locals know as Five Points. Today, a park, a university, high-rise buildings and throngs of motorists and pedestrians make this a bustling area, belying its history of bloodshed. In 1906, Five Points became the epicenter of the Democrat's Atlanta Race Massacre that claimed the lives of at least 25 African Americans and two white residents.

The four days of white supremacist violence that began on September 22 were spurred on by a number of factors, including yellow journalism, rape accusations and a resentment of African Americans enjoying greater access to voting rights and economic opportunity.

Atlanta Offers Opportunity During Reconstruction
During Reconstruction, many African Americans moved to Atlanta from rural areas to pursue job prospects. An industrial, financial and railroad center, Atlanta was widely viewed as the capital of the New South, but the city was also rife with race and class conflicts.

The 1906 gubernatorial race only heightened these tensions. The race featured a neck-and-neck race between Democrat white supremacist Clark Howell, the editor of The Atlanta Constitution, and Democrat white supremacist Hoke Smith, the former editor of The Atlanta Journal. Democratic candidates, both men attempted to win voter support by emphasizing their plans to disenfranchise Black men.

“They were very clear,” says Clarissa Myrick-Harris, an Africana Studies professor and Division of Humanities chair at Morehouse College. “We can't have Negro rule. We have to stop them. We have to keep them from voting. They’re getting too uppity. They're taking over.”

In addition to voting rights, many Democrat white supremacist residents wanted to shut down bars on Decatur Street, one of the thoroughfares that made up Five Points. They argued that these establishments attracted African American criminals. More than crime, however, critics objected to interracial socializing between Black men and white women in the saloons. Others resented the success of Black-owned businesses that were propelling African Americans into Atlanta’s middle and upper classes.

“​​What's remarkable about this period is that in spite of all those things done to suppress, repress, discriminate against, terrorize, massacre, kill and destroy Black people in Black communities, Black people not only survived but in many cases also thrived,” says Myrick-Harris, who co-curated an exhibit about the Atlanta Race Riot to commemorate its 2006 centennial.

“In 1906, many of the Black businesses were located in the Peachtree Street area in downtown Atlanta. They were competitors with white business owners, and they [the white entrepreneurs] didn’t like that.”

Newspapers Print Sensationalistic Stories
The local press capitalized on Atlanta’s growing racial strife with sensationalistic articles. By the end of summer, a series of articles began rolling out—including in newspapers affiliated with the dueling gubernatorial candidates—featuring white supremacist groups and lynchings, as well as alleged sexual assaults of white women by African American men.

“In a couple of cases, the white women said, ‘No, that’s not true. That didn’t happen to me,’” Myrick-Harris says. “But that didn't matter. You had the Atlanta Georgian newspaper publish a three-part series of editorials on the reign of terror for seven women. Seven white women became a pawn in the plan of essentially destroying the Black community and Black men, most notably. There was a fear of Black rule.”

By the evening of September 22, 1906, armed white mobs numbering in the thousands descended upon Five Points and terrorized any Black men, women and children they encountered on streets or in street cars. The mob destroyed Black-owned businesses and homes and targeted the historically Black colleges and universities in the area. A barbershop owned by Alonzo Herndon, one of the nation’s first African American millionaires, was vandalized, Myrick-Harris says.

After days of violence, the state militia quashed the riot, arresting roughly 250 African Americans. No arrests were reported among the thousands of white Atlantans who had beaten, and even killed Black residents. Allison Bantimba, liaison for the Fulton County Remembrance Coalition, says many Black Atlantans were arrested simply for arming themselves to protect their families and neighborhoods. The coalition has learned the names of 14 people killed during the Atlanta Race Riot and aims to identify the other 11, though Bantimba estimates that up to 100 African Americans were killed during the massacre rather than the reported figure of 25.

Myrick-Harris says that the individuals responsible for the violence defy stereotypes. “They were not all so-called lower class, working class, illiterate white people who were in this mob,” she says. “These were the upstanding white citizens of the city. They ran the gamut from lower class, working class, middle class, upper class, law enforcement, lawyers, doctors. They were all a part of this raging mob.”

News reports of the massacre spread throughout the United States and Europe, but much of the coverage was inaccurate because Atlanta officials minimized the degree of death and destruction that occurred to spare the city’s reputation and protect its business interests.

“The newspapers were reporting things like ‘All is quiet now in the city. The violence is over. The city is herself again,’” Bantimba says. “So it was very much like this was a kind of a blip in Atlanta history and not who Atlanta is or what Atlanta is.”

After Massacre, Groups Work to Prevent Future Violence

To prevent another race riot from taking place, prominent figures in Atlanta’s Black and white communities met regularly to discuss the circumstances that led up to the violence. The Atlanta Evening News, notorious for its yellow journalism that escalated the city’s racial tensions, stopped publishing. And city leaders dropped by Black churches to reassure members that safeguards would be instituted to stop future episodes of mob violence.

The activism that took place after the massacre paved the way for the civil rights movement of the mid-20th century. Just age 13 when the Atlanta Race Massacre broke out, Walter White witnessed a white mob kill a Black child. The memory never left him and contributed to his decision to pursue civil rights as a career. He eventually served as head of the NAACP, which formed in 1909.

The massacre also made an impression on Black scholar and activist W.E.B. DuBois, who wrote about it in his essay “A Litany of Atlanta.”

“Atlanta became this incubator, more broadly, for national leadership, for the establishment of national organizations and institutions that would have a national impact in the wake of that 1906 Atlanta Race Riot,” Myrick-Harris says.

Despite this horrific episode of violence, Black Atlantans regrouped and rebounded as best they could. Atlanta's Sweet Auburn Avenue neighborhood continued to develop and flourish, so by the mid-1950s, it was labeled 'the richest Negro street in the world' by Fortune magazine. As Myrick-Harris says, “They rebuilt their businesses. They rebuilt their homes.”

text:
New Era must back its Texas data-center power deal with a $116 million letter of credit within 15 business days of signing. The terms disclosed on 21st September 2026 also promise Vistra a 5% stake in the portion of the project it will power.

Electricity is expected in the third quarter of 2027. The obligation to arrange financial backing starts much sooner!

New Era Energy & Digital signed the agreement on 18 September through a subsidiary. Luminant, a Vistra affiliate, agreed to supply between 200 and 207 megawatts to the Texas Critical Data Center near Odessa. The initial 20-year contract begins when power delivery starts.

For a reader assessing the project, the financing terms matter alongside the announced megawatts. Securing electricity can make a proposed campus more attractive to tenants and lenders. It also creates obligations that the developer must meet before the expected delivery date.

A bank-issued letter of credit gives the supplier a claim against the issuing bank if a demand meets the instrument's terms. The supplier gains payment protection without having to rely entirely on the developer's promise to pay.

The developer may need collateral or a credit facility to arrange that protection. The $116 million face amount does not tell us how much cash New Era must tie up, what fees it will pay or whether the support has already been obtained. Treating the whole amount as money already spent would be wrong.

By delivery, New Era must provide additional acceptable security of up to $82.8 million, in a form agreed by the parties. The filing also links the initial support to construction costs. It can be drawn for unpaid first-phase invoices if the parties also fail to execute the purchase agreement on time. Both conditions matter.

Vistra is due to receive the equity after power begins. The promised interest is nonvoting and represents 5% of the defined project company's fully diluted equity. It concerns the relevant powered portion of the development, rather than 5% of New Era's listed parent.

That gives the supplier two different financial interests. Credit support protects payment under the agreement. Project ownership offers participation in future value, with the risks that equity ownership carries.

The arrangement could help the development proceed. A protected supplier and a developer with contracted power can both benefit. This filing does not establish that the deal is unaffordable or that financing will fail.

Supply remains conditional. New Era identifies obtaining and maintaining credit support as a risk and says the full agreements will accompany its September-quarter report.

Evidence that the required support has been posted would confirm one milestone. It would still leave the separate questions of construction funding, tenants and operating cash flow.

Officials said Rodeo Saltillo will offer much more than rodeo competition. Activities will be held at the new Expo Coahuila facilities.

Speakers emphasized the close cultural connection shared by communities on both sides of the Rio Grande. They noted that the region shares a love for horses, ranching, boots, hats, northern music, carne asada, and family traditions.

Coahuila representatives also highlighted security and tourism as important priorities, saying they are prepared to welcome visitors from Texas and beyond. text:
Two @Tesla nights, seven years apart. Each one brought a headliner and a surprise, and each time the headliner was first to earn a dollar.
​
Nov. 16, 2017: the Semi rolled out, and then the second-generation Roadster drove out of the back of its trailer.
​
The Semi delivered to its first customer in December 2022. The Roadster finally has a reveal date, Oct. 1 in Waco, nearly nine years later, and reservations for it are open again.
​
Oct. 10, 2024: the Cybercab, and then the Robovan. Up to 20 riders or a cargo load, no steering wheel, no pedals.
​
The Cybercab started taking paying riders in Austin this month. The Robovan's latest appearance was a render gliding along an elevated roadway in the Terafab video @elonmusk posted in August.
​
Musk has told us where it sits. At last year's shareholder meeting he agreed that the Robovan is the wheelchair-accessible vehicle he had hinted at, and he slotted it behind Cybercab, Optimus and Semi, probably a couple of years out.
​
In July a Tesla senior policy advisor told the D.C. Council that a purpose-built, wheelchair-accessible autonomous vehicle is in active development in Texas.
​
So the question I would put to @elonmusk @larsmoravy @aelluswamy is the one an East Valley owner-operator has to answer on paper: how long from the Robovan's reveal to a Robovan in service?
​
Tesla's history offers a range. Paying riders in under two years for the Cybercab. A first customer in five for the Semi. A reveal date after nearly nine for the Roadster.
​
Nobody outside Tesla knows where the Robovan lands in that range, and I am not going to pretend I do.
​
What I do know is what it means here. Until it ships, the network runs on the Model Y and the two-seat Cybercab, and neither one was designed around a rider who stays in a wheelchair.
​
A fleet plan cannot run on a reveal date. It runs on the vehicles actually in service, and it owes people a plain answer about which riders those vehicles cannot carry yet.
​
Tesla is building the vehicle for that rider. Until it arrives, the gap belongs to whoever runs the fleet, and saying so out loud is part of the job.
​
Commercial autonomous mobility in the Phoenix East Valley will arrive — sooner than most think. For me, it seems like forever...
​

$WBD: On Monday, attorneys general from 12 states reached a settlement with Paramount and Skydance. Terms include oversight of CBS/CNN by an independent news committee, a commitment to release at least 30–32 theatrical films annually for five years, an additional ~$1.5 billion domestic production pledge, and a promise not to sell off studio lots. Regulatory hurdles in the US (DOJ), EU, and UK have already been cleared. Ellison has indicated internally that clearances are complete and the deal is expected to close in about two weeks. $WBD closed Monday at $30.80 (+10.8%) on massive volume of 230 million shares; the cash offer price is ~$31, meaning the spread has narrowed significantly. $PSKY closed at $9.91; it spiked to $11.49 intraday before pulling back and is trading around $10.13 pre-market. Since buyers pay a premium and sellers gain certainty, the price action was never going to be symmetrical.

The real pressure comes not from the litigation itself, but from the "ticking fee" of approximately $7 million per day that kicks in after September 30. The deadline for the bond exchange has been extended to October 2. Time favors the bulls: the settlement buys speed and public goodwill, rather than downsizing the merger. A failed deal would trigger a completely different scenario—Warner’s library would become even more exclusive, asset sales would increase market supply, and only then would a major library like  LION (one of the last remaining large libraries available for acquisition) see renewed bidding interest. The primary narrative remains deal completion, not a breakup.

For  WBD today, a reasonable range is $29.5–32.0; it is likely to oscillate near the offer price between $30.5 and $31.5, as any spikes are prone to profit-taking by arbitrageurs. For PSKY, the range is $9.7–10.8; financing, debt, and integration costs will weigh on valuation—don't expect it to mirror Warner's gains. In the short term (through early October), assuming the "two-week closing" timeline holds, WBD should gravitate toward $31, while PSKY will likely see event-driven volatility in the $10–11 range. The bond-related hearing on September 24 remains "noise" rather than a decisive factor. For this deal—valued at $81 billion in equity and approximately $110 billion including debt—the primary risk has shifted from "will the state government block it?" to "closing execution and debt integration." Holding WBD is a bet on deal certainty rather than a growth narrative; chasing PSKY is a bet on a highly leveraged post-merger media empire, which leaves far less margin for error.

text:
Whats is BAPS?
Bochasanwasi Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha (BAPS) is a sub-sect of the Swaminarayan Sampradaya. 

What do they believe?
They consider Gunatitanand Swami is considered the personal incarnation of Aksharbrahman (the eternal divine abode and ideal devotee of God) and the first spiritual successor of Bhagwan Swaminarayan. However this only a attempt to create a god figure in the living world where the devotees should consider the sadhu's or guru's who they follow as Aksharbrahman as a successor to Bhagwan Swaminarayan.

Why is this a problem?
The followers of Swaminarayan sect rejects this particular aspect of the BAPS narrative of Gunatitanand Swami as Aksharbrahman. The Swaminarayan sect is a rather young sect which emerged during the life span of Bhagwan Swaminarayan in the early 19th century. The entire account of his life's work has been recorded in various literatures and scriptures. One of them has legal connotations regarding succession, legacy and heritage. This is called "Desh Vibhag Lekh." This is the foundational legal and administrative constitution of the original Swaminarayan Sampradaya.
The Desh Vibhag Lekh explicitly mandates that: Leadership of the Sampradaya is strictly hereditary, passed down through the bloodline of these two householder families. Only the Acharyas have the exclusive authority to initiate new monks (sadhus) and householder disciples, and to install deities (murti pratishtha) in major temples. The Acharyas are the ultimate spiritual and administrative heads (not successors) of their respective dioceses. 
The Desh Vibhag Lekh is the primary reason why non-BAPS traditions reject the idea of Gunatitanand Swami being a "spiritual successor" or "Aksharbrahman" Because Junagadh Mandir falls geographically into the Southern Diocese, Gunatitanand Swami operated under the direct authority of Acharya Raghuvirji Maharaj of Vadtal. This would essentially displace the authority of the Acharya Parampara as the heads of sampradaya by way of creating "next to God" position for Gunatitanand swami which is above the Acharya and then by way of succession every other Swami who succeeded him upto current "Pramukh swami" who they wish to offer the same position as "Aksharbrahman".

Is this a Problem for Sanatan Dharma?
No. It is an debate within the Swaminarayan Sampradaya and it has no relation with the larger Sanatan fold.

What is creating his misconception?
The temple lay-outs are generally give a such a misleading perception as the temples are made differently as compared to other hindu temples.
Throughout his life, Sahajanand Swami (Bhagwan Swaminarayan) actively demonstrated reverence for traditional Vedic deities to preserve the fabric of Sanatan Dharma by installing Traditional Idols. 
In the historic temples he personally constructed (like Ahmedabad, Vadtal, and Bhuj), he installed primary Vedic deities alongside his own manifestations. For example, he installed Nara-Narayan Dev, Laxmi-Narayan Dev, and Radha-Krishna Dev on the central altars, and set up shrines for Shivalingas and Ganesh. Celebrating Vedic Festivals: He strictly observed and organized massive celebrations for standard Hindu holy days, including Maha Shivratri, Janmashtami, Rama Navami, and Ganesh Chaturthi. 

Scriptural Validation: He adopted the Srimad Bhagavatam and the Bhagavad Gita as core scriptures for his fellowship, both of which center heavily on the Lilas of Vishnu, Krishna, and Vedic traditions.
In his authoritative code of conduct, the Shikshapatri, Bhagwan Swaminarayan laid down absolute, legally binding commands regarding how his followers must treat Vedic deities. For example in Shikshpatri (code of conduct) he mandates that "No one shall ever disrespect or speak ill of deities like Shiva, Vishnu, Brahma, Surya, Devi (Durga), or the Brahmins." (Shikshapatri, Verse 21) Speaking ill of other Hindu deities is considered a severe spiritual transgression (aparadh) within the sect". Then,  "When passing by temples of Shiva or other deities, one shall bow to them and offer reverence." (Shikshapatri, Verse 23) Followers traveling or living in places without a Swaminarayan temple are expected to visit traditional Hindu temples with equal humility.

Then how should a Sanatani interpret the Sawaminaryan Bhagwan and the beliefs of the sampradaya?
In summary the Swaminarayn devotees see - Bhagwan Swaminarayan as the ultimate source of liberation, while the Vedic gods are the esteemed Governors of the realms. They do not compete with each other. They rule the universe with Coexistence of Supremacy and profound mutual respect. In the Vachanamrut, Bhagwan Swaminarayan Bhagwan defines the title of Sarvopari with an explanation of his coherence and oneness with previous avatars. He explains this relationship through structural concepts that "prevent" his followers from viewing previous incarnations as "competing" or completely disconnected deities. He explains through anologies that the divine entity acting through Rama, Krishna, or Narasimha is the exact same ultimate consciousness (Parabrahman) that is fully manifests in him. To solidify this coherence practically for his followers, Bhagwan Swaminarayan heavily discouraged treating different avatars as rivals or separate competing forces. In the Vachanamrut, he commands his followers to view the divine forms of past avatars as spiritually flawless, fully divine, and unified in essence. This is why, when establishing his first major temples, he did not place statues of himself on the altars; instead, he installed Nara-Narayana Dev (in Ahmedabad) and Radha-Krishna Dev (in Vadtal). For his devotees, serving these traditional forms with a pure mind is structurally coherent with serving Bhagwan Swaminarayan himself, as they are all different expressions of the same primordial, divine source.

Specific Acts of Devotion and Mandates from Swaminaryan Bhagwan himself:
The Worship of Five Deities (Panchayatana Puja): He established that the five primary deities of orthodox Hinduism—Vishnu, Shiva, Ganpati, Surya (the Sun God), and Parvati (Devi)—must be worshipped with deep respect as manifestations of divine power. The Role of Hanuman and Ganesh: Every Swaminarayan temple features prominent shrines for Hanuman and Ganesh at the entrance. Devotees are mandated to offer prayers to Ganesh at the start of any new venture to remove obstacles, and to worship Hanuman (especially on Saturdays) for protection against evil spirits and mental weaknesses.

About the Video:
1. The video accurately points that BAPS has elevated the Guru's position much higher then what usually the Sanatan Dharma is used to seeing. However the larger section of the Swaminarayan sampradaya pushes back on the this narrative internally. 
2. The post juxtaposes a question or a concern of the core philosophy of Swaminarayan Sampradaya with respect to its alignment within the Sanatan Dharma. I have tried to answer that in the post above.
3. I think that the Swaminarayan Sampradaya as a whole should not be viewed through the ritualistic and philosophical lense of what BAPS as a subsect believes. BAPS is not an authority when it comes to the core principles and the beliefs of the Sapradaya as a whole.
4. Most importantly the "internal debate with the BAPS narrative" should not be seen as threat, opposition, dilution or deviation from the Sanatan Dharma OR a view of the entire Swaminarayan Sampradaya.

text:
While pseudepigraphal and Second Temple writings carry zero binding, canonical authority for establishing divine doctrine, they are not without utility. For a Berean truth seeker, ancient historical and ethical texts—when strictly subordinated to the filter of canonical Scripture—can serve as valuable case studies in human wisdom, moral discernment, and cultural context.

Paul himself modeled this balance. In Acts 17:28, he quoted the pagan Greek poets Aratus and Epimenides (“For in him we live, and move, and have our being”), and in Titus 1:12, he cited Epimenides again. Paul did not treat those writers as inspired Scripture; he used their observations as illustrative cultural tools to expose hypocrisy and point men toward the Living God.

When examined through the unyielding grid of canonical truth, The Testament of Asher yields three sharp, timeless lessons on human nature and spiritual duplicity.

1. The Anatomy of Double-Mindedness (Dipsychia)
The central theme of Asher’s extracanonical discourse is the condemnation of the "two-faced" man (diprosopos)—the person who attempts to serve God while harboring compromise.

The writer astutely observes that evil rarely presents itself as unvarnished villainy; it almost always dresses in the clothing of moral justification. The text warns against:

Doing a wicked deed to accomplish a perceived "good" end.

Fasting and performing religious rites while exploiting the poor.

Showing mercy to an unrepentant criminal while despising the righteous victim.

This historical ethical observation closely mirrors the canonical warning of James 1:8: “A double minded man is unstable in all his ways,” and James 4:8: “Purify your hearts, ye double minded.”

The Lesson: The human heart possesses an almost infinite capacity for self-deception, inventing righteous rationalizations for unholy compromises. A divided allegiance is not partial faithfulness; it is total compromise.

2. The Fallacy of "The Ends Justify the Means"
In The Testament of Asher, the writer explicitly condemns those who steal or extort under the premise that they will use the proceeds to give alms to the poor. The text declares that God rejects any sacrifice bought with the currency of deceit.

This provides a powerful moral lesson that directly reinforces canonical law:

Proverbs 21:27: “The sacrifice of the wicked is abomination: how much more, when he bringeth it with a wicked mind?”

1 Samuel 15:22: Samuel’s rebuke to King Saul, who spared the best of the Amalekite livestock under the pious excuse of sacrificing them to Yahweh: “Hath the Lord as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the Lord? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice.”

The Lesson: God never honors a holy goal achieved through unholy methods. A truth seeker cannot cut ethical corners, tell "useful" lies, or adopt worldly tactics in order to advance God's Kingdom.

3. Contextualizing Second Temple Messianic Expectation
Reading Second Temple literature like the Testaments shows how devout Jews in the centuries leading up to the advent of Christ were wrestling with their own history.

They looked back at the historical failures of their ancestors—such as the northern tribe of Asher compromising with the Canaanites and choosing maritime ease over holy warfare—and tried to construct strict ethical fences to prevent their nation from sliding back into pagan assimilation.

Yet, these texts also reveal the tragic limitation of mere human legalism:

The authors of the Second Temple period understood that man was torn between two inclinations (yetzer ha-tov and yetzer ha-ra).

They correctly diagnosed the problem of moral duplicity.

However, they lacked the power of the New Covenant. They could describe the danger of being "two-faced," but moral exhortation alone cannot regenerate a dead heart.

This highlights why the arrival of Jesus Christ was so vital. Moral codes, ethical treatises, and pseudepigraphal wills can diagnose the disease of double-mindedness, but only the shed blood of Christ and the indwelling Holy Spirit can excise the heart of stone and replace it with a single-hearted love for God (Ezekiel 36:26–27; Jeremiah 31:33).

The Proper Posture of the Truth Seeker
Extra-biblical literature is like an ancient mirror:

It can accurately reflect the moral dilemmas, historical anxieties, and theological struggles of ancient men.

It can offer sharp, common-sense observations on the deceitfulness of sin.

The strict dividing line must always be maintained: Canonical Scripture is the infallible compass; extra-biblical literature is merely a footprint in the sand. We do not base our doctrine on the footprint, but studying where past generations walked can sharpen our awareness as we navigate the narrow path of Truth today.

1.
$SPCX
(Space Exploration Technologies / SpaceX) 

 Business: Three segments — Space (reusable rockets/launches), Connectivity (Starlink), AI (xAI/Grok + compute infrastructure). IPO’d June 2026. Market cap ~$2.06T. 

 Revenue: TTM ~$23.0B (+122% YoY). Q2 2026: $7.8B (+92% YoY) — Connectivity $4.3B, AI $2.6B (+247%), Space $0.96B. 

 Gross Profit / Net Income: TTM gross margin ~52%. Q2 gross profit ~$4.3B. Still net loss (TTM ~–$8.9B; Q2 –$541M) due to heavy AI CapEx and R&D. Adjusted EBITDA strong (Q2 ~$3.5B).

Outlook: Starlink subscriber + enterprise/government growth continues. New multi-year AI compute deals accelerating. Heavy CapEx (AI alone >$23B in H1) pressures near-term profits, but vertical integration (rockets + satellites + AI) creates a long-term moat. Analyst PT mid-point ~$222 (+46%). Risks: valuation, execution, regulation.  

2. $CRDO(Credo Technology)  

Business: High-speed copper & optical interconnects for AI data centers (AECs, DSPs, ZeroFlap optics, silicon photonics). Serves hyperscalers. 

Revenue: FY2026 (ended May 2026) $1.34B (+206% YoY). Q4 $437M (+157% YoY). Q1 FY2027 ~$479M. 

Gross Profit / Net Income: Gross margin consistently 67–68%. Non-GAAP net income FY2026 ~$662M (5x+ growth), net margins ~50%. Strong FCF and ~$1.4B cash. 
Outlook: Optical ramp expected to exceed $600M. FY2027 guidance implies another ~80% growth. High-quality, self-funding growth with expanding product suite. Valuation has compressed; PEG looks attractive. Risks: customer concentration, sequential growth moderation.  

3. $NBIS (Nebius Group) 

 Business: Full-stack AI cloud (GPU clusters + platform). Former Yandex spin-out; also owns Avride and TripleTen. 

 Revenue: TTM ~$1.36B (+500%+). Q2 2026 $582M (+454% YoY), almost entirely AI cloud. 

 Gross Profit / Net Income: Gross margin 74–77%. Q2 Adj. EBITDA $236M (41% margin). GAAP still volatile (Q2 net loss ~$190M) due to interest and non-cash items.

  Outlook: Large multi-year contracts (Microsoft, Meta, etc.), NVIDIA investment, 2026 ARR target $7–9B, full-year revenue $3.0–3.4B. Aggressive CapEx ($20–25B) to scale power capacity to multi-GW. Risks: high leverage/interest expense, execution, competition.  

4. $IREN(IREN Limited)  

Business: Vertically integrated AI cloud data centers + Bitcoin mining, rapidly pivoting to AI. 100% renewable power; >5 GW pipeline. 

 Revenue: FY2026 (ended June 2026) $707M (+41%). AI Cloud $129M (8x growth), Bitcoin mining $578M.  

Gross Profit / Net Income: Gross margin ~69%. Adj. EBITDA ~$246M. Net loss ~$703M (mainly non-cash impairments of $639M). Operating ARR already ~$1B; contracted ARR ~$4B for 2026 capacity. 

 Outlook: Microsoft and other large contracts; major GPU orders. 2026 capacity largely sold out; 2027 discussions ongoing. Risks: impairments, Bitcoin price exposure, high CapEx and debt. 

5. $CRWV (CoreWeave)  

Business: Purpose-built AI cloud platform (GPU clusters + software stack) for AI labs and enterprises.

Revenue: TTM ~$7.59B. Q2 2026 $2.58B (+112% YoY). Revenue backlog ~$104B. 

Gross Profit / Net Income: Q2 gross profit ~$1.70B (gross margin ~66%). Adj. EBITDA $1.51B (59% margin). Still net loss (Q2 –$626M) driven by interest and depreciation. 

Outlook: Explosive demand and massive backlog support multi-year growth. Operating leverage should improve with scale. Risks: high leverage, interest expense, intensifying competition.

Overall Future Trajectory

All five sit at the center of the AI compute, networking, and power build-out.

$SPCX  has the broadest long-term optionality via vertical integration.

$CRDO  offers the cleanest profitability and highest-quality growth.

$NBIS $CRWV, and  $IREN  are high-growth “neo-cloud” plays — capital-intensive with near-term losses but rapid revenue scaling.  

Secular drivers (hyperscaler CapEx, GPU scarcity, power constraints) remain intact into 2027–2028. Near-term volatility will be high due to valuation, interest rates, and execution risk. Medium-term upside looks substantial as scale improves margins.

 Not investment advice. Data from latest public filings. Markets move fast — always do your own due diligence.

ROBOTAXI
Updated 2026-09-22

NEW TODAY
- Testers (Sep 22 CernBasher): another +28 vehicles today — 19 Model Y + 9 Cybercab (tester fleet-add / tracking signal, not Official).
- Folder totals: Robotaxi 233 (+1) + Fleet 4 (0 new) → 237 unique

WHAT IT IS
- Tesla’s paid autonomous ride service. You book a car in the Robotaxi app. The car drives. There is no human driver on unsupervised rides.
- Live cars today are mostly Model Y. The purpose-built Cybercab is the volume vehicle testers say Tesla is prioritizing.
- Camera-only vision. Tesla VP of AI Ashok Elluswamy: no lidar, radar, or HD maps required for safe operation on this stack.
- This how-to merges the public Robotaxi service folder with Owning Robotaxi Fleet (owner / private-fleet economics). Not Cybercab-only bookmarks.

HOW IT WORKS
- Download the Tesla Robotaxi app and join the waitlist. Official robotaxi (Sep 2025): app is available to all; access expands over time.
- Book the ride in Tesla’s app. Elon: Tesla will not partner with Uber or Lyft. “We will have enough demand.”
- Unsupervised means no safety driver. Supervised cities still have a person in the car.
- Official robotaxi (Aug 27): service hours are 6am to 10pm, 7 days/week. Unsupervised fleet is a lot bigger. Upgraded vehicle distribution and routing so you wait less.
- Testers: you can change destination and keep the same trip for multiple stops.
- Cars return to a depot or homebase and park themselves (Houston footage).
- Ashok: FSD v15 is already running on Model Y robotaxis and will run on Cybercab.
- Testers: Tesla is limiting Model Y conversions to prioritize Cybercab, built with an unboxed modular process.
- Testers (Aug 24): Tesla expects Cybercab to replace Model Ys in the Robotaxi fleet over time and become the highest-volume vehicle there. Testers flag Sept 3 / 9/3 as the Cybercab strategy moment. Austin public Cybercab rides described as “imminent.”
- Testers (Sep 7): Cybercab expected to be actively deployed across Tesla’s Robotaxi fleet soon; Austin Cybercab wait times described as going parabolic on demand.
- Testers (Sep 7): Tesla hiring Robotaxi Fleet Support Supervisors night shift across 21 cities (Cybercabs incoming signal).
- Testers (Sep 7): Waymo Q3 2025 occupancy — 90% of trips have 2 or fewer people (two-seater Cybercab justification resurfaced).
