text:
🎥 #هنر_معامله‌گری_ترامپ: #بلعیدن_ونزوئلا، #گرینلند و #ایران توسط #آمریکا؛ #بلعیدن_خاورمیانه توسط #اسرائیل👇👇

👈 اکبر گنجی، ۲۲ سپتامبر ۲۰۲۶

✅ #ایرانی‌ها چهارچشمی مراقب #ترامپِ_نفت‌دزد_و_سرزمین‌دزد باشند تا با #رشوه_قدرت_و_ثروت خودفروشانِ #اسماً_ایرانی را نخرد و نفت ایران یا بخشی از سرزمین‌های ایران (مانند #ونزوئلا و #گرینلند) را از آنِ خود نکند.

✅ یک خانهٔ ۸۰۰ هزار دلاری به #شوهر_وزیر_خارجهٔ_گرینلند داد و آنجا را تصاحب کرد.

✅ ترامپ بارها و بارها به صراحت گفته است که نفت ونزوئلا را از آنِ آمریکا کرده و همین کار را با ایران هم می‌خواهد بکند.
۱۶ دسامبر ۲۰۲۵ در تروث‌سوشال نوشت ونزوئلا باید «همهٔ نفت و زمین و دارایی‌هایی را که قبلاً از ما دزدیده» فوراً به آمریکا برگرداند.
۱۷ دسامبر ۲۰۲۵ به خبرنگاران گفت: «همهٔ حقوق انرژی ما را گرفتند. همهٔ نفت ما را گرفتند، همین چندی پیش. و ما آن را پس می‌خواهیم. غیرقانونی گرفتند.»
۳ ژانویهٔ ۲۰۲۶، پس از عملیات نظامی و بازداشت مادورو، گفت آمریکا ونزوئلا را «اداره» خواهد کرد و «ثروت عظیمی از زمین بیرون خواهیم کشید.»
۲۴ ژانویهٔ ۲۰۲۶ به نیویورک‌پست گفت: «بگذارید این‌طور بگویم، آن‌ها نفتی ندارند. ما نفت را می‌گیریم.» نفت را به پالایشگاه‌های هیوستون می‌فرستاد.
ژوئن ۲۰۲۶ در تروث‌سوشال نوشت به‌زودی جزیرهٔ خارگ و دیگر نقاط نفتی ایران را می‌گیرد و بازار نفت و گازشان را «درست مثل ونزوئلا» کاملاً در کنترل می‌گیرد.
۱۳ سپتامبر ۲۰۲۶ در ایرلند گفت آمریکا نهایتاً از ایران بیرون می‌آید، «مگر اینکه تصمیم بگیریم بمانیم و نفت را نگه داریم، مثل ونزوئلا.»
۹ ژانویهٔ ۲۰۲۶ دربارهٔ گرینلند گفت: «کاری در گرینلند می‌کنم، چه خوششان بیاید چه نیاید... دوست دارم معامله را از راه آسان انجام دهیم، اما اگر از راه آسان نشود، از راه سخت انجام می‌دهیم.»

✅ ترامپ در مورد ایران به دنبال تکرار مدل عراق و ونزوئلاست: کنترل درآمدهای ارزی و دولتی تابع. بارها گفته می‌خواهد مدل ونزوئلا را در ایران پیاده کند.
از ۲۰۰۳ درآمد نفت عراق در حساب بانک مرکزی عراق نزد فدرال‌رزرو نیویورک می‌نشیند و هر رئیس‌جمهور آمریکا فرمان اجرایی ۱۳۳۰۳ را تمدید کرده؛ ترامپ هم ۴ مه ۲۰۲۶ آن را تمدید کرد. رویترز ۲۳ ژانویهٔ ۲۰۲۶ نوشت واشنگتن تهدید کرد اگر نیروهای نزدیک به ایران در دولت جدید باشند، حتی درآمد نفت عراق را هدف می‌گیرد. نیویورک‌تایمز نوشت دولت ترامپ موقتاً انتقال دلارهای خودِ عراق از بانک‌های آمریکا به بغداد را هم بست.
پس از انتخابات نوامبر ۲۰۲۵ عراق، اکثریت شیعه نوری مالکی را نامزد نخست‌وزیری کرد. ترامپ ۲۷ ژانویهٔ ۲۰۲۶ در تروث‌سوشال نوشت اگر مالکی انتخاب شود «آمریکا دیگر به عراق کمک نخواهد کرد» و بدون کمک آمریکا عراق «صفر شانس» دارد. مالکی دخالت آمریکا را رد کرد، اما نامزدی‌اش کنار رفت و با فشار واشنگتن علی الزیدی نخست‌وزیر شد؛ ترامپ مه ۲۰۲۶ گفت «خیلی قوی حمایت می‌کنیم» و ژوئیه او را در کاخ سفید پذیرفت.
در ونزوئلا هم درآمد نفت تحت ترتیبات آمریکاست. رویترز و فایننشال‌تایمز ۱۸ سپتامبر ۲۰۲۶ نوشتند دولت موقت و بخشی از مخالفان نزدیک‌اند حدود ۳۱ تُن طلای ونزوئلا — نزدیک ۴ میلیارد دلار — را از بانک انگلستان به فدرال‌رزرو نیویورک ببرند و دسترسی را آمریکا کنترل کند. زمین‌لرزهٔ دوگانهٔ ۲۴ ژوئن ۲۰۲۶ بیش از ۱۷۰۰ کشتهٔ رسمی داشت و در برخی گزارش‌ها شمار قربانیان بالاتر رفته است. طلا را به نام بازسازی پس از زلزله می‌خواهند آزاد کنند، اما خرج کردنش با نظارت آمریکا و حساب خزانه‌داری است؛ بدون مجوز واشنگتن — و عملاً بدون مارکو روبیو — کاراکاس دستش به ذخایر خودش باز نیست.

✅ بسیاری از رهبران جمهوری‌خواه همین سخنانِ ترامپ در مورد ونزوئلا و گرینلند و ایران را عیناً تکرار کرده‌اند.

✅ در آخرین مورد، کارلا سندز، سفیر سابق آمریکا در دانمارک، به فاکس‌نیوز گفت: «ما ونزوئلا را داریم، ایران را هم خواهیم داشت، و حالا اگر گرینلند را هم داشته باشیم، می‌توانیم با انرژی‌ای که کشف شده، برای صدها سال آینده — و منظورم واقعاً صدها سال است — انرژی مورد نیاز جهان را تأمین کنیم.»

✅ پنج دقیقه افشاگری راشل مدو (@maddow)، تحلیلگر سیاسی برجستهٔ لیبرال آمریکایی، را حتماً ببینید. آدمی را به یاد بدترین دوران استعمار و امپریالیسم می‌اندازد. با این تفاوت که این امپریالیسم عریان را دیگر نمی‌توان «تئوری توطئه» خواند. بسیاری از سیاستمداران آمریکایی همین را گفته‌اند؛ از جمله مایکل مک‌فاول (@McFaul)، سفیر آمریکا در روسیه در دولت اوباما. او ۲۹ اوت ۲۰۲۶ نوشت ترامپ آمریکا را به قرن نوزدهم برگردانده و «مثل یک امپراتوری امپریالیستی معمول آن قرن» رفتار می‌کند و معاملهٔ نفتی ونزوئلا «امپریالیسم عریان است؛ با نیروی نظامی دارایی کشوری در جنوب را می‌گیرند.» ۳ سپتامبر ۲۰۲۶ هم در پاسخ به کاخ سفید نوشت: «اسم این امپریالیسم است. ما از کاربرد زور در کشور دیگر سود می‌بریم.»

✅ گفت‌وگوی سه روز پیش بیل کریستول (@BillKristol) با رابرت کیگان از همه مهم‌تر است. کیگان از نظریه‌پردازان برجستهٔ نئوکان‌ها برای جنگ‌های خاورمیانه، از نویسندگان بیانیه‌های پروژهٔ قرن جدید آمریکایی و از مدافعان مداخلهٔ نظامی پس از جنگ سرد است. همسرش ویکتوریا جین نولند هم از صهیونیست‌های «اول اسرائیل» و به‌شدت جنگ‌طلب است. مناظرهٔ چهارنفرهٔ ۲۰ مه ۲۰۲۶ (۳۰ اردیبهشت ۱۴۰۵) در تالار مریدین تورنتو — جان مرشایمر و استفان والت در برابر ویکتوریا جین نولند و مایک پامپئو، مناظرهٔ مانک با عنوان «به دنبال هیولا نروید» — تاریخی و فراموش‌نشدنی است: https://t.co/AAI3Ns9VcV
کیگان در مصاحبه با بیل کریستول دولت ترامپ را غارتگر و امپریالیستی می‌شمارد که با زور عریانِ علنی نفت ونزوئلا و گرینلند را از آنِ آمریکا کرده است. می‌گوید این استعمارگر سیری‌ناپذیر است و هرچه می‌گیرد سیر نمی‌شود و اشتهایی بی‌نظیر برای خوردن مال دیگران دارد. (مصاحبهٔ رابرت کیگان با بیل کریستول را جداگانه پست کرده‌ام.) کریستول هم از نومحافظه‌کاران و از مخالفان جدی ترامپ است؛ ضدمداخله نشده، اما مداخلهٔ ترامپ را غصب نفت و زمین می‌داند نه رهبری نظم جهانی، و تهدید گرینلند و معاملهٔ نفتی ونزوئلا را قلدری امپراتوری‌وار می‌خواند.

✅ می‌توانم نوشته را ادامه دهم و با فیلم و توییت و مناظره نشان دهم آنچه در مورد ایران رخ داده و می‌دهد همان برنامهٔ امپریالیستی را دنبال می‌کند.
🔺 مایک پامپئو (@mikepompeo)، از نئوکان‌های «اول اسرائیل»، ۲ ژانویهٔ ۲۰۲۶ در ایکس نوشت: «سال نو مبارک به هر ایرانی در خیابان. همچنین به هر مأمور موساد که کنارشان راه می‌رود.» جروزالم‌پست و تایمز اسرائیل همان روز نقل کردند. کانال فارسی‌زبان منتسب به موساد چند روز پیش‌تر نوشته بود: «با هم به خیابان بیایید… نه فقط از دور؛ در میدان هم با شماییم.»
🔺 جان بولتون و مایک پنس نیز همین مواضع را داشته‌اند. هر سه با سازمان مجاهدین خلق نشست داشته‌اند. بولتون ژوئیهٔ ۲۰۱۸ در اجتماع مجاهدین در پاریس گفت پیش از ۲۰۱۹ در تهران جشن می‌گیرند.
🔺 نتانیاهو و دیگر رهبران اسرائیل مکرر گفته‌اند بدون تغییر رژیم در ایران کارشان ناقص است. در انتخابات اسرائیل بر سر «تغییر رژیم در ایران» اختلافی میان رقبا نیست. اسرائیل با مجاهدین خلق هم رابطهٔ وثیقی داشته، اما در سطح علنی از رضا پهلوی و بازتولید نظام سلطنتی پهلوی دفاع می‌کند. شهریار آهی — جدی‌ترین مشاور رضا پهلوی در آن زمان — سال ۲۰۰۶ در نیویورک گفت اسرائیل اول انتشار اسناد محرمانهٔ پروژهٔ هسته‌ای ایران را به ما داد تا انجام دهیم؛ وقتی قبول نکردیم، آن‌ها را به سازمان مجاهدین خلق داد تا منتشرشان کنند.
🔺 ترامپ ۵ آوریل ۲۰۲۶ به فاکس‌نیوز گفت آمریکا «اسلحه، خیلی اسلحه» برای معترضان ایرانی فرستاد، از طریق کُردها، و فکر می‌کند کُردها سلاح‌ها را برای خود نگه داشتند. نیویورک‌تایمز ۴ مارس نوشت سیا پیش از جنگ سلاح سبک به نیروهای کُرد ایرانی داده. احزاب کُرد ایرانی دریافت سلاح را تکذیب کردند.
🔺 وال‌استریت ژورنال ۱۲ فوریهٔ ۲۰۲۶ به نقل از مقام‌های آمریکایی نوشت دولت ترامپ پس از سرکوب اعتراضات ژانویه حدود ۶ هزار دستگاه استارلینک را مخفیانه وارد ایران کرد؛ وزارت خارجه نزدیک ۷ هزار دستگاه خریده بود و ترامپ از ارسال خبر داشت.
🔺 سیا ۲۴–۲۵ فوریهٔ ۲۰۲۶ در ایکس، اینستاگرام و یوتیوب به فارسی نوشت: «سازمان اطلاعات مرکزی صدایت را می‌شنود و می‌خواهد کمک کند» و دستور تماس امن برای خبرچین داد. آسوشیتدپرس و رویترز همان روز گزارش کردند. یاسمین و نور و ایمان پهلوی — به روایت مدارک اینستاگرام‌شان — اطلاعیهٔ سیا را هم‌زمان استوری کردند.

✅ عالی‌ترین رخداد دوران کنونی این است که دولت‌های آمریکا و اسرائیل دیگر مقاصدشان را پنهان نمی‌کنند و هر روز علنی می‌گویند تا کسی را نتوان با برچسب «نظریهٔ توطئه» خفه کرد. دولت امپریالیستیِ نئولیبرال ترامپ و نتانیاهو کاری کرده‌اند که حتی نظریه‌پردازان برجستهٔ نئوکان مجبورند از آن‌ها فاصله بگیرند. رهبران حزب دموکرات — اوباما، بایدن، کامالا هریس، هیلاری کلینتون، سوزان رایس، جان کری، وزیر خارجهٔ بایدن، مشاوران امنیت ملی اوباما و بایدن، و نامزدهای دموکرات در انتخابات میان‌دوره‌ای ۳ نوامبر — عمدتاً می‌گویند برجام خوب کار می‌کرد و ایران با برجام هرگز به سلاح اتمی دست نمی‌یافت (و در این ادعا کاملاً حق با آن‌هاست) و حملهٔ نظامی بی‌دلیل و غیرقانونی و پرهزینهٔ اقتصادی و شکست‌خورده به درخواست نتانیاهو به ایران هیچ لزومی نداشت. اما اگر ترامپ ایران را هم مثل ونزوئلا و گرینلند تصاحب کند و رئیس‌جمهور بعدی یکی از دموکرات‌ها باشد، از آن استقبال خواهند کرد؛ همان‌طور که دولت‌های اوباما و جو بایدن استقلال اقتصادی عراق را به آن برنگرداندند — فرمان اجرایی حساب نفت عراق در فدرال‌رزرو نیویورک در هر دو دولت تمدید شد.

✅ کارل مارکس در بخش اول مانیفست حزب کمونیست تحلیلی درخشان و عمیق از پیروزی‌های مدرنیته در عصر جدید ارائه کرد. منتها مارکس عصر جدید را عصر انقلاب علیه سرمایه‌داری و رهایی انسان‌ها می‌دید که هم تناقضات داخلی کاپیتالیسم به‌نحو ضروری و قطعی به آن منتهی خواهد شد، هم طبقهٔ کارگر اراده‌گرایانه آن را خلق خواهد کرد. اما چنین نشد و حتی مدافعان جدی لیبرال‌دموکراسی — از جمله مهم‌ترین فیلسوف سیاسی نظریهٔ عدالت، جان رالز، و پل استار در کتاب «قدرت آزادی: نیروی راستین لیبرالیسم» — مجبور شدند کودتاها و تجاوزات خارجی «لیبرالیسم امپریالیستی» را به‌نحو جدی نقد کنند. جان رالز که در کتاب «قانون مردمان» از نظریه‌پردازان «مداخلهٔ بشردوستانه» و «جنگ‌های عادلانه» بود، در همان کتاب کودتاهای سازمان سیا در کشورهای دیگر — از جمله کودتای سیا علیه دکتر محمد مصدق در ۱۹۵۳ — را نقد و رد کرد. رالز در بند ۵٫۴ نوشت: «ایالات متحده دموکراسی‌های آلنده در شیلی، آربنز در گواتمالا، محمد مصدق در ایران، و به نظر برخی، ساندینیست‌ها در نیکاراگوئه را سرنگون کرد. محاسن این رژیم‌ها هرچه بوده باشد، عملیات مخفیانه علیه آن‌ها به دست حکومتی اجرا شد که منافع انحصارطلبانه و الیگارشیک بدون هرگونه اطلاع یا انتقاد عمومی انگیزهٔ آن بود. این ترفند با توسل چیره‌دستانه به امنیت ملی در متن رقابت ابرقدرت‌ها آسان‌تر شد؛ چیزی که باعث شد چنین دموکراسی‌های ضعیفی، هرقدر هم به‌طرز باورنکردنی، نوعی خطر محسوب شوند. مردمان دموکراتیک اگرچه توسعه‌طلب نیستند، از منفعت امنیت‌شان دفاع می‌کنند، و حکومت دموکراتیک می‌تواند به‌راحتی برای حمایت از مداخلات مخفیانه به این منفعت متوسل شود، حتی زمانی که محرک آن عملاً منافع اقتصادی پشت پرده باشد.»
رالز حتی به‌صراحت در بند ۱۴٫۱ نوشت: «بمباران اتمی دو شهر هیروشیما و ناگازاکی، که آماج همگی آن‌ها در درجهٔ نخست جمعیت‌های غیرنظامی بود، خطاهای بسیار عظیمی بودند.» و در ادامه (بند ۴٫۴ و پاورقی‌های همین بخش) گفت ژاپن تقریباً تسلیم شده بود و هیچ نیازی به بمباران اتمی آن کشور وجود نداشت. اما ترومن نژادپرست بود و «ژاپنی‌ها را وحشی و بربر خواند و گفت باید با آن‌ها به منزلهٔ موجوداتی وحشی برخورد کرد؛ با وجود این، اکنون چقدر احمقانه به نظر می‌رسد که آلمانی‌ها و ژاپنی‌ها را کاملاً بربر و وحشی بدانیم.»
اگر به عناوینی که دونالد ترامپ در دومین دورهٔ ریاست‌جمهوری‌اش به ایرانی‌ها داده (۱ آوریل ۲۰۲۶، سخنرانی تلویزیونی: «در دو سه هفتهٔ آینده آن‌ها را به عصر حجر برمی‌گردانیم، جایی که به آن تعلق دارند.» همان شب تهدید کرد نیروگاه‌ها را یکجا بزند و گفت نفت را نزده چون اگر بزند «حتی شانس کوچک بقا یا بازسازی» نمی‌ماند. اوایل آوریل: «هیچ پلی، هیچ نیروگاهی… عصر حجر.» گزارش‌های آوریل از زبان ترامپ دربارهٔ ایرانی‌ها: «حیوان»، و یک‌بار «ژن‌های وحشتناک، نه مثل ژن‌های خودمان». ژوئیهٔ ۲۰۲۶ رهبران ایران را «تفاله» و «آدم‌های مریض» خواند. سپتامبر ۲۰۲۶ به اکسیوس: «بروم نابودشان کنم یا نه؟ تصمیم بزرگی است.» در مصاحبهٔ دیگر گزینه‌ها را گذاشت: «ایران را محو کنیم، بگذاریم از نظر اقتصادی بپوسد، یا معامله کنیم.» «ایران را کاملاً نابود می‌کنم»، «به عصر حجر برمی‌گردانم، جایی که به آن تعلق دارند»، «رهبر ایران را من باید تعیین کنم»، «محوشان کنم یا بگذارم بپوسند».) نگاه کنید، دقیقاً همان نگاه نژادپرستانه‌ای را می‌بینید که ادوارد سعید در کتاب «شرق‌شناسی» به‌خوبی تبیین کرده است. (یکی از اتهامات باراک اوباما نزد جمهوری‌خواهان دیدار او با ادوارد سعید بود.) نمی‌توان و نباید این نگرش نژادپرستانه را در بمباران زیرساخت‌های ایران نادیده گرفت؛ از جمله حملهٔ ۲۸ فوریهٔ ۲۰۲۶ به مدرسهٔ ابتدایی شجرهٔ طیبه در میناب که مأموریت حقیقت‌یاب سازمان ملل در ۱۷ سپتامبر ۲۰۲۶ با «دلایل معقول» آن را کار آمریکا و جنایت جنگی دانست: حدود ۱۵۷ کشته، از جمله بیش از ۱۲۰ کودک. رسانه‌های اصلی آمریکا همین گزارش را منتشر کردند. ترامپ گفت اشتباه جنگی بوده است.
حمله نظامی به ایران هیچ ارتباطی با آزادی و حقوق بشر و دموکراسی نداشت و ندارد( ترامپ هرگاه احساس می کند رهبران ایران در حال راه آمدن با او هستند، از آنها تعریف و تمجیدهای شگفت آوری می کند)، این حمله برای نفت و سلطه و استعمار و امپریالیسم و نژادپرستی و منافع اسرائیل است و بس. فقط و فقط همین.

text:
Podcast Summary | Candace: Exclusive Footage: A Tyler Robinson Challenger Appears! TPUSA CAUGHT Gaslighting Middle-Schoolers. | Ep 390

Overview
The center of gravity in this episode is reasonable doubt, applied in two directions at once. Candace Owens argues the criminal case against Tyler Robinson rests on a loose probable cause standard, shaky vehicle identification, and an unexamined second gray Dodge Challenger captured on video the morning of September 10. She then turns the same scrutiny on Turning Point USA, accusing it of misrepresenting a mandatory middle-school assembly as a thriving, voluntary Club America event. The throughline is that small, checkable lies erode the credibility of much larger claims, including the official account of September 10.

Key Themes
- Owens is not a party to the criminal case; the burden to prove aggravated murder beyond a reasonable doubt belongs to the prosecution, not to her.
- Her long-held theory that multiple decoys and possibly multiple Dodge Challengers existed is now supported, in her telling, by footage of a second gray Challenger near campus that morning.
- Detective Hull's probable cause reasoning, which leaned on matching Converse sneakers, is presented as far too thin to distinguish between similar vehicles and similar people.
- The June 17 UVU mass-casualty simulation, with theater makeup, crisis actors, and dozens of agencies, is treated as unusual enough to raise questions about timing, funding, and purpose.
- Turning Point USA's public framing of the Erica Kirk school event collapses under parent testimony about notification timing, locked gym doors, screened questions, and denied parent attendance.
- The absence of a formal opt-out, combined with absence penalties affecting sports eligibility, reframes the assembly as compulsory rather than voluntary.
- The speaker argues that people closest to Charlie Kirk accepted the official narrative and stopped investigating, while outsiders pushed longest.
- Unresolved questions about Erica Kirk's alleged past and TPUSA's faith framing are framed as deserving public answers, even if only to debunk them.
- A private investigator's emailed tip about a Dodge Challenger went unnoticed for roughly 20 days, which the hosts treat as evidence the show should keep widening the aperture.

Detailed Summary
Owens opens by separating herself from the criminal case. She is not a party, and the burden of proving aggravated murder beyond a reasonable doubt sits with the prosecution. Her target is a lower bar: probable cause. She quotes Detective Hull's testimony that matching Converse shoes convinced him the person in a maroon shirt and the person later wearing a black long-sleeve American flag shirt were the same individual, Tyler Robinson.

Her long-held theory is that decoys may have been in play, including multiple people dressed like Tyler Robinson and possibly multiple Dodge Challengers. That theory now has a visual anchor. Footage from the morning of September 10 shows a gray Dodge Challenger and a black Chevy Tahoe SUV arriving at the UVU admissions lot around 8:00 a.m., with two tall individuals exiting and walking toward campus.

The lot sits next to the Woodbury building, where the admissions office is located. Students call it the admin lot. Owens notes it would be convenient for anyone needing to head toward the amphitheater. The two vehicles also left within about a minute of each other around 9:50 a.m., after roughly two hours on campus.

The Challenger's driver is described as a tall single white male in jeans, a backpack, and a hat. The SUV's driver is described as a tall light-skinned male in athletic shorts and a short-sleeve light or gray t-shirt, with a stockier build.

Against that, the established timeline runs as follows. At 8:07 a.m., TMZ footage shows Tyler Robinson in a maroon shirt and shorts walking through a neighborhood near campus. At 8:23 a.m., neighborhood cameras catch his Dodge Challenger. At 8:29 a.m., it enters the UVU parking structure. At 8:43 a.m., a person in a maroon shirt emerges from the garage.

Through 9:24 a.m., Robinson is reportedly on campus, visiting a wooded area near a later-recovered rifle and speaking to a TPUSA employee. At 9:00 a.m., Denny Flood, Brian Harpole, and a security team minus Chris arrive on site. At 9:24 a.m., Robinson descends stairs in the parking structure. At 9:33 a.m., his Challenger leaves the structure.

At 10:09 a.m., Robinson reportedly returns to campus, moves through a tunnel to the parking structure, buys food at Chick-fil-A in the Sorensen Center, eats, and leaves. He later returns without a backpack, still in a maroon shirt and gray shorts. Owens stresses that there is no confirmed location for the Challenger during gaps in this timeline.

The implication is a question of identification. How can investigators reliably distinguish between two similar gray Dodge Challengers, and was the identification resting substantially on Converse sneakers? A neighbor reportedly said he saw a bald guy with two people in the back of the Dodge Challenger, yet authorities still treated the vehicle as Tyler Robinson's car. Owens calls the second Challenger critical and says it and its driver should have been identified during the investigation.

She also points to the TMZ footage as absent from the preliminary hearing and from what she calls the Tyler Robinson sizzle reel. Baron Coleman, filling in during her maternity leave and contractually obligated to care for the Breijit doll, is credited with a theory that an early morning meeting involving multiple people may have occurred before the event.

The UVU thread adds a second layer of unease. A June 17 mass-casualty bomb simulation ran from 10:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m. at the UCCU Center. It involved 50 people in theater makeup with fake injuries, nearly 20 agencies, SWAT, police, fire crews, ambulances, and a life-flight helicopter evacuating fake victims to real hospitals. Owens says such theater-involved drills with federal participation are exceedingly rare, finding only about four universities in the last five years that did something comparable. She questions the timing, the cost, and the choice of theater makeup over real training patients. She notes UVU has a high federal presence as a pipeline school for CIA, NSA, and Department of Defense careers.

The TPUSA segment turns on a single contested event. Owens disputes Turning Point USA's framing of an Erica Kirk appearance at a private school in Idaho. She says it was a mandated assembly for minors, not a voluntary, well-attended student event. TPUSA figures Blake Neff and Andrew Kolvet publicly present it as a successful Club America tour stop with 500-plus students. Owens says the audience was a combined middle and high school assembly and not an opt-in event. She notes there are only about 250 high school students, so 500-plus attendees implies middle school was included.

The event was held at a Flamingo campus. A Monday newsletter described the Thursday assembly as featuring Erica Kirk, who leads Turning Point Faith, speaking on faith and leadership. It said the event was not advertised or placed on social media by NCS or TP Faith. A parent email Owens reads states that parents were notified Monday, the event was described as designed for students, parents who asked to attend were denied, no permission slips were sent, and students were not formally offered an opt-out.

Some parents could independently excuse children, but those absences could penalize kids who play sports. A parent email clarifies that parents pictured at the event were likely there because their children participated or spoke, not because the general parent body was invited. A critical commenter claims parents knew weeks in advance; Owens demands documentary evidence predating the Monday newsletter.

The escalation moved through social media. Blake Neff called Owens's claims full of lies and distortions and shared a tweet from an account called Idaho Heartland Grandma disputing her. Owens counters by citing the account's past tweets, including violent pro-Israel rhetoric about Gaza, and again demands evidence. She says multiple parents emailed her after the event to corroborate her account.

A parent statement sharpens the case. The parent says the event was initiated by TPUSA contacting the school, not organized by students, and was a required school-day assembly including middle schoolers. Gym doors were locked, student questions were screened, and parents who asked to attend were told no. Parents were not given information beforehand about security protocols. Students attended during regular school hours, not as an independently chosen Club America sign-up.

Andrew Kovette stated only three students opted out. The parent says she personally knows more than three who did not attend. Two separate emails from parents reported their children were refused when asking to use the bathroom. The parent notes Nampa Christian has historically welcomed parents to assemblies over the past 10-plus years.

The parent lists the concerns together: a politically controversial public figure and advocacy organization, middle school inclusion, a regular school day, no parental permission, only three days notice, unclear opt-out communication, denied parent attendance requests, and unexplained security procedures. The parent argues it should have been an optional after-school or evening event and criticizes TPUSA for what she calls gaslighting. In order for the Roman government to spread its take over of Churches to the pagan masses of Rome, it had to absorb local customs and deities to make the religion more palatable to converts. They treated Saints exactly like the Roman pagans treated all of their different Gods. 

Examples…

We see the EXACT SAME thing at ancient pagan sites, where the gods and goddesses were believed to be in harmony with the landscape, embodying its qualities.

Ancient pagan beliefs survived into the Middle Ages.

text:
Three Different Lessons Hiding in One Stretch of an Ancient Chronicle

A Byzantine chronicler states his moral outright, rather than leaving readers to infer it: every work done against the decree of God is vain. What follows is offered as proof.

The Chronicon Paschale illustrates that claim with the story of Daniel and the dragon, drawn from the Greek deuterocanonical addition to Daniel known as Bel and the Dragon. The dragon differs from the other false gods Daniel confronts elsewhere in the same book. A golden statue or a set of temple vessels can only be worshipped as objects. A dragon is alive, visible, and biological, a creature the Babylonians could point to and treat as self-evidently divine because it moved and ate. Daniel's method of destroying it, feeding it something that causes it to burst, functions less as a miracle than as an experiment. The lesson embedded in the episode is not simply that false gods fail. It is that they fail once someone is willing to test the claim instead of deferring to it.

The chronicle's ending for the episode repeats a structural device found elsewhere in the same literary tradition. Daniel's accusers, having demanded he be thrown to the lions in his place, are thrown to the lions themselves and immediately killed. The same reversal appears in the Book of Esther, where Haman is executed on the gallows he built for Mordecai, and in Daniel's earlier and better-known lion's den episode, where his accusers meet the fate they had arranged for him. The pattern recurs often enough across this body of literature to function as its own moral claim: a trap set for an innocent person carries risk back toward whoever set it.

A quieter lesson sits in the material immediately following, told without any of the narrative color of the miracle stories around it. Cyrus permits the exiled Jews to return to Jerusalem. Roughly fifty thousand make the journey, lay the altar, and set the temple's foundations. The chronicle then states plainly that neighboring peoples opposed the work, and it remained unfinished for decades, until the reign of Darius. No angel intervenes to speed the process. No miracle resolves the delay. The account simply records faithful effort meeting ordinary political obstruction and stalling for a generation.

Read together, the three episodes are not making identical points. One rewards direct testing of a claim to divinity. One shows danger recoiling onto whoever aimed it at the innocent. One shows that correct religious practice does not guarantee a fast or smooth outcome, and that providence, in the chronicle's own telling, sometimes looks like decades of delay rather than immediate rescue.

text:
What "One Like a Son of Man" Meant Before It Meant Christ

A single sentence added centuries after the fact changed what one of the Bible's most famous visions is usually understood to mean.

The vision appears in Daniel 7: four beasts rise from the sea, representing four earthly kingdoms, followed by "one like a son of man" coming on the clouds to the Ancient of Days, receiving dominion, glory, and a kingdom that will never pass away. The Chronicon Paschale, a seventh-century Byzantine chronicle, quotes the passage and then adds its own line: this figure is God the Word, begotten before the ages. That identification reflects fourth-century Trinitarian vocabulary, developed at the councils of Nicaea and Constantinople, applied backward onto a text written centuries earlier.

Daniel's own chapter supplies a different interpretation a few verses after the vision itself. There, an angelic figure explains the scene directly to Daniel, stating that "the saints of the Most High" will receive the kingdom. Scholars of Second Temple Judaism generally read this as identifying the son-of-man figure with the righteous of Israel as a collective body, rather than with a single individual. On that reading, the four beasts stand for four oppressive empires, and the human figure who follows them stands for the persecuted people who outlast them. The vision offers vindication to a suffering community, not a claim about anyone's divine nature.

A separate strand of ancient interpretation complicates a simple binary here. Jewish apocalyptic texts such as the Similitudes of Enoch treat the son-of-man figure as an individual, a pre-existent heavenly being with judicial authority, exalted above ordinary humans. That reading moves closer to later messianic interpretation without arriving at anything resembling homoousian language, the specific claim that the Son shares one essence with the Father, which is the doctrinal core of the phrase the chronicler inserts.

Removed from the chronicler's gloss, the vision's lesson stands on different ground. Earthly power appears in the text as beastly, predatory, and temporary, four kingdoms rising only to be stripped of authority in sequence. What survives them is not another empire but a people who endured under all four. The reversal, not the identity of any single figure, carries the vision's original force. A chronicler reading centuries later found a different, narrower claim inside the same words, and wrote it into the margin as if it had always been there.

text:
SMITHFIELD FOODS $SFD EARNED A FULL YEAR OF ITS DIVIDEND IN THE FIRST SIX MONTHS:

The Income Len5 is watching Smithfield Foods SFD at $19.80, -$0.06 / -0.30% today, fourth of its 30 names. The Smithfield, Virginia company raises hogs on its own farms, processes them, and turns most of the meat into the packaged bacon, hot dogs, sausage and deli slices sold under Smithfield, Eckrich, Nathan's Famous and Armour.

The verdict: on September 8 Smithfield reaffirmed the one division that pays for the dividend and cut its outlook for the two that do not. Since then the share price has been set entirely by the two it cut.

Start with the payment, because the arithmetic is unusually plain. The board declared $0.3125 a share on July 30 and said the remaining payments this year would be unchanged - an annual rate of $1.25 a share, about 6.3% of this morning's price. Across 393.8M shares that costs roughly $492M a year. Smithfield made $496M of adjusted net income - profit with one-off items set aside - in the first six months of this year alone. Per share, the first half earned $1.25 adjusted. The whole year's dividend rate is $1.25.

And the stock is below where it started. The January 2025 offering sold 7% of the company at $20.00 a share; this morning is $19.80. Dividends have been collected since, but the quoted price is under the offer price twenty months later. Only about 46M of the 394M shares actually trade - WH Group of Hong Kong still owns roughly 88%.

Now the three divisions, from the August 11 report for the quarter ended June 28:

- Packaged Meats: sales $2,023M, -2.7%; adjusted operating profit $265M - what a division earns before interest and tax, with one-off items set aside - or 13.1 cents of every sales dollar
- Fresh Pork: sales $2,008M, -3.5%; adjusted operating profit $14M, 0.7 cents on the dollar
- Hog Production: sales $772M, -8.2%; adjusted operating profit $64M, 8.3 cents on the dollar

Two divisions sold almost exactly the same $2B of meat. One earned nineteen times the other.

Then September 8, before the company spoke at an industry conference. Third-quarter adjusted operating income for the whole company: $115M to $175M. Fresh Pork: a loss of $70M to $90M. Hog Production: a profit of $25M to $45M. Packaged Meats' full-year range: reaffirmed, unchanged, $1,075M to $1,150M. Chief executive Shane Smith said the change came from "external market conditions within portions of the pork value chain."

The next morning the stock fell $1.49 / -6.77% to $20.52 on 3.74M shares against a 2.06M daily average, and it has drifted lower nearly every session since - a one-year low of $19.61 on September 18. From the $22.01 close the day before that update, this is -$2.21 / -10.0%.

Here is what actually broke. Smithfield raises the hogs and also buys hogs to cut, so the two commodity divisions normally lean against each other: cheaper pigs hurt the farm and help the plant. This time both got worse together, because the price of wholesale pork fell faster than the price of pigs. The hedge that the words "vertically integrated" are meant to describe did not work this quarter.

The outside number behind it, and it is a government one: the U.S. Department of Agriculture's wholesale pork carcass cutout - what a processor gets for a whole carcass, per hundred pounds - was $87.54 on Thursday, September 17, the weakest since February 2024. Futures on lean hogs say the pigs get cheaper from here, with the October contract at 78.9 cents a pound against December at 69.6 cents. Cheaper pigs would help the plant. They would not help the farm.

One more piece of arithmetic, because it is the strongest thing on the bear side and it comes entirely from Smithfield's own figures. On August 11 the company guided the full year to $1,225M-$1,375M of adjusted operating profit. The first half delivered $638M. Put the third quarter's new $115M-$175M against those, and the fourth quarter has to produce between $412M and $622M. The best quarter Smithfield has had this year was $300M. On September 8 it reaffirmed Packaged Meats. It did not reaffirm that total.

Smithfield through the six Len5es, plus the Quality Len5:

- INCOME - STRONG, and the Len5 watching it, fourth of 30. Hunts cash reaching owners that the business itself pays for, rather than a large yield on a business that cannot keep paying it. The $1.25 rate takes under half of the $2.67 a share earned across the last four quarters, and Packaged Meats alone is guided to earn $1,075M-$1,150M before interest and tax against a dividend costing about $492M. What would knock Smithfield off the Income Len5: Packaged Meats slipping out of that reaffirmed range, because that division is what the payment actually rests on.

- QUALITY LEN5 - STRONG. Asks only that a business be profitable, earn a real return on the money its owners put in, and not owe more than that. It cleared all three: $484M of reported profit in six months against $7.00B of owners' equity - the shareholders' own stake on the company's books - and $2.00B of total borrowings against that same $7.00B, with $1.35B of cash sitting behind it. No discount is required here, which is exactly why this verdict and the next one differ.

- QUALITY-VALUE - NOT A FIT, and it fails on the half that usually passes. Hunts a business almost nobody could rebuild, bought under its worth. The price is plainly present at about 7.4 times the past year's profit and 1.1 times the company's net worth on its own books. Durability is the gap: two of three divisions are priced by a carcass market Smithfield does not set. What would put it on the Quality-Value Len5: several quarters in which the commodity divisions stop deciding the result.

- DEEP-VALUE AND SPECIAL-SITUATIONS - NOT A FIT, the nearest miss. Hunts a sound business knocked down by a fixable problem, or settled earnings bought cheaply. Knocked down is beyond argument, 33.6% under the $29.81 high of April 10. Settled is what fails: quarterly adjusted profit ran $0.58, $0.83, $0.64, $0.62 and is now modelled at $0.27. What would put it on the Deep-Value Len5: two or three quarters near one profit figure with the price still about here.

- MOMENTUM - NOT A FIT, and not narrowly. Hunts a price near its own one-year high where the recent climb and the longer one agree. It set its lowest price in a year four days ago. What would put it on the Momentum Len5: a close back above the $22.01 it carried the day before that September 8 update.

- GROWTH - NOT A FIT. Hunts profit growth the price has not charged for, on a record of producing it. The price charges very little; growth is the absent half, with company sales guided to roughly flat this year and the profit outlook cut on August 11 and again on September 8. What would put it on the Growth Len5: a year guided upward rather than downward at this multiple.

- HYPERGROWTH - NOT A FIT, the widest miss. Hunts very fast growth on a base big enough that the rate describes a real business. The base is emphatic at $7.5B of sales in six months; the rate is below zero. What would put it on the Hypergrowth Len5: nothing realistic for a pork company founded in 1936.

The comparison that sharpens it: Hormel Foods (HRL) at $20.57, +$0.11 / +0.51% today - the maker of Spam, Skippy and Planters, which buys its raw meat rather than raising it. Hormel is the finished version of what Smithfield's best division already is, and the market pays about 33 times profit for it against Smithfield's 7.4 - even after Hormel cut its own fiscal 2026 sales and profit outlook on August 27, and even sitting much nearer its own one-year low of $19.70 than its $26.60 high. So branded meat is not simply being rewarded. Branded meat that arrives with no hog cycle attached is. Hormel is a pick on none of the six Len5es: at 33 times a profit it has just guided lower, there is no discount for the value-minded Len5es and no growth for the others.

VERDICT: a branded business earning 13 cents on the dollar, bolted to two commodity divisions that are currently doing all the pricing - available at about 7.4 times earnings because the market is valuing the bolt-on rather than the brands.

RISK, and it is about the dividend specifically: the business generated $204M from running itself in the first half while paying out roughly $246M, with $350M-$450M of capital spending guided for the year on top. The $1.35B of cash and net borrowings of only about $654M can carry that, and the holiday quarter is when this industry collects - but for six months the payment ran ahead of the cash coming in.

WHEN: third-quarter results are tentatively due Tuesday, October 27 before the open, a date Smithfield has not confirmed, with about $0.27 a share expected against $0.58 a year earlier. What in them tests this: whether Packaged Meats holds near that $265M quarterly pace, and whether the full-year total finally comes down to meet the arithmetic.

Since September 8 the market has taken a tenth off this company over the price of a wholesale carcass. In that same announcement Smithfield left the branded division - the one earning 13 cents on the dollar and covering the dividend twice over - exactly where it was. A carcass price moves every afternoon. A reaffirmed range gets answered once, on October 27.

Not investment advice.

BREAKING: WHITE HOUSE ANNOUNCES TWO NEW HISTORIC NON ACCORDS

"Some people are calling them the greatest non deals of all time. I'm one of those people."

In a joint address that left several diplomats visibly recalculating their careers, the administration unveiled what it called a "double historic breakthrough" — two entirely unrelated non deals, announced back-to-back, with equal enthusiasm.
DEAL ONE: THE NAURU GUANO-PENGUIN NON ACCORD

Under the agreement, the United States will purchase Nauru's entire strategic guano reserve in exchange for relocating an unspecified number of deported penguins to the Pacific island nation.
A Nauruan government spokesperson, reached for comment, seemed cautiously blindsided:
"We were told this was a trade delegation. We did not know 'penguins' meant actual, physical penguins. We do not have snow. We do not have refrigeration for this many penguins. We have guano. That part checks out. No wonder ALL TRUMP NON DEALS are SH....Y
A visibly exhausted marine biologist, present at the signing for reasons nobody could quite explain, added:
"They're emperor penguins. Nauru is on the equator. I've said this four times in this meeting."
A White House official called it "the single greatest fertilizer-for-flightless-bird exchange in American history" — adding, unprompted, "that bar was not high, but we cleared it."

NON DEAL TWO: THE ICELAND ICE ACCORDS ("OPERATION COOL DOWN")
Minutes later, a second announcement: a long-term exclusive agreement granting Mar-a-Lago sole purchasing rights to Icelandic glacial ice, to be shipped by refrigerated tanker directly to Palm Beach — a plan described as "fixing global warming, personally, from right here."
An Icelandic trade representative offered polite confusion:
"We are happy to sell ice. We sell ice to many countries. We did not realize this particular client believed shipping it to Florida would lower the global temperature. We assumed it was for drinks."
A climate scientist in attendance was less polite:
"You're not fixing global warming. You are shipping a glacier 4,000 miles on a diesel tanker so it can melt somewhere warmer. This is, if anything, a demonstration unit for the problem."
Meanwhile, a Mar-a-Lago events coordinator seemed to be the only person present grasping the actual scale of the undertaking:
"The ice sculpture budget alone is going to be historic."

One was a possible future outcome.

text:
HISTORY IS HAPPENING AGAIN

On September 21, 1911, Canadians went to the polls in an election dominated by a familiar question: How closely should Canada tie its economy to the United States?

Prime Minister Sir Wilfrid Laurier’s Liberal government had negotiated a reciprocity agreement with Washington. It was not full free trade, but it would reduce or eliminate tariffs on many natural products, including grain, livestock, fish and lumber.

Laurier argued that greater access to the enormous American market would benefit Canadian farmers, fishers and other producers. As he told supporters during the campaign, “I have faith in the people. I have faith in the future of Canada.” He framed reciprocity as opportunity, not surrender.

His opponents saw something more dangerous.

Robert Borden’s Conservatives warned that economic integration could weaken Canadian industry, redirect trade away from Britain and place Canada’s independence at risk. In Conservative campaign literature of the time, reciprocity was described as “a step toward annexation”—a phrase that captured the intensity of the fear surrounding the agreement.

Newspapers amplified the divide. The Toronto Globe supported Laurier, arguing that “the farmer will find a wider market and a better price for his produce.” Meanwhile, Conservative-leaning papers warned that Canada risked becoming “economically absorbed by the United States.”

The debate became about more than tariffs. It became a debate about sovereignty, national identity and whether economic dependence might eventually lead to political dependence.

Laurier had governed Canada for 15 years. On September 21, his government was defeated, and Borden became prime minister. The reciprocity agreement died with the Liberal government.

One contemporary observer wrote in the aftermath that the result reflected “a nation unwilling to risk its future upon the goodwill of a foreign power, however friendly.”

More than a century later, Canada and the United States are far more economically integrated than either Laurier or Borden could have imagined. Goods, energy and components cross the border every day, often several times before becoming finished products. Millions of Canadian jobs depend on that trade.

Yet, as Canadians once again confront American tariffs and difficult trade negotiations, the central tension of 1911 feels remarkably current.

Canada benefits enormously from access to the world’s largest economy. But that access also creates vulnerability when American priorities change.

History does not provide an easy answer. Laurier was right about the opportunities offered by a larger market. Borden was right to ask what dependence might cost.

The lesson of 1911 is not that Canada should turn away from the United States. Geography and economics make that neither practical nor desirable.

It is that trade policy has never been only about trade. It is also about national resilience, political independence and Canada’s ability to make its own choices.

In 1911, reciprocity with the United States helped decide an election.

In 2026, the same fundamental question remains: How can Canada prosper alongside its most important trading partner without becoming too dependent upon it?

text:
16:13 Switzerland | 09:13 CME / Chicago
NQ / NASDAQ — NEW YORK SESSION RADAR
22 SEPTEMBER 2026

MORE THAN ONE HOUR AFTER THE OPEN
The first important message from New York is now clear:

MONDAY’S BREAKOUT HAS NOT BEEN REVERSED.

Nasdaq has pushed to another intraday record today, reaching above 27,200, while the broader market remains positive.

But this is NOT a repeat of yesterday’s explosive AI/semiconductor expansion.

Instead, New York is showing a more controlled continuation:

NQ / NASDAQ ↑
OIL ↓
US 10Y ↓
BROAD MARKET ↑
SEMICONDUCTORS MIXED

That distinction matters.

The market is holding yesterday’s breakout while rotating internally rather than relying exclusively on another vertical move in chips.
────────────────────
FIRST HOUR — WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED?
────────────────────
Nasdaq opened higher and subsequently reached a NEW INTRADAY RECORD above 27,200.
The S&P 500 and Dow are also positive.
Nasdaq has been trading roughly +0.4% to +0.5% during the morning.

This is important because yesterday’s +2.3% Nasdaq surge has NOT immediately triggered broad profit-taking.

Instead, buyers defended the higher valuation area.

Market breadth has also been constructive, with advancing stocks outnumbering decliners on both the NYSE and Nasdaq.
Therefore:
THIS IS NOT YET A FAILED BREAKOUT.

It is a breakout undergoing its first real intraday confirmation test.

────────────────────
VERSUS YESTERDAY
────────────────────

Monday:

NASDAQ +2.3%
SOX +4.3%
AMD +10%
INTEL +12.2%
ARM +17%

Today:

The INDEX remains strong.

But yesterday’s semiconductor leaders are no longer providing the same acceleration.

AMD has traded roughly 1–2% lower after yesterday’s extraordinary move.

Other chip names have also experienced profit-taking.

This creates an important divergence:
NASDAQ → NEW RECORD
SEMICONDUCTOR MOMENTUM → COOLING

For now, that is consolidation rather than a bearish signal.

After Monday’s extraordinary semiconductor expansion, some profit-taking is entirely normal.
But it means the quality of any further NQ advance must now be monitored carefully.
────────────────────
NVIDIA / SEMICONDUCTORS
────────────────────
This remains today's critical internal indicator.
Yesterday demonstrated that the AI trade could broaden beyond NVIDIA.

Today tests whether that breadth can survive.

The bullish interpretation is:

AMD/Intel/other chips consolidate yesterday’s enormous gains without breaking their underlying structure while NVDA and Big Tech keep NQ supported.

The bearish interpretation would emerge if:

AMD ↓↓
Intel ↓↓
NVDA ↓
SOX ↓↓
NQ begins losing the morning structure.

We are NOT seeing enough evidence yet to call this a semiconductor-led reversal.

At this stage it looks more like:

PROFIT-TAKING AFTER EXPANSION.

────────────────────
THE MOST IMPORTANT DEVELOPMENT:
OIL
────────────────────

Oil continues to provide macro relief.

WTI has fallen more than 2%, towards approximately $93–94.

Brent is around $98.
This is a major change from last week, when Brent approached $110 and became an inflation shock.
Markets are responding to hopes that diplomatic progress between the US and Iran could eventually help reopen the Strait of Hormuz, while Saudi Arabia has also been testing its East-West pipeline.

For NQ, this matters enormously:

OIL ↓
→ INFLATION RISK ↓
→ TREASURY YIELDS ↓
→ FED PRESSURE ↓
→ TECH VALUATION PRESSURE ↓

This is probably the most important macro support underneath today's Nasdaq strength.

────────────────────
US TREASURIES
────────────────────

US 10Y: approximately 4.95%

The yield remains BELOW the critical 5% threshold.

That is constructive for NQ.
Remember what happened last week:
10Y > 5%
oil near $110
= severe pressure on technology valuations.
Today:

10Y ≈ 4.95%

Brent ≈ $98
= substantially easier macro conditions.

This is one reason NQ has been able to absorb semiconductor profit-taking without producing a significant index reversal.

The relationship remains extremely important:
NQ ↑ + 10Y ↓ = CONFIRMED
NQ ↑ + 10Y ↑ = CAUTION
NQ ↓ + 10Y ↑ + VIX ↑ = REGIME WARNING

────────────────────
BIG TECH
────────────────────

The broader technology complex is helping compensate for the cooling in yesterday’s semiconductor leaders.

Apple is modestly positive.

AI enthusiasm also remains structurally present despite profit-taking in several chip names.

The important point is that NQ has NOT become dependent on AMD repeating yesterday’s +10% move.

Leadership is rotating.

That is healthier than an index being supported by a single parabolic group.
────────────────────
MARKET BREADTH
────────────────────
Breadth has been positive.
Advancers have exceeded decliners on both the NYSE and Nasdaq during the morning.
This provides useful confirmation.

If Nasdaq were making a record while most stocks were declining, the breakout would deserve considerably more scepticism.

That is not the structure currently visible.
────────────────────
DXY / FX
────────────────────
The dollar remains relatively firm, particularly against the yen.

USD/JPY remains important after the BOJ’s rate increase because the yen weakened despite tighter Japanese monetary policy.

For NQ this remains a secondary rather than primary driver today.

But watch for any sudden yen appreciation.

Japanese intervention risk has not disappeared, and a violent unwinding of yen-funded carry trades could spill rapidly into global risk assets.

────────────────────
VIX / VOLATILITY
────────────────────

There is currently no clear volatility confirmation of a risk-off reversal.
That matters.

A modest semiconductor pullback without a corresponding volatility expansion is fundamentally different from:

SEMIS ↓
NQ ↓
VIX ↑↑

The latter would indicate genuine institutional hedging.
The former is consistent with ordinary profit-taking.

────────────────────
GEOPOLITICS
────────────────────

The Middle East remains today's biggest unscheduled catalyst.

Markets are currently pricing some probability of diplomatic progress between Washington and Tehran.

That is helping oil.

But this remains fragile.

Any headline threatening:
Strait of Hormuz reopening prospects,
Iran negotiations,

Saudi infrastructure,

or regional energy supply

could reverse crude rapidly.

And if oil reverses sharply higher, NQ's favourable cross-asset configuration changes immediately.

────────────────────
FED / RATES
────────────────────

Markets are still digesting last week's 25bp Fed hike.

Today does not contain the type of major scheduled macro release capable of independently resetting the entire rates curve.
Instead, attention remains on Fed communication.
The question is no longer:

“Will the Fed hike?”

It is:

“HOW MANY MORE HIKES?”

That makes the 2Y Treasury particularly important.

If Fed commentary pushes the 2Y sharply higher, NQ could react even if the 10Y initially remains below 5%.

────────────────────
WHAT HAS CHANGED SINCE THIS MORNING?
────────────────────
The pre-market question was:
Will yesterday's AI breakout survive profit-taking?

After more than one hour of New York trading, the preliminary answer is:

YES.

But with an important qualification.

The INDEX breakout has survived.

The SEMICONDUCTOR acceleration has not continued at yesterday’s intensity.

That changes today's regime from:
EXPLOSIVE AI/SEMICONDUCTOR MOMENTUM
to:

BULLISH INDEX CONTINUATION WITH INTERNAL ROTATION.

That is still constructive.

But it is a lower-momentum regime.

────────────────────
BULLISH / BUY SCENARIO — 60%
────────────────────
The record breakout survives and today's consolidation develops into trend continuation.
CONFIRMATION:

• Nasdaq holds above the prior breakout area
• morning pullbacks remain shallow
• semiconductor selling remains controlled
• NVDA remains stable/positive
• Big Tech continues supporting the index
• US 10Y remains below 5%
• Brent remains below $100
• VIX remains contained
• market breadth remains positive

Under that configuration, today would become a textbook follow-through session:

EXPANSION MONDAY
→ CONSOLIDATION TUESDAY
→ HIGHER STRUCTURE PRESERVED
That would leave the NQ regime constructive into the afternoon.
INVALIDATION:

Loss of the morning structure combined with deteriorating semiconductor breadth and rising Treasury yields.

────────────────────
BEARISH / SELL SCENARIO — 40%
────────────────────

The new record becomes an exhaustion move.

CONFIRMATION:

• Nasdaq falls back below the breakout
• semiconductor losses accelerate
• NVDA joins the weakness
• Big Tech breadth deteriorates
• 10Y reverses towards/above 5%
• oil reverses sharply higher
• DXY strengthens
• VIX expands
• market breadth turns negative

The critical issue would NOT be NQ falling by itself.

It would be several markets turning simultaneously.

That would tell us today's record was rejected rather than consolidated.

INVALIDATION:

NQ recovers intraday weakness while yields and oil remain contained.

────────────────────
EDGE
────────────────────

BULLISH: 60%
BEARISH: 40%
EDGE: MODERATE.
The bullish probability has increased slightly from the pre-market assessment.

Why?

Because we now have information that did not exist before the open:

Nasdaq tested higher prices and made a NEW RECORD.

Market breadth remained positive.

Oil continued falling.

The 10Y remained below 5%.

And semiconductor profit-taking has NOT, so far, been sufficient to reverse the index.

That is meaningful confirmation.

But yesterday's extreme semiconductor momentum is cooling, so this is not an environment in which chasing every NQ extension automatically offers a strong edge.

────────────────────
WHAT TO WATCH NEXT
────────────────────
The next test is whether New York can turn this morning structure into an afternoon trend.
Watch five things together:

NQ / Nasdaq — does the record breakout hold?

SOX / NVDA — does semiconductor selling stabilise?

US 10Y — does it remain below 5%?

BRENT / WTI — does the geopolitical premium continue falling?

VIX — does volatility remain suppressed?

If all five remain aligned, the probability of trend continuation increases.

If NQ makes new highs while semiconductors weaken further and yields/VIX begin rising, the divergence becomes increasingly important.

CURRENT REGIME: BULLISH CONTINUATION / POST-BREAKOUT CONSOLIDATION — Nasdaq has confirmed Monday’s strength with a new intraday record, while lower oil and sub-5% Treasury yields support the move; semiconductor momentum is cooling but has not yet produced a regime reversal.

text:
📜 HOOK & AUTHENTIC QUOTE

We have built a civilization that can send signals to deep space, yet we cannot survive five minutes alone with our own minds. 

We mistake motion for progress, and noise for living. But a century ago, Franz Kafka left behind a radical prescription for the human soul:

"You do not need to leave your room. Remain sitting at your table and listen. Do not even listen, simply wait, be quiet, still and solitary. The world will freely offer itself to you to be unmasked, it has no choice, it will roll in ecstasy at your feet."
— Franz Kafka, *The Zürau Aphorisms*

Kafka wasn't advocating for apathy. He was revealing a forgotten truth: the universe only unveils its depth to those who possess the courage to be still.

⚡ THE MODERN MIRROR

Look at how we live today. 

The moment a quiet pause occurs—in an elevator, at a red light, in bed before sleep—we reach instinctively for a pocket-sized rectangle of glowing glass. We bleed away every idle second into the infinite scroll.

Blaise Pascal famously noted that all of humanity's problems stem from man's inability to sit quietly in a room alone. 

Today, we have institutionalized that inability. 

We trade deep contemplation for micro-doses of outrage, validation, and distraction. In doing so, we have traded genuine inner peace for perpetual mental agitation. We are no longer thinkers; we are passive consumers of synthetic reality.

🧠 DEEP ANALYSIS

Why has stillness become our greatest threat?

1. The Fear of the Unmasked Self
When the noise stops, the mirror appears. In true silence, every suppressed insecurity, unaddressed grief, and existential question rises to the surface. We do not avoid quiet because it is boring; we avoid quiet because it demands self-confrontation. Distraction is the modern anesthesia for the soul.

2. The Monetization of Your Agitation
Your lack of inner peace is not an accident—it is an economic model. Silence generates zero ad revenue. Contemplative minds do not buy things impulsively to fill an emotional void. A multi-billion-dollar attention economy depends precisely on keeping you too stimulated to ever "sit at your table and listen."

3. The Death of Deep Cognition
Contemplation is the soil from which original thought, creativity, and wisdom grow. When you never allow your brain to reach a state of quiet waiting, you lose the ability to process life deeply. You become an echo chamber of other people's opinions, reacting to everything, understanding nothing.

4. Mistaking Being Occupied for Being Alive
We wear busy-ness like a badge of honor. But frantic activity without quiet reflection is merely aimless drift. Without stillness, you are not living a life; you are simply reacting to a sequence of external triggers.

💡 THE PHILOSOPHICAL TAKEAWAY

Reclaiming your sanity in the 21st century requires an act of radical rebellion: You must reclaim your quiet room.

Inner peace is not something you go out to find, achieve, or purchase. It is what remains when you finally stop running away from yourself. 

Kafka’s promise was profound: the world unmasks itself not to the loud, the frantic, or the hyper-connected, but to the still.

To reclaim your life, step away from the feed. Close the laptop. Put down the phone. 

Sit at your table. Wait. Be quiet. 

Let the world roll in ecstasy at your feet.

***

Syria’s Imperiled Transition 
How Shock Therapy Threatens the Post-Assad Peace
By @AbuJamajem - Sam Heller
September 22, 2026

In Syria today, nearly everyone seems to be struggling. People of all classes and backgrounds can barely afford food, rent, utilities—the basics of a dignified life. The country is attempting to leave behind half a century of tyranny and 14 years of civil war for a new and freer political order. It is also recovering from an economic collapse so precipitous that it ultimately helped topple the dictator Bashar al-Assad in 2024. As the country has proceeded in its political transition under President Ahmed al-Shara, however, living conditions for most Syrians have only become worse. Costs have soared, and a promised post-Assad economic boom has not materialized. Syria’s new government has offered citizens some symbolic victories, including an end to international isolation, but, for most people, it has not delivered materially. In fact, a number of its policy choices have made their lives even harder.

Of all the problems Syria now faces, including intercommunal violence and the possible fragmentation of the country, the economy is the biggest one. Yet the country’s new leadership has insisted on austerity measures that have made the cost of living even more unbearable for the average Syrian.

Syria is by no means the only country experiencing an affordability crisis. But it is one of the world’s most politically fragile states. If the new government cannot provide for ordinary Syrians, it risks unrest that could derail the country’s post-Assad transition.

BITING COSTS

Syrian rebels led by the Islamist faction Hayat Tahrir al-Sham ousted the Assad government in December 2024. Shara, the group’s leader, eventually assumed the presidency and has since overseen the consolidation of the country’s new institutions and its postwar recovery.

His administration has scored some real wins. After decades of political isolation, Syria has gained the support of regional and global powers, including the United States, and secured the removal of most international economic sanctions. Shara’s government has for the time being kept the country from breaking apart; after defeating Kurdish-led forces in Syria’s northeast earlier this year, it is now working to reintegrate the formerly semiautonomous region. It has in large part reined in revenge attacks and sectarian killings, although pro-government partisans perpetrated two massacres of minority Alawites and Druze last year. And Shara has mostly shielded Syria from the effects of the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran, even as it has spread elsewhere through the region.

Where the new Syrian government has fallen short is in its management of the economy. Of course, reviving commerce and industry was going to be a formidable challenge for any post-Assad government. Fourteen years of civil war displaced more than half the country’s population and caused the economy to contract by more than 50 percent. The World Bank has estimated that the war caused more than $108 billion in physical damage, largely in and around three economically vital cities, Aleppo, Damascus, and Homs. The World Bank reckons that two-thirds of Syrians now live in poverty, with an income below $3.65 per person per day. According to the UN Development Program, 90 percent of Syrians are living in poverty, and 66 percent in extreme poverty.

By the last several years of Assad’s rule, conditions had grown miserable. In fact, economic collapse contributed to the regime’s implosion in December 2024, as half-starved Syrian soldiers abandoned the front lines in the face of a rebel advance. In these circumstances, even an amply resourced, expert-led government would now struggle to restart the economy. The Shara government is neither of those things.

Syrians, impoverished by economic mismanagement and war, cannot afford even the bare necessities. The cost of living far exceeds the average citizen’s income. Based on the current unofficial exchange rate, World Food Program estimates that monthly needs for a Syrian household of five, including food and utilities, cost about $197. The Syrian Center for Policy Research, a Damascus-based think tank, puts the monthly abject poverty line at roughly $255. Yet the official monthly minimum wage is equivalent to only $95. Many Syrians depend on remittances from relatives abroad to get by.

To make matters worse, the cost of living in Syria has been rising steadily. The World Food Program calculates that the cost of essentials increased by 34 percent between July 2025 and 2026. Syrians’ purchasing power has been further diminished by a weakened currency, which initially strengthened after December 2024 but has since approached Assad-era lows.

More than 80 percent of Syrians lack reliable access to sufficient food. A joint assessment by the government and World Food Program found some improvement on this front from 2024 to 2025, but only insofar as the proportion of food-secure Syrians increased from 11.1 to 18.4 percent. After a severe drought that limited agricultural production in 2025, ample rainfall this year should improve the availability of domestically grown food. But it is unclear whether Syrians can actually afford to buy from local markets.

Housing costs have also skyrocketed. According to the Syrian Center for Policy Research, rents increased almost 66 percent between May 2025 and May 2026. After trying to live elsewhere, many people have returned to homes and neighborhoods shattered by the war after they found themselves unable to afford the rents in less damaged areas. Costs are biting even for middle-class and upper-middle-class Syrians, who need to contend with rents that have doubled or tripled, as well as rising school tuitions.

HALF-BAKED

Although much of Syria’s hardship can be chalked up to the devastation of war and decades of Assad-era mismanagement, some of the country’s problems are the product of the Shara government’s policies. The country’s new leaders have undertaken a shock therapy program of economic liberalization without, it seems, fully accounting for the acute vulnerability and poverty of most Syrians.

In the Assad government’s final, most threadbare years, it slashed subsidies that it could no longer afford. The Shara government has gone even further. Months after taking power, it increased the price of state-subsidized bread—the staple of the Syrian diet—by nearly 1,400 percent. Although the state has since held the price of a standard bread bundle steady, it has repeatedly shrunk the amount of bread per bundle. Early this year, the government massively increased electricity tariffs, in some cases by as much as 800 percent. This new pricing effectively shifted the cost of restoring the country’s power infrastructure to consumers and businesses; many people have simply stopped paying impossibly high bills.

Syria’s new authorities brought fuel prices in line with global averages early on, sharply increasing costs for farming, transportation, and other sectors. On September 13, the government raised fuel prices again—40 percent in the case of diesel—while citing global energy markets and ongoing repairs to a key Syrian refinery. Protests erupted across the country in response to the price hike. They are the largest demonstrations since Assad’s ouster.

The Shara government has tried to compensate for inflation by increasing public-sector salaries: in March alone, it approved a 50 percent raise. The benefit of these higher wages is diminished by continuing inflation, however, and it has not been distributed equally. The government laid off hundreds of thousands of Assad-era employees last year, even as it hired many of its own loyalists, including for the newly reconstituted military and security services.

The Shara government has additionally opened the country to most imports, dismantling strict controls that conserved foreign currency reserves and protected local manufacturers. Syrian producers already working in adverse conditions now struggle to compete with cheap imported goods.

AMATEUR HOUR

The economic challenges facing the Shara government are daunting. It inherited a state that was effectively bankrupt. The government has projected some revenue from customs duties and consumption-related fees and taxes, and it is working to position Syria as a regional trade hub by developing road and rail links and embarking on new pipeline projects. It has retaken control of the country’s northeast, which is comparatively rich in natural resources and farmland. Yet restoring oil and gas production in the northeast will require substantial investment, and increasing wheat production might be a net drain on government coffers.

Foreign governments have not supported Syria to the extent Damascus may have expected. The United States has helped reconnect Syria to international financial networks and encouraged investment in the country, but it has not made large commitments to its recovery or convened a “friends of Syria” conference to mobilize donors—as it did for Iraq, for example, in 2016. Gulf states such as Saudi Arabia and Qatar have sent some assistance, including support for public-sector salaries, but they have not agreed to keep Syria afloat financially. Their ability to further support Syria is also in question as these powers deal with the effects of the Iran war.

The World Bank has provided grants, but the Shara government’s decision to eschew international loans has likely cut off Syria from additional liquidity in the near term. The government has not spelled out why it rejects international borrowing, although Shara has said he doesn’t want Syria “to live on assistance, or on politicized loans.” Humanitarian aid has in any case fallen away; earlier this year, cuts to donor funding, especially from the United States, forced the World Food Program to end its subsidized bread program and halve general food assistance.

Shara has envisioned a recovery powered by private investment, not aid. Yet he seems to have believed that investment would be more forthcoming. Many of the memorandums of understanding that his government initially announced with would-be investors have not translated to real commitments. Significant obstacles to foreign investment persist: the security situation is still unsettled, and Syria lacks legal and regulatory frameworks and a fully functional financial system. Investments that have been announced skew toward real estate megaprojects that seem disconnected from the country’s development needs.

The Shara government is short on economic expertise. The president relies on a handful of Hayat Tahrir al-Sham veterans as key advisers and policymakers. Their experience in governing is limited to running a small rebel-held enclave in northwestern Syria between 2017 and 2024. Shara has stripped power from legacy state institutions such as the ministries of economy and transportation and concentrated it in a handful of newly created, opaque entities linked to the presidency, including a so-called sovereign fund meant to manage a vast portfolio of state-owned assets and property appropriated from business figures linked to Assad.

The lack of know-how shows. Major policy announcements, such as this month’s fuel price increase, are abrupt and seemingly made without real study or outside consultation. And although reliable economic data has long been hard to come by in Syria, the Shara government has sometimes presented dubious figures. In March, Shara himself announced that the Syrian economy had grown between 30 and 35 percent the previous year. The Syrian Center for Policy Studies estimated that the real growth rate in 2025 was only 0.3 percent.

PATIENCE RUNNING THIN

Although the policies of the Shara government have not foreclosed an eventual recovery, they have likely delayed it and made life harder for ordinary Syrians. If basic needs are not met soon, people could lose faith in the country’s post-Assad political order.

According to polling by the magazine Syria in Transition, 52 percent of Syrians disapproved of their government’s performance in June—up from 44 percent in April. A majority of respondents in both April and June said they struggled to cover their living expenses at least once a month, and in April (the latest month with available data), 66 percent said the government was not doing enough to curb high prices. Between April and June, the number of respondents pessimistic about the country’s trajectory jumped from 30 to 46 percent.

Immediately after Assad’s fall, Syrians were willing to excuse their new government’s shortcomings. Nearly two years later, they seem more ready to express frustration. That discontent probably won’t take the form of armed struggle because Syrians are, on the whole, tired of war. But they are increasingly mounting smaller-scale protests and strikes to demand economic relief and improved public services.

Economic hardship also adds to Syria’s general combustibility, making other political and sectarian issues potentially more explosive. The Shara government is now trying to reintegrate the Kurdish northeast, including by folding Kurdish militias into the national military. At the same time, though, it is removing subsidies in the formerly semi-autonomous region—which had its own economic regime for years—hugely increasing the cost of fuel and other essentials for people living there. On the Mediterranean coast, meanwhile, authorities are trying to establish a functional relationship with the Alawite community at a time of acute economic stress. Alawites not only face the same cost-of-living pressures as their fellow Syrians but also have suffered disproportionately from public-sector layoffs and the dissolution of the Assad’s military and security services. Many are afraid to leave their villages because of safety concerns. On the coast and elsewhere, rising prices and mass unemployment are a recipe for social instability.

A Syria that is poor and violent is in no one’s interest. After years of misery and bloodshed, the country needs a chance, finally, to recover. Now, as the Shara government tries to revitalize the economy, it needs to do so with social stability in mind. The authorities must prioritize affordability so that the country’s most vulnerable are not casualties of liberalizing reforms. The government should develop new subsidies for bread, electricity, transport, farming, and industrial production while the country is emerging from economic collapse. Its international partners, meanwhile, need to provide Damascus with the resources to deliver meaningfully for ordinary citizens, and to provide a social safety net as it pursues structural reforms. Investing in energy and real estate won’t be enough to revive Syria.

The government also needs to open more channels of communication with the public to build confidence and manage discontent as Syrians endure what was always going to be a difficult transitional period. That means communicating frankly and transparently about the rationale for its economic decision-making, consulting with Syrian businesses, and empowering the newly formed parliament to play a meaningful oversight role.

Syrians were relieved to see Assad finally go, but they don’t have endless reserves of patience for Shara’s government. The country’s new leaders need to improve material conditions for ordinary Syrians immediately, or risk losing the people’s trust.

In 1918, influenza killed between 17 and 100 million people, as much as 5 percent of the global population.

During the 1918 pandemic, most scientists believed bacteria caused the disease. The influenza virus was not isolated until 1933! Around that same time, pathologists in Nashville devised a method to culture various viruses in fertilized chicken eggs.

After sterilizing the egg shells with a germicide, they pricked each one with a needle and injected a drop of virus-laden liquid into the amniotic sac. The inoculated eggs were incubated, allowing the virus to multiply. Researchers then siphoned out this fluid, now teeming with virions, and purified it for further vaccine development.

Around 1940-1941, Thomas Francis Jr., a physician at the University of Michigan, decided to make a vaccine using these egg-grown viruses. However, the U.S. Army initially feared that doing so would cause viruses to mutate and inadvertently repeat the 1918 pandemic. In response, Francis’ team, which included a young Jonas Salk, developed a method to inactivate viruses with formaldehyde, allowing them to be recognized by the immune system without causing disease and contagion.

Most seasonal flu vaccines today are still made with a nearly identical method as those pioneered by Francis and Salk in 1941. Thanks to improved surveillance and forecasting, though, we can now create “trivalent” or “quadrivalent” vaccines by injecting multiple viral strains into eggs to confer broader immunity. The World Health Organization selects these strains months in advance based on global surveillance data.

Over the last century, however, the WHO has consistently struggled to make highly effective influenza vaccines.

Because viral strains keep shifting, vaccines have to be administered every year to be effective. And their efficacy varies greatly from one year to the next. The 2014-2015 seasonal vaccine, for instance, was only 19 percent effective due to a mismatch between the selected strain and the circulating one. Even in good years, such as 2010-2011, the vaccine tops out at about 60 percent efficacy.

Fortunately, there are now hundreds of new influenza vaccines in clinical trials, many of which may offer much wider and more enduring protection. Read "The Quest for Universal Flu Vaccines": https://t.co/KilRgp40Zq
