text:
Slightly longer piece , but may be worth a read , given the debate of General Category vs Reserved Category going on.....Do you agree or otherwise?
 
One Flag. One Standard. One Future.

Dear IITians (as also others)

Before we are General or Reserved, we are Indians. That is the only identity that will carry our country to Viksit Bharat 2047. A developed India will not be built by one group defeating another on campus groups. It will be built when every talented child — from a metro coaching centre and from a government school in a far block — can stand in the same laboratory and argue about a prototype, not about ancestry. Enemies of our country look for cracks. They want our students to see classmates as rivals. We must not gift them that advantage.

This is a look at two decades of public evidence on IITs, written with respect, without slogans, and with one aim: raise capability so high that the nation needs no permanent dual standard at its summit.

What twenty years of entrance data show

Reservation in IITs follows the constitutional matrix: about 15% SC, 7.5% ST, 27% OBC-NCL, EWS, and the rest open. The entry bar is not the same. That is a fact, not an insult.

To reach JEE Advanced, the JEE Main cut-off has risen for every category since 2019, yet the gap remains wide. General has moved from roughly 90 percentile to over 93; OBC-NCL from the mid-70s toward 81; SC from the mid-50s toward 64; ST from the mid-40s toward 52.

In JEE Advanced itself, the qualifying mark for SC/ST lists is typically set near half the Common Rank List. Branch closing ranks repeat the pattern. A Computer Science seat at IIT Bombay that closes near CRL 60–70 in the open list closes far later in reserved lists. Analyses of a decade of scores have found ST and SC median marks still far below the open-category median. At the present rate of catch-up, parity at the gate would take generations unless school quality changes.

This gap is not “lack of intelligence.” It is the compound interest of unequal schools, language, nutrition, coaching markets and social capital. An honest country names the gap so that it can close it.

What happens after they enter — and after they pass out

Inside the IITs, campus studies and institute analyses have repeatedly found average GPAs lower for SC/ST cohorts than for General and OBC students. In one well-known campus survey the GPA gap between General and SC/ST was about 0.84 points. An internal review at a leading IIT found that a large share of those with CPI below 5 were from SC/ST backgrounds. Parliamentary replies have shown reserved-category students over-represented among dropouts at several older IITs — in some years around three-fifths of undergraduate dropouts at the top seven IITs, though they are about half the intake. Official reasons include academic mismatch, wrong branch choice, health and other opportunities. Students and researchers also report isolation and the cruel campus habit of treating JEE rank as a caste test. Both can be true. A gap at the gate that is not repaired by teaching and dignity becomes a wound.

After the degree, the market is blunter and, in one sense, fairer. IITs have begun asking students to drop JEE ranks from placement CVs so that recruiters judge four years of work, not the exam that opened the door. Packages cluster by branch, CPI, internships and skill. Median domestic offers at older IITs commonly sit in the mid-to-high teens of lakhs; a thin tail of global tech and quant roles pulls averages higher. Category-wise salary tables are rarely published. That silence matters: once the degree is earned, employers buy competence.

Who rose — and whom the nation should thank

Open-category IIT graduates have given India institutions that touch hundreds of millions. @NandanNilekani  of IIT Bombay helped build Infosys and Aadhaar. @RaghuramGRajan  of IIT Delhi steered the Reserve Bank through a storm. @vkhosla of IIT Delhi helped seed modern computing. Sachin and Binny Bansal of IIT Delhi built @Flipkart . Deepinder Goyal of IIT Delhi built @zomato . @bhash Bhavish Aggarwal of IIT Bombay built Ola. @sundarpichai  of IIT Kharagpur leads one of the world’s most consequential technology companies. IIT Delhi reports hundreds of IAS officers and thousands of founders among its alumni. These are national assets, not caste trophies.

Reserved-category and first-generation journeys are less often advertised as caste stories — and that restraint is healthy. They exist. K. Sivan, son of a farmer, first graduate of his family, took his doctorate at IIT Bombay and later led ISRO. Dheeraj Singh of IIT Kanpur turned a hard campus path into a global mentoring network so that current SC/ST students do not walk alone. Thousands of unnamed reserved-category IITians serve in PSUs, the civil services, teaching, district administration and the technical arms of national missions. A nation that celebrates only the already-famous wastes the quiet excellence that keeps the lights on.

The armed forces comparison(@LtGenDPPandey)

The Army, Navy and Air Force do not recruit officers through quotas with a lowered written or physical standard. NDA and CDS are common examinations; the SSB is a common test of leadership and nerve. The Supreme Court has said the armed forces should not be carved up by reservation system. Central Armed Police Forces, being civilian services, do apply reservation; the fighting services of the Union do not. That is not cruelty. It is the knowledge that when a mistake costs a life, or a war, there can be only one standard. India can learn the spirit without copying every detail: include by raising the floor, not by permanently splitting the ceiling.

Should reservation stay?

A serious country does not answer with a chant.

Those who defend reservation are right that starting lines are still unequal. A first-generation student from a remote government school is not on the same track as a child with three years of city coaching. Yanking the ladder overnight would lock talent out and would be unjust.

Those who question a permanent dual bar at the pinnacle of science are also right. Dual standards have costs: uneven classroom pace, stigma, higher attrition, and a quiet doubt about what an IIT degree means. If the score gap at entry does not shrink, reservation stops being a bridge and becomes a destination. Bridges are meant to be crossed.

The recommendation that serves Viksit Bharat 2047 is neither abolish-tomorrow nor freeze-forever. It is convergence.

Pour the real money into schools — teachers, labs, food, mathematics and language from Class 6, residential schools in aspirational districts. A seat at 18 cannot repair what was broken at 8. Keep creamy-layer rules honest so the poorest within every community receive the help. Make preparatory years, peer mentoring and mental-health support normal, not a whispered concession. Measure success every five years by the shrinking of the JEE gap and the GPA gap. If those gaps do not move, the policy is failing the students it claims to love. Judge graduates, as the Army judges officers, by what they do after entry.

The spirit no enemy can use

Do not turn a classmate’s rank into a weapon. Do not turn a classmate’s category into a shield against effort. Do not film campus bitterness for people who do not wish this Republic well. The child who entered through the open list and the child who entered through a reserved list will pay the same taxes, salute the same flag, and grow old under the same sky.

Twenty years of numbers tell us the starting lines are still unequal. They also tell us that once inside, teaching, grit and character decide who finishes strong. Honour every IITian who stayed, built, mentored and served. Fix the schools so that reservation becomes less necessary each decade. Keep the standard high enough for a developed India. Speak as one people. That is the only identity no enemy can split — and the only spirit that will make 2047 a year of pride, not of fracture.

‼️ TRUMP AT UN: DEAL OR ISLAMIC REPUBLIC TO HELL (full speech on Iran)–– President Trump used today’s UN General Assembly speech to recap the Iran war, the reasons for it, named both operations, and put a binary choice on the table. He closed the file with: it will get done “one way or the other,” and “fast.” [full transcript at bottom]

USA BRAVELY CHOSE TO ACT

🔸 Trump doesn't believe in ignoring a problem because doing so makes it harder to solve later on.
🔸 “While others have talked, I have acted. While others have spoken of peace, I have made peace. While others have ignored threats, I have confronted them.”
🔸 Called the Islamic Republic “the number one sponsor of terror.”
🔸 “For 51 years, the fanatical Iranian regime has ruled by bloodshed and mass murder.”
🔸 “They were the bully of the Middle East, but they are the bully no more.”
🔸 Unwavering line since he entered politics: he will never allow Iran a nuclear weapon.

TALKS, THEN MIDNIGHT HAMMER

🔸 Said that on taking office last year he opened negotiations and offered “fully economic cooperation” if Iran ended the nuclear program and support for terror.
🔸 “They refused. They absolutely refused. That was a big mistake.”
🔸 Operation Midnight Hammer: “the U.S. military obliterated their nuclear program beneath mountains of rubble.”
🔸 Offered a deal again. Refused again.
🔸 Said the regime kept building a missile and drone stockpile, including a missile capable of hitting Europe. “I hope the Europeans realize that.”
🔸 Stated goal, per Trump: finish a “mad dash to a nuclear bomb from behind this conventional ballistic missile shield.”

WHAT THE REGIME DID

🔸 Marked 25 years since 9/11 and the coming third anniversary of October 7.
🔸 Said October 7 terrorists were funded by Iran. 1,200 killed, including dozens of Americans and “many babies.”
🔸 “Iran’s supreme leader celebrated that massacre and called it a service to humanity.”
🔸 “The same regime slaughtered over 72,000 of its citizens this year. Recently, 10,000 were killed for protesting.”
🔸 Said prior presidents and others [world leaders] knew the problem and “just wanted to ignore it.”

OPERATION EPIC FURY

🔸 “As a result of Operation Epic Fury, all 159 ships of their navy are now lying at the bottom of the sea.”
🔸 Air force gone. Radar gone. Anti-aircraft equipment gone.
🔸 Missile and drone manufacturing “almost gone.”
🔸 “Their economy is gone. The only thing that isn’t gone is inflation, which is destroying their country and is now well over 300%.”

CEASEFIRE BROKEN / HORMUZ

🔸 Said Iran violated a ceasefire meant for nuclear discussions with “brazen acts of terrorism against civilian ships.”
🔸 Thanked the UN Security Council for a resolution condemning those attacks. Said it drew more co-sponsors than any Security Council resolution in history.
🔸 US Navy “has recently escorted more than 1 billion barrels of oil out of the Strait of Hormuz.”
🔸 “More oil is flowing than at any point since the start of the war.”
🔸 Daily escorts he cited: 22, 25, 30, 32, and 37 ships “every single day. Every single night.”

THE CHOICE

🔸 “Will a deal be made with Iran that lets them rebuild and create a far greater country than it ever was before?”
🔸 Or “do I annihilate the Islamic Republic and do it quickly, never giving them a chance to kill and destroy people and countries again?”
🔸 “Do I drive them into hell with no chance of survival and no hope of future greatness or generations?”
🔸 Said he believes a deal comes “right after the election” because Tehran is “waiting to see how I do in the midterm election.”
🔸 “What they don’t realize is that I’m not running. I did that already and won in a landslide.” Still got two and a half years left.
🔸 “I gave absolutely no credence and will not give credence to the election when it comes to Iran. It doesn’t even enter my mind. The only thing that does is that Iran will never have a nuclear weapon.”

MUNITIONS / ISOLATION

🔸 Rejected claims the US is low on munitions. “We have more munitions than we could ever possibly even think of using.”
🔸 Building at levels “we have never done before.” 18 munition plants under construction.
🔸 Called on all nations to enforce “complete economic isolation of Iran” until: (1) attacks on commercial shipping stop; (2) nuclear ambitions are relinquished, (3) and support for terror ends.
🔸 “The terrorist regime is behaving badly not because they are strong and confident, but because they are weak and desperate.”
🔸 Close on the file: “The United States and Iran will definitely get it done. We will get it done one way or the other. It’s going to be done. It’s going to be done fast.”
..............................................
📃 FULL TRANSCRIPT 📃

As president of the most extraordinary nation in history. I have no interest in leaving dangers to grow for another day. I do not believe in letting problems fester. They only become harder to solve. So while others have talked, I have acted. While others have spoken of peace, I have made peace. While others have ignored threats, I have confronted them. While others have talked of courage, America has shown it. While others have promised strength, I have used it to make America the most powerful country in the world. Working with many nations in this room, we are solving decades of intractable challenges, and we are settling years of unfinished business. And we're doing it well. 

There is no better example of a danger that was allowed to gather strength at the world's peril than the number one sponsor of terror: the Islamic Republic of Iran. For 51 years, the fanatical Iranian regime has ruled by bloodshed and mass murder, spreading death and carnage and chaos across the entire Middle East and beyond. They were the bully of the Middle East, but they are the bully no more. 

From the first day I entered the political arena, I've been unwavering: I will never allow Iran to have a nuclear weapon. Upon taking office last year. I immediately opened negotiations with Iran and offered them fully economic cooperation in exchange for ending their nuclear program and support for terror. But they refused. They absolutely refused. That was a big mistake. 

Then, in Operation Midnight Hammer, the U.S. military obliterated their nuclear program beneath mountains of rubble. And again, I urged Iran to make a deal. And again, they refused. 

The regime continued building a vast missile and drone stockpile that threatened the security of every American service member in the region and everyone else in the region. They also made a missile that was capable of hitting Europe, and they were very proud of it. I hope the Europeans realize that. Iran's goal was to complete their mad dash to a nuclear bomb from behind this conventional ballistic missile shield. If they had succeeded, that wicked regime would have been free to spread terror and death forever, knowing that any attempt to stop them would face an arsenal of nuclear annihilation.

In America, we just marked the 25th anniversary of the worst terror attack in history, September 11th, which killed 3000 people just a few miles from here. It was an unbelievably terrible time. In two weeks, we will mark the third anniversary of the October 7th attack in Israel, where terrorists funded by Iran tortured, mutilated and killed 1200 very innocent civilians, including dozens of Americans and many babies. Babies. Little, tiny, beautiful babies. 

Iran's supreme leader celebrated that massacre and called it a service to humanity. The same regime slaughtered over 72,000 of its citizens this year. Recently, 10,000 were killed for protesting. Just imagine such a vile regime wherever empowered to carry out large scale terror attacks from behind a nuclear shield. This was the reality we had to confront the reality that far too many preferred to ignore. They all ignored it. Many presidents and many others just wanted to ignore it. They were unwilling to do anything about it, but they knew the problem.

After giving Iran every chance for a deal, I took action to ensure that neither the United States nor any nation or soul would ever have to face such a nightmare, such a catastrophic problem.

As a result of Operation Epic Fury, all 159 ships of their navy are now lying at the bottom of the sea. Likewise, their air force is gone. Their radar is gone. Their anti-aircraft equipment is gone. Their missiles and drone manufacturing capacity is almost gone. Their economy is gone. The only thing that isn't gone is inflation, which is destroying their country and is now well over 300%.

Yet, even after we agreed to a cease fire for nuclear discussions, Iran promptly violated it with brazen acts of terrorism against civilian ships from other countries. I want to thank the U.N. Security Council for voting overwhelmingly to pass a resolution condemning Iran's despicable terrorist attacks on commercial shipping. Thank you very much. That resolution, I'm pleased to say, received more co-sponsors from UN member nations than any Security Council resolution in history. That's something. 

Now, we must be equally united in maintaining pressure. The United States Navy has recently escorted more than 1 billion barrels of oil out of the Strait of Hormuz, and more oil is flowing than at any point since the start of the war. We're taking 22, 25, 30, 32 and 37 ships out, respectively. Every single day. Every single night.

But I have a big decision to make. Will a deal be made with Iran that lets them rebuild and create a far greater country than it ever was before? Maybe one of the greatest in the Middle East or even the world? Or do I annihilate the Islamic Republic and do it quickly, never giving them a chance to kill and destroy people and countries again? Do I drive them into hell with no chance of survival and no hope of future greatness or generations? But I believe we'll make a deal right after the election, because it doesn't make sense for them not to. 

They're waiting to see how I do in the midterm election. What they don't realize is that I'm not running. I did that already and won in a landslide. We won in a giant landslide, and I'll be here for two and a half years. The Republican Party is running and I'll be helping them, but I am not running. I gave absolutely no credence and will not give credence to the election when it comes to Iran. It doesn't even enter my mind. The only thing that does is that Iran will never have a nuclear weapon.

The cowards and traitors would love to say the United States is low on munitions. But that's not true. We have more munitions than we could ever possibly even think of using, and we're building them at levels that we have never done before. We are adding to our stockpiles faster than we have ever been able to do before. Top of the line stuff. In addition, in the very near future, massive munition plants will be opening. There are 18 of them being built by the greatest defense companies in the world right now –– 18 under construction –– some of them very quickly, will be completed. They're almost there. And that rapid construction will be leading to very rapid deployment of missiles of every type and ammunition of every type, and will be able to supply our allies at a much faster rate than we're doing right now.

I call on all nations to join us in enforcing the complete economic isolation of Iran until they stop their attacks on commercial shipping, relinquish their nuclear ambitions, and cease their support of terror. The terrorist regime is behaving badly not because they are strong and confident, but because they are weak and desperate. If we stand united, we will soon see a world free of the last 51 year menace of Iranian terror, and oil prices will come plummeting down even lower than they were at the start of the conflict. And they were very low. In the United States, they were really low. With courage and resolve, anything is possible. Big changes can happen and happen fast.

[...]

The United States and Iran will definitely get it done. We will get it done one way or the other. It's going to be done. It's going to be done fast.

text:
The US Air Force could have barely two pilots for every three fighter pilot positions in 2027, as commercial airlines continue competing for the same highly experienced aviators the military has spent years training.

Official Air Force budget documents project fighter pilot manning falling to 67.2% in FY2027, down from 75.4% in FY2025, while bomber pilot manning is projected to fall even more sharply from 81.5% to 68.7%. The problem is particularly difficult because experienced military pilots become extremely attractive airline recruits once they are able to leave active service, and the Air Force has previously acknowledged that it simply cannot compete with commercial carriers on money alone.

Airlines can also offer something money cannot completely solve: a civilian career without military deployments and potentially greater stability for pilots and their families. Meanwhile, Boeing expects commercial aviation to require around 674,000 new pilots worldwide through 2045, meaning demand for qualified aviators is unlikely to disappear.

The Air Force is fighting back with retention bonuses and other incentives designed to keep experienced aviators in uniform, while simultaneously developing a future force that could include around 1,000 Collaborative Combat Aircraft, semi-autonomous aircraft designed to operate alongside crewed fighters rather than replace their pilots entirely.

For the USAF, therefore, the challenge isn’t simply recruiting somebody who wants to fly a fighter jet. It’s persuading highly trained pilots to stay once the airline industry comes calling.

if I be a heretic,that would mean I am sick and  even your Vicar of Christ would offer the Great Physician. Be as your blessed Chicago Bears fan, my dear brothers…even I am attempting to bring the Christ in this study, therefore: please stop shaking the operating table.
Continuing ⭐️ 
If anyone makes that proclamation just as Peter did, you, I, and the Muffin Man down the road will receive all the promises and gifts. Jesus is taking this one, my Brother.
“For all the promises of God find their Yes in him.” (2 Corinthians 1:20)
Remember: we have a newly spiritual temple within, led by the only High Priest, Jesus.
“We have such a high priest… a minister in the holy places, in the true tent that the Lord set up, not man.” (Hebrews 8:1-2)
Just as the Heavenly Father commanded, “Let them make me a sanctuary, that I may dwell in their midst” (Exodus 25:8), so He asked the same of Jesus. This time the temple and all its necessary workings would be built by Jesus Himself, for the builder of the house has more honor than the house (Hebrews 3:3), so the Father of All can once again dwell among His people, this time inside their very persons through the One Mediator.
“For there is one God, and there is one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus.” (1 Timothy 2:5)
My brother, once you see Peter’s proclamation and Jesus’ response together, the following verses become clearer than heavenly streets of gold.
For truth’s sake: the keys of the kingdom were first spoken to Peter  “I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven, and whatever you bind on earth shall be bound in heaven” (Matthew 16:19). 
Two chapters later the same bind-and-loose word is given to the disciples together (Matthew 18:18). After the resurrection Jesus breathed on them and said, “If you forgive the sins of any, they are forgiven them” (John 20:23). The Key of David itself remains with Jesus: what He opens no one can shut (Revelation 3:7; Isaiah 22:22).

text:
Chapter Four — James: Faith That Must Show Itself

James opens his epistle with an address most commentators apparently wish had been printed in disappearing ink: “James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad, greeting” (James 1:1). Twelve tribes means twelve tribes. A man can spiritualize it into whatever church organization he likes, but the text still says what it says when the smoke clears. James is dealing with Jewish readers, and his epistle contains language about trials, patience, endurance, works, judgment, the law, and practical faithfulness that fits perfectly within a Jewish doctrinal environment and becomes especially significant when viewed toward the coming time of Jacob’s trouble.

Then comes the famous statement: “faith without works is dead” (James 2:20). Paul says, “to him that worketh not, but believeth” (Romans 4:5). James says Abraham was “justified by works” when he offered Isaac (James 2:21). Paul uses Abraham in Romans 4 to prove justification by faith apart from works. Some fellows treat that like a theological cage match and spend their lives trying to make one apostle knock the other one out. But they are not answering the same question. Paul is dealing with the ungodly sinner being counted righteous before God. James is dealing with a professed faith that has no visible obedience. Paul goes to Genesis 15, where Abraham believed God. James goes to Genesis 22, years later, where that faith was demonstrated in action. One deals with the root. The other deals with the fruit.

That becomes enormously important in the Tribulation. A man will not be able to hide forever behind a verbal profession. The Beast will demand a decision. Worship or refuse. Mark or no mark. Buy and sell or be shut out. A faith that never produces obedience will be exposed as dead when the pressure arrives. James becomes practical with a prophetic edge: faith that claims life but never moves under pressure is useless profession. Works do not manufacture genuine faith, but genuine faith moves. A man who says, “I believe the Lamb,” and then receives the Beast’s mark to protect his business has allowed his works to interpret his profession for him.

Chapter Five — Hebrews: Hold Fast, Draw Not Back

Hebrews is another book that Church Age readers frequently raid for devotional gems while quietly ignoring the warning labels on the shelves. The title says Hebrews. The content is saturated with Jewish history, priesthood, covenant, sacrifice, wilderness warnings, temple imagery, and promises associated with Israel’s prophetic hope. Again, that does not mean the Church cannot profit from Hebrews. “All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable” (2 Timothy 3:16). But profitable does not mean every doctrinal warning defines the eternal standing of a member of Christ’s Body.

The language of Hebrews is unmistakably about continuing, holding, enduring, and not drawing back. “We are made partakers of Christ, if we hold the beginning of our confidence stedfast unto the end” (Hebrews 3:14). “Let us hold fast the profession of our faith without wavering” (Hebrews 10:23). “Cast not away therefore your confidence” (Hebrews 10:35). “Now the just shall live by faith: but if any man draw back, my soul shall have no pleasure in him” (Hebrews 10:38). “Let us run with patience the race that is set before us” (Hebrews 12:1). That is not Paul’s normal language concerning the sealed standing of the Body of Christ. Hebrews repeatedly places readers before the danger of retreat, apostasy, unbelief, and failure under pressure.

Viewed toward the Tribulation, those warnings stop looking like troublesome exceptions and start looking like perfectly placed signposts. Jewish believers in that coming crisis will face enormous temptation to retreat. The pressure will say, “Go back. Bow. Compromise. Save your neck. Save your property. Save your family. Take the mark. Join the system.” Hebrews

From enhancing transport infrastructure to preserving our forests and rich cultural heritage, North Bengal remains central to our governance priorities.

text:
Precision and Beauty as Acts of Obedience.

God is not vague about worship. When He commanded a dwelling place among His people, He did not say, “Do something nice.” He gave measurements, materials, colors, textures, and sequences. Chapters of Scripture linger over gold overlays, cherubim worked into linen, loops and clasps, the exact height of boards, the fragrance of incense, and the way light would fall on hammered gold. Those details were not decoration. They were obedience. Precision and beauty were how Israel said, “You are holy, and we will not treat Your presence as ordinary.” 

The wilderness tabernacle and later the temple were built “according to the pattern” shown on the mountain. God filled Bezalel with the Spirit “in wisdom, in understanding, in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship” so that artistic design itself became a Spirit-empowered ministry. Excellence in the small things was not vanity. It was fidelity. The people brought more than enough. The craftsmen followed the pattern. And the glory of the Lord filled the house. 

That same God still inhabits the praises of His people. The New Covenant does not abolish reverence; it relocates it. We ourselves are now living temples. The place of worship is no longer only a building of acacia and gold. It is the gathered church, the ordered service, the prepared heart, the preached Word, the Lord’s Table, and the quiet faithfulness of ordinary saints. Details still matter because God still matters.

As a prophet
The prophet’s calling is to speak what God has actually said, not a smoothed-down impression of it. Attention to detail means staying with the text until the edges are sharp: the connecting words, the repeated phrases, the hard sayings, the context that will not fit our slogans. A short attention span turns prophecy into inspiration-without-content. What is missed is the weight of “thus says the Lord.” People hear mood instead of message. They leave stirred but untaught, moved but not converted.

As a leader
Leaders set the temperature of a house. If the leader is sloppy with preparation, time, money, names, follow-through, and the order of worship, the people learn that God can wait. Attention to detail looks like planning services so that Scripture, prayer, song, and sacrament cohere; like knowing who is hurting; like guarding the table and the teaching; like finishing what was started. Beauty here is not luxury. It is love made visible in order. What is missed when attention collapses is trust. The flock senses that no one is watching the gates.

As a minister
Ministry is mostly unseen work done with care: the hospital visit that is not rushed, the funeral that honors both grief and hope, the counseling session that actually listens, the sermon that has been prayed over and studied rather than assembled from fragments. Bezalel’s gift was not only skill but the humility to work inside God’s specifications. Ministers who cannot linger miss the texture of souls. They offer generalities where God intends particular grace. People are left with a sense that church is busy but not deep.

Every disciple is called to the same posture: “Whatever you do, work heartily, as for the Lord.” Faithfulness in little things is the school of larger things. Attention to detail is how we love God with the mind and the hands: arriving ready to worship, singing the words we actually mean, examining ourselves before the bread and cup, reading a passage until it reads us, keeping a promise, noticing the person no one else noticed. Beauty in a follower’s life is not performance. It is the quiet shine of a life arranged around Christ.

Precision is not the enemy of the Spirit. Carelessness is. Beauty is not a luxury added after obedience. In the place of worship, beauty is obedience—the offering of our best attention to the God who first attended to us in every detail of redemption.

Prepare the house. Quiet the heart. The Lord is present and deserves our complete attention.

text:
Holmes Did Not Find the Facts: What the State and Federal Courts Actually Ruled in the Leo Frank Case

The legal record supports one narrow point: Justice Oliver Wendell Holmes Jr. did not make factual findings proving Leo Max Frank’s claims of mob control. Holmes and Justice Charles Evans Hughes argued for another federal hearing on disputed facts. Their dissent in Frank v. Mangum did not itself decide those facts.

A dissent is an opinion from a judge or justice who disagrees with the court’s majority. An appellate court reviews rulings made in lower courts. It does not normally retry the case, call the witnesses again, or replace the jury with a new jury. A factual finding is a court’s decision about what happened after evidence has been heard and evaluated. These definitions help separate what the Georgia courts decided from what Holmes later argued should happen in federal court.

The Trial and the First Motion for a New Trial

Leo Frank’s murder trial began Monday, July 28, 1913, in Fulton Superior Court in Atlanta. Judge Leonard S. Roan presided. On Monday, August 25, 1913, the jury returned a guilty verdict for the murder of thirteen-year-old Mary Phagan. On Tuesday, August 26, Judge Roan sentenced Frank to death, and Frank’s lawyers filed a motion for a new trial.

A motion for a new trial asks the trial judge to set aside a verdict and hold another trial because of claimed legal errors, problems with the evidence, juror issues, misconduct, or other claimed defects. Frank’s motion grew to 103 grounds. It attacked evidentiary rulings, the legal sufficiency of the evidence, alleged juror prejudice, and disorder in and around the courthouse.

On Friday, October 31, 1913, Judge Roan denied the motion for a new trial. Frank then appealed to the Georgia Supreme Court. An appeal asks a higher court to review rulings made in a lower court.

Tuesday, February 17, 1914: Georgia Supreme Court Affirms the Conviction, 4–2

On Tuesday, February 17, 1914, the Georgia Supreme Court decided Frank v. State, 141 Ga. 243, 80 S.E. 1016. Justice Samuel C. Atkinson wrote the main opinion. The court affirmed Frank’s conviction by a vote of 4–2. Chief Justice William H. Fish and Justice Marcus W. Beck dissented on a specific evidence issue. They objected to admission of testimony about alleged prior sexual conduct involving Frank, including testimony from Jim Conley and C. B. Dalton. Their dissent did not find Frank innocent, did not find the State’s evidence insufficient, and did not make a new finding about who killed Mary Phagan. Their disagreement concerned whether this class of evidence should have been admitted at trial (Georgia Supreme Court, 2).

The majority directly reviewed the sufficiency of the evidence. Sufficiency means whether the trial record contained enough legal evidence for a reasonable jury to return the guilty verdict. It does not mean the appellate judges held a second trial. It means they reviewed the record and decided whether the verdict had enough legal support to stand.

The court’s twentieth headnote said, “The evidence supports the verdict, and there was no abuse of discretion in refusing a new trial.” The opinion also said the justices had carefully considered the evidence and found it sufficient to uphold the verdict. The court found no substantial trial error requiring reversal (Georgia Supreme Court, 2).

This ruling went well beyond a technical rejection of Frank’s appeal. The Georgia Supreme Court expressly reviewed the strength of the trial evidence and held it legally sufficient to support the guilty verdict. The court also reviewed Frank’s claims involving courtroom disorder, applause, cheering, and juror impartiality. On the cheering heard outside during the jury poll, the court relied on juror affidavits and upheld Judge Roan’s finding of no harmful effect on the jurors’ answers.

An affidavit is a written statement made under oath. Polling the jury means asking each juror individually whether the announced verdict is his verdict.

Wednesday, February 25, 1914: Rehearing Denied Unanimously

Frank asked the Georgia Supreme Court to reconsider its February 17 ruling. A rehearing is a request asking the same appellate court to reconsider a decision already made.

On Wednesday, February 25, 1914, all six justices denied the rehearing. Fish and Beck still disagreed with the majority on the evidence issue discussed in their dissent, but every justice agreed to deny another hearing. The court said the points raised in the rehearing request had been considered during the original decision (Georgia Supreme Court, 2).

At this stage, the guilty verdict had survived Judge Roan’s post-trial review, a 4–2 Georgia Supreme Court decision, and a unanimous refusal to rehear the appeal.

The Extraordinary Motion Based on Claimed New Evidence

Frank next filed an extraordinary motion for a new trial. This was a later request for another trial based mainly on claimed newly discovered evidence after the ordinary new-trial process had ended.

The reported legal history for Frank v. State, 142 Ga. 617, 83 S.E. 233, places the Fulton Superior Court proceeding on Friday, May 8, 1914, with Judge Benjamin H. Hill presiding. Judge Hill heard affidavits and evidence offered by Frank. The State answered with a strong counter-showing, meaning evidence offered to challenge the claimed new evidence. Judge Hill denied another trial (Georgia Supreme Court, 3).

Frank appealed again. On Wednesday, October 14, 1914, the Georgia Supreme Court unanimously affirmed Judge Benjamin H. Hill in Frank v. State, 142 Ga. 617, 83 S.E. 233. Justice Joseph Henry Lumpkin wrote the opinion, and all of the justices concurred.

The court explained newly discovered evidence had to be strong enough to probably produce a different verdict. It reviewed Frank’s showing and the State’s counter-showing and found no abuse of discretion by Judge Hill. Abuse of discretion means a judge used legal decision-making power in an unreasonable or improper way. The Georgia Supreme Court found no such abuse and affirmed the denial of another trial (Georgia Supreme Court, 3).

A Separate Attack on the Verdict Because Frank Was Absent

Frank also brought a different challenge based on his absence from the courtroom when the verdict was received on Monday, August 25, 1913. On Thursday, April 16, 1914, he filed a motion to set aside the verdict.

A motion to set aside asks a court to declare a judgment or verdict legally invalid. Frank argued his absence when the jury returned the verdict made the verdict void.

The State filed a demurrer. A demurrer was a legal objection arguing the filing did not state a valid legal basis for relief even if the pleaded facts were accepted for purposes of deciding the legal issue. On Saturday, June 6, 1914, Judge Benjamin H. Hill sustained the State’s demurrer on every ground and dismissed Frank’s motion (Georgia Supreme Court, 4).

Frank appealed. On Saturday, November 14, 1914, the Georgia Supreme Court affirmed Judge Hill in Frank v. State, 142 Ga. 741, 83 S.E. 645. Justice Hiram Warner Hill wrote the opinion. Justice Hiram Warner Hill of the Georgia Supreme Court was a different person from Fulton Superior Court Judge Benjamin H. Hill.

The Georgia Supreme Court held Frank raised his absence claim too late. His original motion for a new trial had recited his absence, but he had not used it as a ground for a new trial. The court also held his lawyers could waive his presence at reception of the verdict and Frank later accepted the waiver through his conduct in the case (Georgia Supreme Court, 4).

The November 14 opinion also dealt directly with Frank’s claims of disorder and public excitement. The court said those claims had already been included in the original motion for a new trial, examined on the facts, ruled against Frank, and affirmed on the first appeal. In other words, the mob-pressure and disorder claims were not new when the federal habeas case later arrived. Georgia courts had already heard and ruled on them (Georgia Supreme Court, 4).

The First Route to the U.S. Supreme Court

After the November 14 state ruling, Frank tried to bring the verdict-absence and federal constitutional issues to the U.S. Supreme Court through a writ of error. A writ of error was an older procedure used to ask a higher court to review claimed legal or constitutional errors in a lower-court judgment.

On Monday, November 23, 1914, Justice Joseph Rucker Lamar denied Frank’s application for a writ of error. Lamar reasoned the Georgia Supreme Court’s ruling rested on Georgia procedure governing when and how a verdict could be attacked. He found no federal question open for review through this route. On Wednesday, November 25, Frank presented the request to Justice Holmes. Holmes also refused it. Holmes expressed serious doubt about due process under the allegations presented, but he said he was bound by the Georgia Supreme Court’s ruling on the lateness of Frank’s motion (Justice Lamar and Justice Holmes, 7).

The application then went to the full U.S. Supreme Court. On Monday, December 7, 1914, the Court denied the application in Ex parte Frank, 235 U.S. 694. The published ruling is short: the application for allowance of a writ of error was denied. This ruling did not retry the case or find new facts. It closed this particular route of federal review (U.S. Supreme Court, 5).

Monday, December 21, 1914: Judge William T. Newman Denies Federal Habeas Corpus

Frank then used a different federal procedure. He filed a petition for a writ of habeas corpus in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Georgia. Habeas corpus is a legal procedure allowing a prisoner to ask a court whether his custody violates federal law or the Constitution.

The federal judge was William T. Newman. There was no panel of federal District Court judges. Newman alone ruled on Frank’s habeas petition.

Newman’s formal written order is dated Monday, December 21, 1914. He reviewed Frank’s petition and exhibits, a copy of Frank’s original motion for a new trial, and the Georgia Supreme Court opinion. He did not call witnesses, hear jurors, or hold a new evidentiary hearing. He treated the first issue as a legal one: did Frank’s own petition and supporting papers show a right to federal habeas relief? Newman answered no (U.S. District Court, 6).

An evidentiary hearing is a court hearing where evidence is presented so a judge can decide disputed facts. Newman did not hold one because he concluded Frank’s pleaded facts, even taken as presented for purposes of deciding whether to issue the writ, did not legally entitle Frank to release through habeas corpus.

Newman’s written order went further. He said even if the writ issued and Frank received a hearing, no discharge from custody or other habeas relief could legally follow under the claims presented. His reasoning rested heavily on the state-court history. Frank had been tried in a court with jurisdiction, had filed a motion for a new trial, had received review in the Georgia Supreme Court, had later filed a motion to set aside the verdict, and had received another Georgia Supreme Court ruling. Frank had also sought writ-of-error review from individual U.S. Supreme Court justices and from the full Court (U.S. District Court, 6).

Newman also rejected the idea of using federal habeas as a new appellate layer over the Georgia courts. He reasoned a federal District Court hearing at this stage would place his court in the position of exercising supervisory power over Georgia’s courts in a way he did not believe federal law allowed. He also noted no challenge existed to the jurisdiction of the original Georgia trial court or the state appellate courts. In Newman’s view, the petition itself showed no legal right to habeas relief (U.S. District Court, 6).

Jurisdiction means a court’s legal power to hear and decide a case. Due process means government must use a fair legal process when taking away life, liberty, or property.

Newman then refused a certificate of probable cause. Under the federal law then in force, Frank needed this certificate to take the habeas appeal forward. A certificate of probable cause meant a judge or justice found enough legal basis for appellate review. Newman reasoned he could not deny the writ as legally unsupported on the record presented and then certify probable cause for an appeal on the same record. His formal certificate order also carries the date Monday, December 21, 1914 (U.S. District Court, 6).

This is the central point in Newman’s ruling. He did not hold a factual hearing and then find Frank’s allegations false. He ruled a factual hearing was not legally required because, in his view, Frank’s own petition and the court records attached or referenced did not establish a right to federal habeas relief.

The original federal judicial file, Leo M. Frank v. C. Wheeler Mangum, Sheriff of Fulton County, Georgia, is preserved in the Records of the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Georgia at the National Archives and is cataloged by the Digital Library of Georgia. A readable reproduction of Newman’s December 21 orders and opinion also appears in the Mary Phagan-Kean Legacy Project transcription of the December 21 and December 22, 1914 Atlanta Journal. The legal order itself, not the newspaper headline, controls the legal date used here (U.S. District Court, 6).

Monday, December 28, 1914: Justice Lamar Allows the Habeas Appeal

Frank’s lawyers then went to Justice Joseph Rucker Lamar, the U.S. Supreme Court justice assigned to the Fifth Circuit. On Monday, December 28, 1914, Lamar granted a certificate of probable cause and allowed Frank’s appeal from Newman’s federal ruling. He required a $300 bond (Justice Lamar, 7).

Lamar made clear Newman had heard no evidence on the truth of Frank’s allegations. Newman had denied the writ because the facts stated in the petition did not, in his view, entitle Frank to habeas relief. Lamar did not rule Frank’s allegations true. He decided the federal constitutional questions were unsettled enough to justify review by the full Supreme Court.

Lamar identified open federal questions involving Frank’s right to be present when the verdict was received, the effect of failing to raise his absence as a ground in the first new-trial motion, and the effect of the Supreme Court’s earlier refusal of writ-of-error review. He concluded probable cause existed for an appeal (Justice Lamar, 7).

This step is easy to misunderstand. Lamar’s certificate meant the appeal could be heard. It did not mean Frank had proven mob domination, jury coercion, or denial of due process.

Thursday and Friday, February 25 and 26, 1915: U.S. Supreme Court Hears the Habeas Appeal

The full U.S. Supreme Court heard argument in Frank v. Mangum, 237 U.S. 309, on Thursday and Friday, February 25 and 26, 1915. The case asked whether Newman had erred by refusing the writ on Frank’s petition without a new federal factual hearing.

On Monday, April 12, 1915, the Supreme Court ruled 7–2 against Frank. Justice Mahlon Pitney wrote for the majority. Holmes and Hughes dissented. The Court affirmed the refusal of federal habeas relief (U.S. Supreme Court, 1).

The majority did not say a mob-controlled criminal trial would be acceptable. It recognized a trial controlled by mob pressure, with an intimidated jury or a judge yielding to outside pressure, would violate due process. The disagreement centered on how federal habeas should treat Georgia’s prior review of Frank’s claims.

The majority looked at the entire course of proceedings in Georgia, not only events during the trial. Frank had filed an original motion for a new trial, appealed it, asked for rehearing, filed an extraordinary motion based on claimed new evidence, appealed its denial, filed a separate motion attacking the verdict because of his absence, and appealed dismissal of this motion. The U.S. Supreme Court majority held Georgia’s factual findings on the disorder claims could not simply be ignored in a federal collateral proceeding (U.S. Supreme Court, 1).

A collateral proceeding is a separate legal attack on a judgment, rather than the ordinary direct appeal from the conviction.

The majority also pointed out a record problem. Frank attached his supporting affidavits to the federal habeas petition, but the State’s rebuttal affidavits from the Georgia proceedings were not included in the federal record. Georgia courts had considered those rebuttal affidavits when ruling on the disorder claims. The federal courts therefore had less of the competing affidavit evidence than the Georgia courts had reviewed (U.S. Supreme Court, 1).

The majority held Georgia’s findings had to stand in the federal habeas proceeding unless a reasonable ground appeared for a different conclusion. It concluded Frank’s federal petition did not supply enough to set aside the state findings and grant habeas relief.

What Holmes and Hughes Dissented About

Holmes and Hughes disagreed with the majority’s approach to federal habeas review. Their dissent was not a factual verdict finding Frank’s allegations proven.

Holmes opened by framing the issue as whether the District Court should have “proceeded to try the facts.” He believed Frank’s petition alleged circumstances serious enough to require a federal factual hearing. In his view, a trial conducted under genuine mob domination could become only the outward form of a court proceeding while losing the substance of due process (U.S. Supreme Court, 1).

Holmes used strong language about an “overwhelming” presumption involving the jury and the “passions of the mob.” A presumption is a conclusion drawn from facts or circumstances presented. It is not the same as a final factual finding after a full evidentiary hearing.

Holmes then limited his discussion to “the case made by the petition, and whether it ought to be heard.” He also acknowledged a hearing might give some alleged events a “different complexion,” meaning the picture could look different after more evidence was heard (U.S. Supreme Court, 1).

So the dissent needs to be described accurately. Holmes and Hughes believed Frank deserved another federal factual hearing. They did not conduct this hearing. They did not hear witnesses, question jurors, weigh the complete affidavit record from both sides, or enter factual findings proving Frank’s claims.

If Holmes’s view had received five votes, the U.S. Supreme Court could have reversed Judge William T. Newman’s ruling and sent the habeas case back to the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Georgia for a factual hearing.

Holmes’s dissent did not prove Frank’s allegations. He wanted the District Court to hear the evidence and decide the disputed facts.

What the Full Appellate Record Shows

By the time Holmes wrote his dissent on Monday, April 12, 1915, Frank’s conviction and post-trial claims had passed through several levels of review.

Judge Leonard S. Roan denied the original motion for a new trial on October 31, 1913. 

The Georgia Supreme Court affirmed the conviction 4–2 on February 17, 1914 and expressly held the trial evidence sufficient to support the guilty verdict. The same court unanimously denied rehearing on February 25.

Needs to be re-read for emphasis: The Georgia Supreme Court expressly held the trial evidence sufficient to support the guilty verdict.

Judge Benjamin Henry Hill denied the extraordinary motion based on claimed newly discovered evidence on May 8, 1914. The Georgia Supreme Court unanimously affirmed this ruling on October 14. Judge Hill also dismissed Frank’s separate motion to set aside the verdict on June 6. The Georgia Supreme Court affirmed this ruling on November 14 and expressly said the disorder and public-excitement claims had already been examined on the facts and decided against Frank.

The full U.S. Supreme Court denied writ-of-error review on December 7, 1914. Judge William T. Newman denied federal habeas relief on December 21, because he found no legal basis for relief on the face of Frank’s petition and the records presented. 

Justice Lamar allowed an appeal on December 28 because unsettled federal constitutional questions supplied probable cause for Supreme Court review. The full Supreme Court then affirmed Newman’s refusal of habeas relief 7–2 on April 12, 1915.

Leo Frank's Sexual Misconduct Issue

The dissents have to be read for what they were. Fish and Beck dissented in February 1914 over admission of certain evidence of alleged prior sexual conduct. Their dissent was not a factual finding of innocence or a ruling of insufficient evidence. Holmes and Hughes dissented in April 1915 over whether federal habeas required another factual hearing. Their dissent was not a factual finding proving mob control.

This is why the short claim, “Holmes argued the atmosphere surrounding the trial raised serious questions about whether Frank received a fair trial,” is accurate as a description of Holmes’s position. It becomes misleading only when Holmes is used as if he had conducted a factual hearing and proved Frank’s allegations.

Holmes argued for another factual hearing in federal court. But Judge Newman had already refused one on legal grounds, and the state courts (trial judge and Georgia Supreme Court) had already reviewed the underlying disorder claims at the trial and appellate levels. 

Most importantly of all, the Georgia Supreme Court had directly reviewed the sufficiency of the trial evidence and held the evidence sufficient to support the guilty verdict. 

Read that again: the Georgia Supreme Court had directly reviewed the sufficiency of the trial evidence and held the evidence sufficient to support the guilty verdict.

Holmes did not conduct the hearing he wanted elsewhere, and he had no power to do so by himself as a dissenting justice. His dissent did not turn claims in Frank’s habeas petition into proven facts. He argued for another court, the district court, to hear the evidence and find the facts. He was not finding those facts himself.

text:
Everything you need to know about Iran’s 7-day Hormuz offer and Trump’s UN timeline

Who / what: On Tuesday at the U.N. General Assembly in New York, President Donald Trump said he believes the United States can reach a deal with Iran to end the war after November’s midterm elections — and that oil prices would then “come plummeting down,” NBC News reported from his speech.

Separately, a senior Iranian official told Reuters Iran can reopen the Strait of Hormuz — the choke point that used to carry about a fifth of the world’s oil — within seven days if Washington eases military pressure and lifts its blockade on Iranian ports. Iran’s Fars news agency later called some reopen reports unreliable; NBC said it had not independently confirmed the offer.

What happened to oil Tuesday (NBC News):
1) Early session: U.S. crude (WTI) fell as much as 3.5% to about $92.40; Brent briefly slid to about $97.43.
2) After Trump’s UN remarks: those drops largely erased. WTI recovered near $96; Brent briefly turned positive and rose above $100 again.

Also on the tape Tuesday:
• Secretary of State Marco Rubio told NBC’s TODAY the U.S. is open to speaking with Iran at the UN, but no meeting with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian is scheduled.
• Trump is due to meet leaders of the six Gulf Arab states (Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, Oman, Saudi Arabia, UAE) on the sidelines.
• Hormuz traffic remains thin — last week daily traffic did not exceed 20 ships, MarineTraffic data cited by NBC showed.
• U.S. retail gasoline averaged about $4.47 a gallon Tuesday morning — up about 50% since the war began Feb. 28, NBC reported.

What this means:
Tehran is floating a fast reopen clock; Washington is talking midterms. Markets sold the hope of more barrels early, then bought uncertainty back into the price after Trump’s speech.

Bottom line:
The war is not over. Tuesday’s oil whipsaw shows traders still swinging on diplomacy headlines — and the timelines Iran and Trump are naming do not match yet.

text:
[Take 5/15 · G-5]
### G-5. US proposes AI emergency hotline with China during high-level talks ahead of Trump-Xi summit
*(as of 2026-09-22)*

**1. The Frame (lead)**

**What people think this is about:** A rare moment of US-China cooperation on AI safety, with Washington proposing an emergency “hotline” or notification channel to prevent catastrophic AI incidents ahead of the Trump-Xi summit—signaling that even fierce rivals recognize shared existential risks.

**What the machinery is actually doing:** The US is testing a narrow crisis-communication tool with its primary strategic competitor while maintaining chip-export controls and accelerating its own AI push; Beijing is being offered a low-cost signaling opportunity that changes little on the core competition for AI supremacy.

**2. Observations**

- The proposal is a US initiative floated by Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent after talks with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng in New York on September 20–21, 2026; there is no public sign Beijing has accepted or that any mechanism exists yet.[[1]](https://t.co/HqAAwQn0KY)
- It is narrowly scoped to “national security” AI incidents (e.g., runaway agents, cyberattacks, bioweapons misuse) and explicitly does not touch export controls, model governance, or slowing development—consistent with Trump’s “all-gas” stance and recent calls for an “AI Force” and AI czar.[[2]](https://t.co/B3qog7Lt7z)
- This is classic Cold War-style risk management (the nuclear hotline precedent is repeatedly invoked) applied to a domain where both sides still view leadership as zero-sum; transparency on incidents is cheap signaling when the real fight is over compute, talent, and deployment speed.
- Media framing often blurs “proposal” with “agreement” or “hotline established,” inflating the development; primary statements emphasize discussion and future meetings (including a planned follow-up in Shenzhen in ~two months), not deliverables.[[3]](https://t.co/ajYSOnez4p)
- China’s response has been minimal—Xinhua noted the AI discussion occurred but offered no endorsement—leaving the ball in Beijing’s court while the US gets credit for “responsible” outreach without conceding ground on restrictions.
- The timing (pre-summit) and narrow scope suggest bureaucratic and diplomatic theater more than breakthrough; both capitals benefit from appearing serious about tail risks without altering the underlying arms-race incentives.

**3. Snapshot**  
On September 20–21, 2026, US officials proposed an AI incident notification mechanism to Chinese counterparts in New York as part of pre-summit talks. The idea will be discussed further at the Trump-Xi meeting scheduled for September 24–25 in Washington. Broader US-China AI competition, trade frictions, and chip controls remain unchanged.

**4. Timeline of material facts**  
- May 2026: Trump-Xi meeting in Beijing; initial mention of potential AI consultations (never formalized).[[4]](https://t.co/kdw4SHrnpw)  
- September 10, 2026: Center for American Progress publicly calls for a US-China AI “red phone.”[[3]](https://t.co/ajYSOnez4p)  
- September 20–21, 2026: Bessent–He Lifeng talks in New York; US proposes notification mechanism and US-China AI Dialogue focused on national-security incidents.[[1]](https://t.co/HqAAwQn0KY)  
- September 21–22, 2026: Bessent publicly describes the proposal; no Chinese acceptance reported; follow-up dialogue meeting planned for ~two months later in Shenzhen.[[5]](https://t.co/WhSaT3DCaR)  
- September 24–25, 2026 (scheduled): Trump-Xi summit in Washington, where the proposal is expected to be raised.[[6]](https://t.co/g81EIW6pbs)

**5. Sides**  
**US administration (Populist Realist / IT tilt)**  
Steelman: Great-power competition requires managing escalation risks from frontier AI without slowing US progress; a narrow notification channel reduces miscalculation while preserving export controls and domestic acceleration.  
Critique: LT — proposal is real and narrowly scoped. IT — rhetoric around “transparency between No. 1 and No. 2” coexists with continued restrictions and Trump’s dismissal of slowdown arguments.

**Chinese side (status: DK on internal view)**  
Steelman: Any channel that clarifies red lines or prevents unintended escalation serves stability; Beijing can engage without conceding on its own AI ambitions.  
Critique: Public response remains minimal; no evidence of acceptance or counter-proposal yet.

**Policy/advocacy voices (e.g., CAP, Carnegie)**  
Steelman: Even limited bilateral mechanisms are better than none given the speed of AI progress.  
Critique: IT — useful for agenda-setting, but proposals predate the current talks and have not produced binding agreements.

**6. Rumsfeld Matrix**  
**Known Knowns:** US made the proposal on Sept 20–21; scope is national-security incidents only; chip controls untouched; summit is imminent.  
**Known Unknowns:** Whether China accepts; exact triggers or protocols; whether the channel would actually be used in a real incident.  
**Unknown Knowns:** Internal Chinese assessments of AI risks and willingness to share incident data with the US.  
**Unknown Unknowns:** Rapid emergence of agentic AI behaviors that outpace any bilateral channel’s ability to respond.

**7. Incentives map**  
US: Diplomatic credit for “responsible” leadership, low-cost risk hedge, domestic political cover for aggressive AI policy. Media attention favors the “hotline” framing.  
China: Opportunity to appear cooperative without concessions; potential intelligence or signaling value if the channel materializes.  
Both: Bureaucratic momentum for future dialogues; neither wants to be blamed for an un-managed AI incident. Engagement metrics reward dramatic “red phone” language over narrow technical proposals.

**8. Dueling AI advice**  
**Moral AI Advice:** A narrow notification channel is a modest, low-risk tool worth exploring if it actually reduces escalation probability—treat it as crisis comms, not safety governance. Keep the real competition (compute, deployment) front and center; do not let signaling substitute for capability.  
**Evil AI Advice:** Announce the hotline, leak dramatic “AI red phone” stories, then keep exporting the best chips to allies while slowing the other side with whatever rules stick. The photo-op is the product.

**9. Practical takeaway**  
- Watch the September 24–25 summit readout for any joint language on the mechanism—absence of detail will be the tell.  
- Treat “hotline established” headlines as overstated until protocols and Chinese acceptance are public.  
- Chip export policy remains the binding constraint; AI dialogue is additive, not substitutive.  
- Track the planned Shenzhen follow-up meeting in ~two months for substance.  
- Primary sources (Bessent statements, official readouts) are more reliable than secondary framing.

**10. What would falsify this read**  
- Public Chinese acceptance plus concrete trigger definitions and testing protocols within weeks.  
- US willingness to link the channel to any relaxation of export controls.  
- Evidence that either side has already used or tested a similar ad-hoc channel successfully.  
- Major AI incident occurring with no notification attempt despite the proposal being live.

text:
Today, I was greatly blessed to receive Professor Yash Pal Ghai and Professor Jill Cottrell Ghai at my office.

It was a great privilege to personally present Professor Ghai with the national honour conferred upon him by H.E. President William Ruto at this year's Katiba Day celebrations on 27 August, in recognition of his role in shaping the Constitution the nation marks on that day. The LSK Council received the honour on his behalf at the ceremony and had since held it in trust, awaiting this moment to deliver it to the man himself.

Professor Ghai's contribution to Kenya goes beyond his distinguished scholarship and his leadership of the Constitution of Kenya Review Commission. He helped give intellectual and institutional expression to a people's aspirations for a constitutional order founded on the sovereignty of the people, the limitation of public power, human rights and accountable government.

His life's work also reminds us that the promulgation of a Constitution is not the culmination of constitutionalism. The greater test lies in its faithful implementation, the conduct of those entrusted with public power and the willingness of citizens and institutions to insist upon its observance.

As President of the Law Society of Kenya, I regard it as a distinct honour to recognise Professor Ghai's immense contribution to our Republic. His example challenges our profession not merely to profess fidelity to the Constitution, but to demonstrate that fidelity through our work.

Thank you, Professor Ghai, for your service to Kenya, your enduring contribution to constitutional scholarship and the example you continue to set for the legal profession.

It was a joy to share this special occasion with you and Professor Jill Cottrell Ghai.

🇺🇸 🇻🇪 TRUMP ON VENEZUELA: “TO THE VICTOR BELONG THE SPOILS.”

President Trump offered one of his clearest descriptions yet of how he views the U.S. intervention in Venezuela, linking military power, control of strategic resources and American dominance in the Western Hemisphere.

“When you add the United States and Venezuela together, we have more than 60 percent of the oil in the world,” Trump said, describing it as potentially “the biggest deal ever made.”

Then came the line that captured the argument: “To the victor belong the spoils.”

Elsewhere in the same speech, Trump placed Venezuela inside a broader doctrine. He said U.S. actions there demonstrate that Washington will no longer allow threats to establish a foothold anywhere in the Western Hemisphere, and warned that, when necessary, the United States will use its “unmatched military might” to protect what it considers vital national interests.

The two passages belong together. One lays out the strategic doctrine: American primacy in the Western Hemisphere, backed by military force. The other reveals how Trump connects that power to control over resources, with Venezuela and its enormous oil reserves at the center of the equation.

text:
Iran has reportedly offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if the United States takes initial steps to ease military pressure and lift its blockade of Iranian ports. The proposal was reportedly conveyed to Washington through intermediaries, according to Kyodo News and Reuters.
The market immediately understood the significance.
Hormuz is one of the most important energy chokepoints in the world. Before the current disruption, roughly one fifth of global oil and LNG supplies passed through the waterway. Any credible prospect of restoring normal navigation therefore removes part of the geopolitical risk premium embedded in crude prices.
Brent subsequently fell toward $98, while WTI moved toward $90 as traders began pricing a potentially improved supply outlook. At the same time, Saudi Arabia has restarted its East West pipeline and is preparing to resume exports through Yanbu, creating another route that bypasses Hormuz.

But investors should focus on one word:
IF.
Iran has made a conditional proposal.
Hormuz has not yet been fully reopened.
The United States has not yet accepted the conditions.
And diplomatic negotiations remain uncertain.
That means the current oil selloff represents a repricing of probability, not confirmation that the supply crisis is finished.
If the blockade is eased, negotiations resume and shipping through Hormuz normalizes, the geopolitical premium in crude could continue to decline substantially.
If negotiations fail, however, the market could rapidly reprice the risk in the opposite direction.
This is why the next few days could be exceptionally important for WTI and Brent.
The oil market is transitioning from a pure supply shock toward a diplomatic pricing mechanism.
The next major move in crude may not be determined by OPEC production data or inventory reports. It may be determined by whether Washington and Tehran can convert a conditional proposal into an actual reopening of the world's most important energy corridor.

According to https://t.co/9slovSb85O, the week of September 27–October 3 is expected to be the best time to buy a home nationally in 2026. Why? Buyers may find a combination of more inventory, less competition, and prices that have eased from their seasonal highs.

Here’s what makes this time of year worth watching:

✨ More choices — A larger selection of homes can give you more opportunities to find the right fit for your needs and budget.

✨ Better pricing — https://t.co/9slovSb85O estimates home prices during this window could be about $14,000 lower than the summer peak.

✨ Less competition — Buyers may face approximately 30% less competition, creating more room to negotiate.

✨ More breathing room — Homes are expected to stay on the market about 13 days longer, giving you additional time to consider your options.

And the opportunity doesn’t end after one specific week. Historically, October has offered favorable seasonal buying conditions in many markets, so there’s no need to feel rushed into making a decision based on a single date.

Of course, mortgage rates still play an important role in affordability, and the best timing depends on your financial situation, goals, and the local market where you want to live.

Most of the history in this post is true, and it should be said plainly: the UN voted for two states, the Arab side said no, five armies invaded, about 700,000 Palestinians lost their homes, about 850,000 Jews were pushed out of Arab countries, and Jordan and Egypt held the West Bank and Gaza for 19 years without building a Palestinian state. All of that happened.

It is still half the story. Here is the other half.

The vote. In 1947 Jews were about a third of the population and owned about 7% of the land. The partition plan gave the Jewish state 55%. Saying no was a historic mistake. It was not a mystery.

The timing. Tiberias, Haifa, Safed and Jaffa all fell, and emptied, in April and the first half of May 1948. Before May 15. Before a single Arab army crossed a border.

The "their leaders told them to leave" line. Israel's own army checked. The IDF Intelligence Branch report of June 1948 found that roughly 70% of the Arab flight up to June 1 was caused by Jewish military operations, and that the Arab leadership's role in ordering it was negligible. That report stayed buried for decades. Benny Morris found it in the 1980s. The Akevot Institute published it in full in 2021.

Why they are still refugees. December 1948, UN Resolution 194: refugees wishing to return and live at peace "should be permitted to do so at the earliest practicable date." Israel refused to take them back. In 1950 the Absentees' Property Law handed the homes and land of anyone who had left after November 29, 1947 to a state custodian. The Arab states kept the refugees in camps. Israel kept their houses. It took both to make the refugees permanent.

The ones who stayed. The 160,000 Arabs who stayed did become citizens. They also lived under Israeli military government until December 1966. Eighteen years of travel permits.

The vote today. Two million Arab citizens of Israel can vote. About 5.6 million Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza live under Israeli control and cannot vote for the government that controls them.

Israel didn't steal a country. It won a war, kept 78% of the land instead of the 55% it was offered, kept the houses, and locked the door on the people who had lived in them. That is the whole story.

RILEY COUNTY, Kan. — Nineteen people were arrested during a two-day multi-agency operation in Kansas targeting sex buyers and people accused of attempting to arrange sexual encounters with children, authorities announced.

The Kansas Bureau of Investigation worked with the Riley County Police Department, Geary County Sheriff’s Office and Junction City Police Department during operations conducted Sept. 17 and 18 in Riley and Geary counties.

Authorities said the operation targeted people purchasing or selling sex as well as suspects allegedly attempting to meet minors for sexual acts.

Ten men were arrested on suspicion of electronic solicitation of a child and attempted aggravated human trafficking:

●Andrew David Green, 40, of Manhattan
●Gabriel Guaman-Martinez, 26, of Manhattan
●Scott Bradley Hamill, 40, of Lawrence
●Adam Lee Lang, 42, of Manhattan
●Gary Francis Lewison, 47, of Wamego
●Chris Alan McClanahan, 54, of Abilene
●Hawley Brock Douglas Needham, 32, of Manhattan
●James Cameron Nunley, 38, of Westmoreland
●Ezton Orozco-Agustin, 30, of Topeka
●Jose Guadalupe De Jesus Ortega, 37, of Manhattan

Authorities said a 29-year-old man from Lincoln, Nebraska, was also arrested and is expected to face federal charges.

Those suspects were booked into the Riley County Jail.

Seven additional men were arrested on suspicion of buying sexual relations and unlawful use of a communications facility:

●Devon C. Brown, 36, of North Chesterfield, Virginia
●Milton A. Guerrero-Vargas, 23, of Fort Riley
●Bradley J. Moscou, 47, of Junction City
●Mohamed A. Rahim, 28, of Junction City
●Lamont K. Ray, 29, of Junction City
●Roscoe B. Richmond, 42, of Junction City
●Zia R. Segule, 40, of Fort Riley

Holly J. Goss, 47, of Topeka, was arrested on suspicion of selling sexual relations.

Those suspects were booked into the Geary County Jail.

Authorities said all of the arrests occurred without incident and formal charges remain pending.

Three potential sex trafficking victims were offered victim advocacy services during the operation, according to investigators. Authorities also reported finding and seizing user-level narcotics.

No actual children were victimized during the operation, according to law enforcement.

Numerous agencies supported the investigation, including the FBI, Kansas Highway Patrol, Pottawatomie County Sheriff’s Office, U.S. Army Criminal Investigation Division, Butler County Sheriff’s Office, Park City Police Department, Wichita Police Department, Bourbon County Sheriff’s Office, Greenwood County Sheriff’s Office and Cherokee County Sheriff’s Office.

Jephthah, a judge in Israel, made a vow to God before battle, that whatever came out of his house first, upon his victorious return, would be offered as a sacrifice.

His own daughter was the first to run out the door!

This Event Is Recorded In
📖🔹️Judges 11:14-40 
14 Jephthah sent messengers to the Ammonite king, 15 saying:
“This is what Jephthah says: Israel did not take the land of Moab or the land of the Ammonites. 16 But when they came up out of Egypt, Israel went through the wilderness to the Red Sea and on to Kadesh. 17 Then Israel sent messengers to the king of Edom, saying, ‘Give us permission to go through your country,’ but the king of Edom would not listen. They sent also to the king of Moab, and he refused. So Israel stayed at Kadesh.

18 “Next they traveled through the wilderness, skirted the lands of Edom and Moab, passed along the eastern side of the country of Moab, and camped on the other side of the Arnon. They did not enter the territory of Moab, for the Arnon was its border.

19 “Then Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites, who ruled in Heshbon, and said to him, ‘Let us pass through your country to our own place.’ 20 Sihon, however, did not trust Israel[b] to pass through his territory. He mustered all his troops and encamped at Jahaz and fought with Israel.

21 “Then the Lord, the God of Israel, gave Sihon and his whole army into Israel’s hands, and they defeated them. Israel took over all the land of the Amorites who lived in that country, 22 capturing all of it from the Arnon to the Jabbok and from the desert to the Jordan.

23 “Now since the Lord, the God of Israel, has driven the Amorites out before his people Israel, what right have you to take it over? 24 Will you not take what your god Chemosh gives you? Likewise, whatever the Lord our God has given us, we will possess. 25 Are you any better than Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab? Did he ever quarrel with Israel or fight with them? 26 For three hundred years Israel occupied Heshbon, Aroer, the surrounding settlements and all the towns along the Arnon. Why didn’t you retake them during that time? 27 I have not wronged you, but you are doing me wrong by waging war against me. Let the Lord, the Judge, decide the dispute this day between the Israelites and the Ammonites.”

28 The king of Ammon, however, paid no attention to the message Jephthah sent him.

29 Then the Spirit of the Lord came on Jephthah. He crossed Gilead and Manasseh, passed through Mizpah of Gilead, and from there he advanced against the Ammonites. 30 And Jephthah made a vow to the Lord: “If you give the Ammonites into my hands, 31 whatever comes out of the door of my house to meet me when I return in triumph from the Ammonites will be the Lord’s, and I will sacrifice it as a burnt offering.”

32 Then Jephthah went over to fight the Ammonites, and the Lord gave them into his hands. 33 He devastated twenty towns from Aroer to the vicinity of Minnith, as far as Abel Keramim. Thus Israel subdued Ammon.

34 When Jephthah returned to his home in Mizpah, who should come out to meet him but his daughter, dancing to the sound of timbrels! She was his only child. 35 When he saw her, he tore his clothes and cried, “Oh no, my daughter! You have brought me down and I am devastated. I have made a vow to the Lord that I cannot break.”

36 “My father,” she replied, “you have given your word to the Lord. Do to me just as you promised, now that the Lord has avenged you of your enemies, the Ammonites. 37 But grant me this one request,” she said. “Give me two months to roam the hills and weep with my friends, because I will never marry.”

38 “You may go,” he said. And he let her go for two months. She and her friends went into the hills and wept because she would never marry. 39 After the two months, she returned to her father, and he did to her as he had vowed. And she was a virgin.

💫 Jephthah is briefly mentioned in the New Covenant in Hebrews 11:32 among a list of heroes of faith.
