text:
An emerging story behind this water color by a student studying architecture at Urbana-Champaign in 1948.

This watercolor (and the preparatory pencil sketch on the back)  by architectural student Joseph Jerome "Joe" Oshiver (1922–2016), is dated October 22, 1948 and it  offers a rare look at the cross-disciplinary studio education defining the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (UIUC) during its legendary post-war boom.  This still life is a physical case study of how mid-century campus politics, institutional design standards, and the explosive avant-garde environment of 1948 intersected in Chicago's fine art community of the day.

The back of the drawing features a prominent blue ink stamp reading: "UNIVERSITY OF ILLINOIS — OCT 22 1948 — TEST — DEPT. OF ART."  This artifact provides a critical insight into the structural crossover of the departments under Dean Rexford Newcomb's College of Fine and Applied Arts.   At UIUC, architecture was intentionally nested alongside fine painting, industrial design, and landscape layout. Architecture students did not merely take engineering and drafting courses; they were funneled directly through the Department of Art for timed, practical studio tests to master freehand spatial rendering, perspective, and color application.  Oshiver’s watercolor was not a leisurely hobby piece—it was a high-stakes, timed institutional examination designed to grade his physical speed and architectural eye under pressure.

text:
The Subversion of American Institutions and the Reality of Freedom

Academic Subversion, Political Realignment, and the Cuban Reality

Wednesday, September 23, 2026
Dr. Joel P. Rutkowski
Policy Analysis

Executive Summary

The enduring axiom, "Communism will never come to America—but freedom will come to Cuba",
(https://t.co/oFUlQgdoaA) encapsulates a profound geopolitical and domestic truth. While the United States is structurally insulated from a violent, Bolshevik-style overthrow, it is currently grappling with a sophisticated ideological subversion. Over the last several decades, Marxist methodologies—repackaged as Critical Theory and identity politics—have profoundly transformed American university curricula.

This academic capture has not remained confined to the ivory tower; it has metastasized into the legislative and regulatory frameworks of the progressive wing of the Democratic Party. By shifting the goalposts from "equality of opportunity" to "equity of outcome," this ideological alignment seeks to fundamentally restructure the American economic and legal systems. Grounded in foundational conservative principles—such as individual liberty, limited government, free-enterprise capitalism, and the rule of law—this paper examines the mechanics of this curricular transformation, its translation into Democratic policy, and the stark contrast provided by the ongoing, tragic reality of the Cuban communist experiment.

Part I: The Transformation of University Curricula

The transformation of American higher education did not happen by accident. It is the result of a generational project to replace classical liberal education—rooted in the pursuit of objective truth, the Western canon, and individual merit—with a pedagogy centered on power dynamics, grievance, and systemic deconstruction.

1. The Erasure of the Canon and the Rise of Critical Pedagogy

Beginning in the late 1980s, universities systematically dismantled core curricula that centered on Western civilization. In its place, faculties adopted Critical Pedagogy (heavily influenced by Marxist educational theorist Paulo Freire) and Critical Race Theory (CRT).

The Paradigm Shift: Education was no longer viewed as a means to impart knowledge or develop independent civic virtues, but as a tool for "consciousness-raising" and political liberation.
Epistemological Relativism: Curricula across the humanities and social sciences began to teach that concepts such as meritocracy, the scientific method, and objective truth are merely "social constructs" designed by dominant groups to maintain power.

2. The Weaponization of University Administration and Accreditation

The ideological shift in the classroom was cemented by the explosive growth of university bureaucracies.
The DEI Apparatus: Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) bureaucracies act essentially as ideological enforcers. By requiring mandatory "diversity statements" for faculty hiring and promotion, these offices have effectively instituted political litmus tests that weed out conservative, libertarian, and classical liberal scholars.

Accreditation Capture: Moving into the 2024–2026 period, conservative reformers have rightly identified that institutional accreditors have often mandated DEI compliance as a condition for university accreditation, forcing even historically moderate or religious institutions to adopt radical frameworks to maintain access to federal student aid.

3. Downstream Effects: The Capture of K-12 Education
The most dangerous consequence of higher education's ideological drift is its impact on teacher training colleges. Graduate schools of education—such as Columbia’s Teachers College—have integrated radical theories into the core training of future K-12 administrators and teachers. Consequently, the civic education of American youth has increasingly shifted from instilling patriotism and constitutional literacy to promoting guilt, historical revisionism, and hyper-racialization.

Part II: The Policy Trajectory of the Democratic Party

As generations of students graduated from these ideologically unified universities, they entered the media, corporate America, and politics. Over the last two decades, the intellectual outputs of the academy have become the explicit policy inputs of the Democratic Party’s progressive base.

1. The Redefinition of Civil Rights: Equality v. Equity

The traditional liberal civil rights framework of the 1960s—championed by figures like John F. Kennedy and Martin Luther King Jr.—sought colorblind equality of opportunity. Today, influenced by academic critical theory, the progressive left pursues "Equity."

Policy Reality: Equity demands equal outcomes. When applied to public policy, this requires the state to actively discriminate to balance demographic ledgers. This is evident in proposals for race-based reparations, the targeted cancellation of student loan debt, and attempts to embed "disparate impact" theories into federal regulatory enforcement to mandate racial parity in lending, housing, and school discipline.

2. Economic Radicalism and State Direction

While the Democratic Party retains moderate factions, its center of gravity has been pulled toward democratic socialism. Traditional Marxist economics have been modernized for the 21st  century:

Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG): Progressives have attempted to bypass the legislative process by using financial regulators and massive asset managers to choke off capital to traditional energy sectors and enforce social quotas on corporate boards.

The Green New Deal & Wealth Redistribution: Framed as an environmental imperative, policies like the Green New Deal are fundamentally massive state-directed economic overhauls that seek to centralize industrial planning and impose punitive wealth taxes on private capital.

3. Judicial and Legal Deconstruction

Academic "Critical Legal Studies" teaches that the law is not a neutral arbiter of justice, but a tool of class and racial oppression. This theory has manifested in Democratic policy through:

Progressive Prosecutors: The election of local district attorneys who refuse to prosecute entire categories of property and public-order crimes, leading to urban decay.

Institutional Attacks: Escalating rhetoric aimed at packing the Supreme Court or abolishing the electoral college whenever constitutional guardrails impede radical legislative agendas.

Part III: The Cuban Reality — A Warning to the West
While affluent American students debate the virtues of socialism in taxpayer-subsidized lecture halls, the tragic reality of applied Marxism is playing out 90 miles off the coast of Florida.

1. The Enduring Failure of 1959

For nearly seven decades, the Cuban regime has served as a laboratory for the exact economic and social centralization advocated by academic Marxists. The results are undeniable: complete economic collapse, the annihilation of civil society, and catastrophic poverty.

Current Crisis (2024–2026): Cuba is currently experiencing unprecedented economic despair, characterized by widespread starvation, rolling blackouts, and infrastructural collapse. This has sparked major protests across the island—from the historic July 11 (11J) uprisings to ongoing 2025 and 2026 demonstrations against the dictatorship of Miguel Díaz-Canel.

2. The Totalitarian Inevitability

The Cuban experience proves a core conservative truth: You cannot centrally plan an economy without centrally planning the people. The utopian promises of free healthcare and equitable wealth distribution in Cuba quickly devolved into the systemic persecution of political dissidents, the suppression of religious freedom, and the imprisonment of hundreds of peaceful protesters.

The contrast is stark: The American constitutional republic diffuses power to protect the individual, while the communist state concentrates power to enforce the collective, invariably resulting in tyranny.

Part IV: Strategic Policy Recommendations

To arrest the institutional march of radical ideology and support the ultimate liberation of captive nations, the U.S. must adopt a robust, conservative policy framework rooted in bedrock principles of individual liberty, limited government, and national sovereignty.

Dismantle the Higher Education Cartel:

Accreditation Reform: Congress and the Department of Education must strip the monopoly power of regional accreditors that use their gatekeeping authority to mandate DEI compliance.

Protect Title VI: Ensure that federal funding is withheld from universities that violate the Civil Rights Act by enforcing race-based hiring, admissions, or racially segregated campus events.

Legislative Guardrails Against Administrative Overreach:

Codify the Prohibition of Mandatory Equity: Outlaw "disparate impact" compliance mandates in federal contracting and hiring, upholding the conservative principle of absolute colorblind equality under the law.

Defund Ideological Bureaucracies: Remove federal funding from bureaucratic offices that explicitly promote critical race theory or gender ideology over merit and constitutional equality.

Unflinching Foreign Policy on Cuba:
Maximum Pressure: The United States must reject any appeasement of the Cuban regime. 

Washington must maintain targeted economic sanctions against the Cuban military and intelligence apparatus.

Information Warfare: The U.S. should actively provide satellite internet and technological workarounds to the Cuban people to bypass state censorship, allowing them to organize and expose the regime's human rights abuses to the world.

Conclusion and Final Thoughts: Defending the Republic Against Soft Subversion and Totalitarian Twilight

The Synthesis of Institutional Drift and Ideological Realities

The trajectory of this comprehensive analysis—from the structural capture of American universities to its downstream manifestation in progressive Democratic policy, contrasted against the brutal reality of the Cuban experiment—leads to an inescapable conclusion. The greatest threat to the American constitutional order does not currently present itself as an armed insurrection or a sudden violent revolution. Instead, it is a slow, methodical ideological colonization of the institutions that shape the minds, laws, and economic architecture of the nation.

As demonstrated through the intellectual genealogy of Western Marxism and Critical Theory, the shift from economic determinism to cultural hegemony allowed radical leftist doctrines to bypass the traditional working class and embed themselves deep within the ivory tower. Universities, originally designed as temples of open inquiry, the pursuit of objective truth, and the transmission of the Western canon, were systematically converted into bureaucratic incubators of grievance. By replacing colorblind equality of opportunity with equity-of-outcome mandates, identity politics, and systemic deconstruction, these institutions have successfully minted generations of activists, administrators, and policy architects who now populate the upper echelons of corporate governance, media, and progressive politics.

Within the Democratic Party, this dynamic has created an ongoing ideological civil war. While the institutional party machinery retains anchors in traditional liberalism, the gravitational pull of the progressive base has steadily advanced state-directed economic interventions, regulatory overreaches, and identity-driven social engineering. When policy proposals bypass legislative debate through administrative fiat, Environmental, Social, and Governance-ESG financial mandates, or weaponized regulatory compliance, they mirror a soft, bureaucratic authoritarianism that is fundamentally at odds with classical liberal democracy and conservative governance.

The Axiom Revisited: Why the Republic Endures and Cuba Yearns

This brings us back to the foundational axiom governing this analysis: "Communism will never come to America—but freedom will come to Cuba."

The resilience of the American republic lies in its structural design. The United States was built upon a bedrock of Lockean philosophy and conservative principles: the sanctity of private property, the fragmentation of federal power, the rule of law, and an unyielding commitment to the sovereign individual over the collective state. These architectural guardrails make a literal, totalitarian communist takeover structurally impossible under our current constitutional framework. Americans possess an inherent, culturally ingrained skepticism of state power and an attachment to liberty that acts as a profound immune system against hard socialism.

Yet, an immune system can be weakened from within. The danger facing America is not that it will wake up transformed into a mirror image of the former Soviet Union, but that it will slowly erode its own intellectual and moral foundations until its constitutional freedoms are hollowed out. When free speech is suppressed under the guise of "safety," when merit is abandoned for ideological quotas, and when the rule of law is subverted by progressive prosecutorial discretion, the republic suffers death by a thousand cuts.

In stark contrast, the tragedy of Cuba serves as an enduring, empirical indictment of applied Marxist ideology. While affluent Western academics theorize about equity in air-conditioned lecture halls, the Cuban people continue to endure generations of institutionalized starvation, systemic oppression, and economic devastation under the weight of totalitarian central planning. The persistent, courageous protests of the Cuban populace—from historic uprisings to ongoing resistance against the Díaz-Canel regime—demonstrate that the human desire for freedom cannot be permanently extinguished by secret police or ideological indoctrination. It also affirms that totalitarian states are inherently fragile, unsustainable, and ultimately doomed to collapse.

Final Strategic Imperatives

To ensure that the axiom holds true—that America remains permanently insulated from terminal ideological decay, and that Cuba eventually breaks its chains of tyranny—policymakers, civic leaders, and citizens must act with unwavering resolve:

Restore Institutional Integrity: We must dismantle the ideological monopolies in higher education through legislative oversight, the elimination of mandatory diversity statements, and the defense of absolute intellectual pluralism. Academic freedom must be reclaimed from ideological compliance officers.

Defend the Rule of Law and Free Enterprise: We must forcefully reject equity-based social engineering, bureaucratic overreach, and economic central planning. Prosperity and justice are inextricably bound to individual merit, colorblind legal protections, and dynamic free markets.

Maintain Moral Clarity Abroad: U.S. foreign policy must never offer moral equivalence or economic lifelines to totalitarian regimes. By maintaining maximum pressure on communist dictatorships like Cuba and standing firmly with those fighting for liberty, America reaffirms its unique role as a beacon of hope for a free world.

Ultimately, freedom is never more than one generation away from extinction. It is not passed down in the bloodline; it must be fought for, protected, and actively taught. By confronting ideological subversion at home with intellectual courage and standing resolutely for liberty abroad, the United States can safeguard its own constitutional experiment and hasten the inevitable dawn when freedom finally comes to Cuba.

⬛️ The largest airports in the world by land area.

    1    @DammamAirports King Fahd International (DMM) – Saudi Arabia – ~300 sq mi / 776 km²

    2    @kingkhalid_j King Khalid International  (RUH) – Saudi Arabia – ~145 sq mi

    3    @DENAirport Denver International (DEN) – USA – ~53 sq mi

    4    Kuala Lumpur International  (KUL) – Malaysia – ~39 sq mi

    5    iGA Istanbul Airport (IST) – Türkiye – ~29.5 sq mi

    6    Dallas/Fort Worth (DFW) – USA – ~27 sq mi

    7    Southwest Florida (RSW) – USA – ~21 sq mi

    8    Orlando International (MCO) – USA – ~21 sq mi

    9    Washington Dulles (IAD) – USA – ~20 sq mi

    10    Beijing Daxing (PKX) – China – ~18 sq mi

These rankings measure pure physical footprint, not passenger numbers. The biggest sites often run at lower density, while compact hubs like Atlanta achieve far higher throughput on much less land.

Density, however, does not dictate landmass. 

A large footprint is frequently a deliberate choice, securing future flexibility, extra runways, cargo space and expansion room rather than maximising present utilisation. 

High density works when demand is already intense. Lower density on ample land is rational when the priority is long-term optionality.

This distinction matters for infrastructure-poor regions. Building capable airports ahead of fully realised traffic is not automatically vanity. 

Necessity is not always pre-recognised, policy often lags, and physical capacity can itself help create industrial, cargo and connectivity opportunities.

Ethiopia offers a live example. Addis Ababa Bole (ADD/HAAB) is approaching its expanded limits of around 22–25 million passengers with little room left to grow. 

The new Bishoftu International Airport (BIA), under construction since January 2026, is designed for an initial 60 million passengers by 2030 and an ultimate capacity of 110 million on a substantial greenfield site with multiple runways. 

It is a clear bet on future hub potential rather than current density alone. 

Sustaining that advantage across Ethiopia will also require capable secondary airports and supporting infrastructure so that capacity continues to outpace necessity rather than lag behind it.

Large land, lower initial density and future-ready standards can be a strategic developmental choice.

🇮🇳 How did India know Pakistan was preparing to strike - before the first bombs were dropped?

In November 1971, India received a crucial warning that Pakistan was preparing air strikes against Indian military bases.

The information reportedly came from within the Pakistani establishment.

India placed its Air Force on alert.

✈️ On December 3, Pakistan launched the strikes.

But India was ready.

Just 13 days later, Pakistani forces surrendered in Dhaka, and Bangladesh was born.

So, who helped get that warning to India?

The story leads to Rameshwar Nath Kao — R.N. Kao, the man who would build India’s external intelligence agency from the ground up.

Born in Benares in 1918, Kao cleared the Civil Services examination in 1940 and joined the Indian Imperial Police, the predecessor to the IPS.

After Independence, he was deputed to the Intelligence Bureau. The 1962 war with China exposed major gaps in India’s intelligence capabilities and strengthened the case for a dedicated external intelligence organisation.

🔹 Kao became part of that effort.

He headed the Aviation Research Centre and played a key role in strengthening India’s external intelligence capabilities.

In 1968, R&AW was created as India’s dedicated external intelligence agency, with R.N. Kao as its first chief.

For nearly nine years, he built its organisational structure, developed intelligence networks and worked closely with the government on national security.

He later advised Indira Gandhi and Rajiv Gandhi and was associated with the establishment of the National Security Guard.

Much of his work remained behind the scenes.

But the warning before the 1971 war offers a glimpse of how intelligence gathered quietly can influence events long before history records them.

🎬 Now, Kao’s story is returning to public attention through Karan Johar’s upcoming film based on Nitin Gokhale’s book, R.N. Kao: Gentleman Spymaster.

text:
Grok is the above accurate to history:

No. The tweet mixes some accurate observations about Temple-era practice with significant historical inaccuracies, overstatements, and polemical framing.
What the biblical text actually requires
Leviticus 16 (and related passages in Leviticus 23 and Numbers 29) describes Yom Kippur as a day on which the high priest entered the Holy of Holies, offered specific sacrifices (a bull for himself and two goats—one sacrificed, one sent as the scapegoat to Azazel), sprinkled blood, and performed rites to purify the sanctuary and the people. The people were commanded to “afflict your souls” and do no work. That Temple-centered ritual could only be performed while the Temple and priesthood functioned. https://t.co/CwdTQ0TQp4 
Those specific rites ended when the Romans destroyed the Second Temple in 70 CE. Modern Jewish observance does not include a high priest entering the Holy of Holies, live animal sacrifice, or a scapegoat ritual. That part of the tweet is factually correct.
What was not invented around 200 AD
The holiday itself, its date (10 Tishrei), its name, the work prohibition, and the command to afflict oneself are in the Torah, not a 2nd–3rd century rabbinic invention. Fasting on the day is already attested while the Temple still stood:
•  Philo of Alexandria (early 1st century CE) describes Jews spending the day in fasting and prayer.
•  Josephus also refers to the fast.
•  A Dead Sea Scroll (Pesher Habakkuk, 2nd century BCE) contains an early reference to Yom Kippur as a day of affliction. https://t.co/KP9oblsvFK 
Synagogues and communal prayer existed before 70 CE. After the Temple’s destruction, Jewish practice shifted emphasis to repentance (teshuvah), prayer, confession, charity, and the biblical self-affliction (fasting plus additional restrictions later specified in the Mishnah). Rabbis explicitly justified this by citing prophetic texts such as Hosea (“we will offer the words of our lips instead of bulls”). The famous story of Rabbi Yochanan ben Zakkai after 70 CE frames acts of loving-kindness as an effective substitute for the lost Temple rites. https://t.co/CwdTQ0TQp4 
The Mishnah (compiled around 200 CE) and later Talmud preserve detailed memories of the Temple service and codify the post-Temple rules. That is development and adaptation after a catastrophe, not wholesale fabrication of a new holiday.
On “Pharisee Cult” and “not in the Christian Old Testament”
Pharisees were a real Second Temple-era group (mentioned in the New Testament). After 70 CE their approach—emphasizing Oral Torah, study, prayer, and synagogue—became the main surviving stream of Judaism because the priestly Temple system no longer existed. Calling it a “cult” that invented a fake holiday is rhetorical, not historical analysis.
The day, the date, fasting/self-affliction, and atonement language are in the Hebrew Bible / Christian Old Testament. What is absent today are the Temple rituals that required a standing Temple. Both Jewish and Christian traditions recognize that those rituals cannot currently be performed. Christianity interprets Jesus’ death and the Temple’s destruction as fulfilling or ending the sacrificial system (see the Epistle to the Hebrews); rabbinic Judaism interprets the same events as requiring a shift to prayer and repentance.
Bottom line
The tweet correctly notes that modern Yom Kippur lacks the Leviticus 16 Temple rites. It incorrectly presents the holiday as a 200 AD invention disconnected from the biblical day. The core observance (the date, fasting, seeking atonement) has continuity; the method changed because the Temple was gone. The rest of the language (“Temu-Hebrew,” “blasphemous stench,” Christmas costume analogy) is theological polemic, not a precise historical account

text:
Thiyaga Deepam Annan Thileepan shines in Tamil memory as the Lamp of Sacrifice a young soul who offered his own life so that the dream of Tamil Eelam might live.
Born Rasiah Parthipan on 29 November 1963 in the green village of Urelu near Urumpirai in Jaffna, he was the youngest son of a beloved schoolteacher. Gentle in speech, firm in purpose, he grew into a young man who loved his people with a quiet and complete devotion. The suffering of the Tamil nation touched him early. He joined the struggle for Tamil Eelam and took the name Thileepan a name that would one day be spoken with reverence across the Tamil homeland.
He served not only with courage in the field but with kindness among the people. After he was wounded in 1987 he became the political leader of Jaffna, a trusted voice who listened, explained, and stood close to ordinary families. When the Indo-Lanka Accord arrived, many hoped that justice for the Tamil people would finally dawn. When those hopes began to fade, Annan Thileepan chose the path of supreme non-violent sacrifice.
On 13 September 1987 he placed five just demands before India demands for the freedom of Tamil prisoners, an end to the colonisation of Tamil lands, a true interim administration, an end to new police stations in the north and east, and the protection of Tamil villages and schools. Two days later, on 15 September, he sat before the sacred Nallur Kandaswamy Temple. Tens of thousands gathered around him. He told them he was not fasting against the Indian people, but so that the pledges given to the Tamil nation would be honoured.
He refused food. He refused even a single drop of water. For twelve days the Lamp of Sacrifice burned before the eyes of his people. On the morning of 26 September 1987, at 10:48, at only twenty-three years of age, Annan Thileepan gave his life. His body was offered to the medical faculty of the University of Jaffna, a final gift of service.
He did not die in vain. His fast became a sacred flame in the heart of the Tamil Eelam struggle. Every September the people light lamps, lay flowers, and speak his name. They remember a brother who chose love of nation over his own breath.
The dream he carried a free, secure, and dignified Tamil Eelam still lives. The additional hope that now walks with his memory is bright and unshaken: that this sacred dream will be fulfilled soon, and that the light of Thiyaga Deepam Annan Thileepan will one day shine over the homeland he loved more than life itself.

text:
I'm a historian of Palestine. 

This post on the 1948 Palestine War is not history, it's propaganda replete with distortions & lies. Let's go through them one by one:

Myth #1: The Zionists "accepted the partition plan." This is false. The Zionist leadership in Palestine rejected the plan:

While the Jews of Palestine celebrated in public, Zionist leaders rejected the partition plan in private. Ben Gurion said as much in his diary: “Such a demographic balance [proposed by the plan in which the Jewish state would be only 55% Jewish] questions our ability to maintain Jewish sovereignty,” David Ben-Gurion argued in early December. “Only a state with at least 80% Jews is a viable and stable state,” he said. (Ilan Pappe, The Ethnic Cleansing of Palestine, 48). In other words, the Zionist leadership rejected the plan because it put too many Palestinians in the Jewish state.

The Zionist leadership was not just unsatisfied with the demographic balance, but also the borders. That’s why, from the earliest weeks of fighting, Jewish militias attacked & depopulated Palestinian neighborhoods, villages and cities in areas allocated to the Arab State, including Jaffa, Acre, the Western and Lower Galilee, the Jerusalem Corridor, the Judean Hills, the Latrun area and Jerusalem itself, designated as an international zone.

As Ben-Gurion put it in his diary in early December, “no such thing in history as a final arrangement— not with regard to the regime, not with regard to borders, and not with regard to international agreements,” a view he had been expressing for more than a decade (Simha Flapan the Birth of Israel, p.13, 23-4)  For the Zionist leadership, the borders proposed by the UN were not effectively irrelevant.

Myth #2: "the Arab side started the war." This is false.

Today, every Israel apologist will tell you “the Arabs” fired the first shot of the 1948 War, but that’s not how the violence was interpreted by the Zionist leadership at the time, nor is what historians believe today.

On November 20, 1947 a week before the Partition plan announcement, the Lehi gang, unprovoked, raided a house near Ra‘anana belonging to the Abu Kishk bedouin tribe & executed 5 men from the Shubaki family. 

Seif al-Din Abu Kishk carried out a revenge attack for the 20 November attack on November 30, the day after the announcement of the plan, ambushing a Jewish bus in the Coastal Plain near Kfar Syrkin, killing 5, and then carrying out another attack on a bus, southbound from Hadera, killing two more (Morris, 1948: A History, p.76). 

This is the incident that Zionists today love to point to -- yet it had nothing to do with the 1948 War, indeed, it was unrelated to it, as the Zionist history Benny Morris himself admits.

The organized Palestinian Arab response to the plan was not one of violence, but civil disobedience, a three-day general strike launched by the Arab Higher Committee, the closest thing to a political body representing the Palestinians. (Morris, 1948: A History, p.76). 

This came amidst sporadic mob attacks, shootings and gradually expanding clashes (ibid, 77-8) in which Arab fighters attacked Jewish supply lines, Jewish fighters attacked Palestinian neighborhoods, towns and villages. 

Myth #3: "The [Arab] goal was that there would be no Jewish state": 

The most capable Arab fighting force was the Jordanian army and they signed a mutual non-aggression pact with the Zionist movement before May 15, 1948. In fact, they recognized the Jewish State before it even came into existence. [Avi Shlaim, Collusion across the Jordan]

Another one of the Arab militias in Palestine led by Fawzi al-Qawuqji  began seeking a truce with the Zionists in January 1948, and continued through February and March 1948.  He tried to negotiate directly with the Zionist leadership. He offered a non-aggression pact that would keep the Jewish forces within the designated Jewish state. His proposals, needless to say, were rejected. (Pappe, The Ethnic Cleansing of Palestine, p.116). 

The opposite of what you said is correct. It was the Jewish goal that there would be no Arab state in Palestine.

Myth #4: "Israel was the underdog." [Or, as this writer puts it: "Israel had no real army and barely any weapons, and many of its soldiers were Holocaust survivors who had come ashore only months earlier. They won because the alternative was to die."

Israel had a military advantage over both the native Palestinian Arabs and the invading Arab armies. This is the unanimous consensus of every historian of the 1948. All of them. Cite me a historian who has written about the 1948, and I'll show you someone who agrees the Jewish forces had a clear military advantage. 

As per the holocaust survivors, indeed, the Zionist movement sent Hagannah officials into the Displaced Persons camps in Europe to transform refugees into ethnic cleansers, and, beginning in Nov. 1947, the Zionists imposed a conscription on all holocaust surviving men aged 18-35 in the camps. They were conscripted against their will and forced to serve in the army of a country that didn't exist yet. Many of them did not want to fight. (see: Yosef Grodzinsky, In the Shadow of the Holocaust: The Struggle Between Jews and Zionists in the Aftermath of World War II and Molly Crabapple, Here Where We Live Is Our Country)

Myth #5: "Some were told by their own leaders to leave their villages until the Arab armies had won." This is pure fiction. 

100% of the 750,000 Palestinian Arabs who became refugees during the 1948 were forcibly expelled by Israel. That's because none of them were allowed to return to their homes after the war.  if a country denies you the right to go to your home -- this is what we call in the english language, forcible expulsion. 

Myth #6: "The roughly 160,000 Arabs who stayed in Israel became Israeli citizens."

Actually, some 30,000-40,000 were expelled from Israel between 1949-1959 and the rest were subject to belligerent Israeli military occupation. 40-60% of the properties of these Palestinians who eventually became Israeli citizens was confiscated.  They needed to apply to the army to receive a permit to leave their village. On the 30,000-40,000 expelled, see https://t.co/1d4VqUjxvE on the belligerent military occupation see Shira Robinson, Citizen Strangers: Palestinians and the Birth of Israel's Liberal Settler State.

If you want to learn more about the history of Palestine from a historian rather than a genocide apologist, I offer courses on the history of Palestine here: https://t.co/SMV6pMrxEi

text:
The official video from the Prime Minister’s Office argues that the documentary NAZA is a manufactured smear.  Manufactured?

To justify this, the video claims that: anonymous, uncorroborated “soldiers” invent a story of deliberate civilian targeting; the IDF in fact records the lowest civilian-to-combatant ratio in the history of urban warfare; Hamas’s embedding and tunnels explain the deaths; and the army’s warning systems, abort procedures, and human oversight prove it is “the world’s most moral army.” 

Each of those claims can be tested against the same body of reporting the film draws on (plus earlier investigations by the same journalists) and against publicly available data, the journalistic basis being: ‘NAZA’: Exposing Israel’s killing machine in Gaza https://t.co/2Ct5DJR3Fm

1. “Unverified anonymous sources manufactured the case.”

NAZA rests on 24 interviews with people the directors identify as current or former intelligence and targeting personnel, most from Unit 8200.  The same journalists previously published a detailed investigation in +972 Magazine and Local Call that first described the “Lavender” and “Gospel” systems.  Multiple officers independently described the same workflow: an AI model trained on known militants that generated tens of thousands of additional names, a 20-second human check that often consisted only of confirming the target was male, and pre-approved collateral thresholds of 15–20 civilians for junior operatives.  The IDF has not denied that these tools exist; it has only disputed the most extreme characterizations and the 500-civilian single-strike claim.  Patterned, consistent testimony from people who operated the systems is not the same as an unverified rumor.  (Report: Israel used AI tool called Lavender to choose targets in Gaza | The Verge https://t.co/CqXwnan41A)

2. “Historically lowest civilian casualty ratio.”

John Spencer’s 1:1 to 1:1.5 combatant-to-civilian figure is produced by taking the Gaza Health Ministry’s overall death total and subtracting the IDF’s own, unverified count of Hamas fighters killed.  Independent tallies (Airwars, UN agencies, alongside academic reconstructions) consistently show a higher civilian share, especially among women and children.  Even if one accepts the IDF numbers at face value, a 1.5:1 ratio in a densely packed, years-long urban campaign that also produced famine, the destruction of most housing stock, and the collapse of medical infrastructure is not automatically “the lowest ever.”  Mosul (roughly 2.5:1) and other battles occurred under different constraints and with different rules of engagement; they do not prove that every Israeli strike met the legal test of proportionality.  Ratios also ignore indirect deaths and the fact that many of those labeled “combatants” were low-level or loosely affiliated. (Gaza and the Conduct of Urban War: Civilian Harm, Risk, and Responsibility https://t.co/uhDFh3TjJ3)

3. “Always a human decision and sophisticated assessment.”

Officers who used Lavender described the human role as a rubber stamp.  After the system flagged 37,000 people, operators were expected to process targets at a rate that left roughly 20 seconds per name.  Gospel, the companion system for buildings, similarly accelerated target generation from dozens per year to dozens per day.  The film and earlier reporting document a policy of striking a target’s family home even when the individual was known to be elsewhere (“where’s daddy”).  That is not the same as a painstaking, case-by-case legal review.  The existence of some aborted strikes (the video shows one example involving children) does not cancel the scale of the approved list or the accepted collateral numbers. (The machine did it coldly https://t.co/SEWh6VLXJO)

4. “Unprecedented warnings and precautions.”

Leaflets, text messages, and phone calls occurred.  They frequently gave hours rather than days, directed people into areas that were later bombed, and offered no realistic safe destination once “humanitarian zones” themselves came under fire.  Repeated forced displacement, the destruction of hospitals and bakeries after they had been designated shelters, and the killing of aid-convoy personnel are documented by multiple NGOs and UN agencies.  Precautions that are systematically insufficient or followed by attacks on the places of refuge do not meet the IHL requirement of “feasible” precautions.  Hamas’s use of civilian areas and tunnels raises the risk; it does not erase the attacker’s independent duty.

5. “Hamas embedding explains everything; therefore the army remains the most moral.”

Hamas does embed among civilians and has built an extensive tunnel network.  That fact is relevant to assessing individual strikes and to understanding why civilian harm is high.  It does not convert a policy of high accepted collateral, AI-generated mass targeting, and statements by senior officials that “there are no uninvolved civilians” into evidence of exceptional morality.  “Most moral army” is a slogan that has been used for decades; it is not a measurable legal or empirical category.  International humanitarian law judges distinction, proportionality, and necessity in each attack, not comparative slogans.  Testimonies that the objective in some strikes was simply “to destroy” and that operators internalized “there are no innocents in Gaza” cut against the claim of unique restraint. (‘NAZA’: Exposing Israel’s killing machine in Gaza https://t.co/2Ct5DJR3Fm)

The video treats the existence of process (warnings, legal cells, some aborted missions) as proof of outcome.  The counter-evidence is the outcome itself - tens of thousands of civilian deaths, the systematic use of tools that industrialize targeting, and the consistent accounts of the people who ran those tools - plus the fact that independent investigators have been denied access.  That is the case NAZA actually puts forward, not a manufactured blood libel.  

APPENDIX: Video commentary: "Horrors on Israel’s Internet" https://t.co/l7Drn9K2Eq via @YouTube

text:
THE ANGELS UNDER THE EUPHRATES:

Revelation 9 is one of the strangest chapters in the Bible.

A lot of people skip it because they don’t know what to do with it. They’ll talk about the antichrist, the mark, Armageddon, all that. But when you get to these four angels chained under the Euphrates, most folks just move on.

Revelation 9:13-14 says:

“And the sixth angel sounded, and I heard a voice from the four horns of the golden altar which is before God,
Saying to the sixth angel which had the trumpet, Loose the four angels which are bound in the great river Euphrates.”

That’s a wild verse.

Four angels are bound in the great river Euphrates.

Bound means restrained. Held back. Locked down.

So right away, these are not holy angels. Holy angels don’t need chains. These are fallen angels. God has them confined until the exact moment He’s ready to use their release as judgment.

That alone tells you something about the unseen world.

There are beings we can’t see that are not free to do whatever they want. Satan doesn’t run loose like he owns the place. Fallen angels don’t move outside God’s permission. God can bind them. God can hold them. God can release them. God can use even their wickedness to bring judgment exactly when He says.

Revelation 9:15 says:

“And the four angels were loosed, which were prepared for an hour, and a day, and a month, and a year, for to slay the third part of men.”

An hour.

A day.

A month.

A year.

God has the time marked.

These four aren’t released because hell finally breaks free. They’re released because God gives the command.

And what are they prepared to do?

Slay the third part of men.

This is mass death on the earth during the trumpet judgments.

Now look where they’re bound.

The Euphrates.

That river carries a lot of weight in the Bible.

Genesis 2 mentions the Euphrates around the world connected to Eden. Later, that region becomes tied to Babel and Babylon. Man’s rebellion, false worship, empire-building, occult religion, and the world system that keeps lifting itself up against God all come out of that general area.

Then in Genesis 15:18, God promises Abraham’s seed the land from the river of Egypt to “the great river, the river Euphrates.”

So the Euphrates is tied to early creation history, ancient rebellion, Babylon, and the border of Israel’s promised land.

When Revelation points back to the Euphrates, God is dragging all that history back onto the table.

Eden.

Babel.

Babylon.

Israel.

Rebellion.

Promise.

Judgment.

That river has been sitting in the Bible from the beginning, and in Revelation 9 it becomes the place where four fallen angels are released.

Then John sees the army connected to this judgment.

Revelation 9:16 says:

“And the number of the army of the horsemen were two hundred thousand thousand: and I heard the number of them.”

Two hundred million.

Then the description gets even stranger.

Horses. Breastplates of fire, jacinth, and brimstone. Heads like lions. Fire, smoke, and brimstone coming out of their mouths. Tails like serpents.

Doesn’t sound like normal warfare.

Some people say it’s a future human army. Some say it’s demonic. I think the wording leans demonic, or at least supernatural and demonic in character. Either way, modern tanks and helicopters or not.. John describes what he sees, and what he sees is terrifying.

Revelation 9:18 says:

“By these three was the third part of men killed, by the fire, and by the smoke, and by the brimstone…”

A third of mankind dies from this judgment.

And the world still doesn’t repent.

That’s the part people don’t like to face.

Revelation 9:20-21 says the survivors still refuse to repent of their idols, murders, sorceries, fornication, and thefts.

So don’t buy the idea that if God just made Himself more obvious, everybody would turn to Him.

Revelation says men will watch judgment fall from heaven and still cling to their sin.

The word translated “sorceries” is:

φαρμακεία - pharmakeia

It points to sorcery, occult practice, enchantment, and drug-connected spiritual deception. It’s talking about the dark spiritual system that has always followed rebellion against God.

That fits the whole passage.

The Euphrates is connected to ancient rebellion.

Babylon is connected to false worship.

The world in Revelation is full of idolatry, violence, sexual corruption, theft, and sorcery.

Then God releases four bound angels from that same prophetic region, and judgment tears through the earth.

This is not a fairy-tale.

This is future history written before it happens.

The world laughs at the Bible now. It treats Revelation like symbolism, madness, or religious scare language.

But God has appointments already set.

The four angels are bound.

The hour is chosen.

The command will come.

And when the sixth trumpet sounds, the world won’t be debating whether Revelation should be taken seriously.

They’ll be living inside it.

That’s why this chapter should sober people up.

Jesus is not just meek and mild for paintings.

He is the Lamb who was slain and the Lion who takes the earth back.

He saves now.

He judges later.

And the only safe place before judgment falls is in Him.

Christ died for our sins. He was buried. He rose again the third day. Right now, the door is open. Grace is still being offered.

But Revelation 9 reminds us God’s patience has an end.

The angels under the Euphrates are not a myth.

They are bound until the appointed time.

And when God says, “Loose them,” the whole earth will learn that His Word was never playing.

text:
Based on available information, EnerVenue no longer holds any active U.S. federal or state tax incentives. It did secure a significant state/local package in 2023, but it voluntarily abandoned those incentives when it pivoted manufacturing to China in 2024.

📜 The Abandoned Kentucky Incentives (2023)

In March 2023, EnerVenue announced a planned $264 million factory in Shelby County, Kentucky, which was tied to a substantial incentive package:

· State Incentives: The Kentucky Economic Development Finance Authority approved up to $10.3 million in performance-based tax incentives under the Kentucky Business Investment program .
· Local Incentives: Shelby County offered an additional package worth $20 million over 25 years, comprising property and wage tax rebates .

📉 Current Status: Abandoned in 2024

The company pulled out of the Kentucky deal in 2024, choosing instead to build its high-volume manufacturing line in Changzhou, China . As a result, it gave up those tax incentives . Its current $300 million funding round is specifically earmarked for the China facility .

🇺🇸 The Federal Tax Credit Question (Unresolved)

EnerVenue's technology has historically been promoted as qualifying for U.S. federal incentives like the Investment Tax Credit (ITC) domestic content bonus . However, manufacturing in China creates a major obstacle for those credits, especially under stricter "foreign entities of concern" rules designed to limit supply chain exposure to China .

As of April 2026, CEO Henning Rath stated the company had not yet reached a clear conclusion on whether its China-built batteries can still allow U.S. customers to claim those tax credits, but expected clarity within a couple of months .

text:
A man walked up to a Miami Gardens food truck, flashed a badge and told the owner he was “the most important ICE agent in Miami.”

Jonathan Gonzalez Reyes is now in jail on charges including impersonating an officer and aggravated assault.

Surveillance video appears to show him arriving in a vehicle with blue flashing lights, wearing a badge and carrying what appears to be a holstered gun. Owner Luis Rodriguez says Reyes offered to fix immigration problems for money and deliberately talked about Nicaraguans and Haitians where his employees could hear him.

Rodriguez told him to leave.

About a month later, Rodriguez says Reyes returned, threatened an employee with a gun, threatened to pistol-whip him and claimed he would plant drugs inside the business to get it shut down.

His bond was set at $11,000. ICE told NBC6 this was the first it had heard about the case.

See the link to the article in the comments.
